# Amulet Essentials — every record, flattened

## โบมินกอง · Bo Min Gaung · Bo Min Gaung image (weikza saint)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/bo-min-gaung/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/bo-min-gaung.json
id: bo-min-gaung · level: kind
native: ဘိုးမင်းခေါင် (my)
aliases: โบมินกอง · อองมินกอง · รูปวิชชาพม่า · Bo Min Gaung · Bo Min Kaung · Aung Min Gaung · Bodaw Aung Min Gaung · Bo Min Gaung statue · weizza saint image
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall) · region: mm
origin:  ·  · Bo Min Gaung: born 2 May 1880 near Mount Popa, Kyaukpadaung Township; died 5 September 1952 at Mount Popa. Images are twentieth century onward. · Mount Popa, and altars across Myanmar
what (th): รูปของโบมินกอง วิชชาผู้เป็นที่นับถือที่สุดของพม่ายุคใหม่ เกิดใกล้ภูเขาโปปา มรณภาพที่นั่นเมื่อ พ.ศ. ๒๔๙๕ ศิษย์เชื่อว่าท่านยังอยู่ ให้ความฝัน โชคลาภ และความคุ้มครอง จึงตั้งรูปไว้บนหิ้งและพกติดตัว
what (en): Images of Bo Min Gaung, the most venerated weikza of modern Burmese Buddhism: born near Mount Popa in 1880, died there in 1952. Devotees hold that he did not die as others do, that he bestows dreams, wealth and protection, and his image sits on household altars and travels as a locket. A named being venerated through the object, which is what places it with the devas rather than with Buddha amulets.
story: Born in Kyaukpadaung Township in 1880, he spent his last years at Mount Popa, oversaw the Pyi Lone Chan Thar Kat Kyaw pagoda there in 1952, and died that September. His statue is enshrined at Shwedagon and his photograph on altars across the country. The tradition tells that he appeared only in photographs taken by certain devotees, and that he could send dreams, wealth and protection. Thai has no name for him beyond the transliteration.
keeping: Veneration: flowers, water, respect, a place on the altar. Worship, not parenting — nothing is fed and nothing is closed.
- look at: Lay dress: taikpon jacket, singlet, checked paso. A robed figure is a monk image, not Bo Min Gaung [cited]
- look at: Statues of Bo Bo Aung stand beside his on Burmese altars; two lay figures together is the weikza pair [cited]
- look at: Photographs are a primary medium: the tradition holds he appeared only in photographs taken by certain devotees, so framed prints and photo-lockets are as common as cast figures [cited]
- look at: His statue is enshrined at Shwedagon; commercial pieces copy the enshrined type [cited]
- look at: A cheroot in the hand is usual in the trade's images; treat it as a habit of the type, not a rule [tradition]
- vs rup-lersi: A Thai lersi wears a tiger skin and a topknot or antlered cap; Bo Min Gaung wears a Burmese jacket and paso. Both are non-monk sages kept for protection; Thai class leaves the lersi unplaced, this record venerates a named being.
- vs luang-pu-thuat: Luang Pu Thuat is a robed monk on a tablet or medallion; Bo Min Gaung is a layman. The robe decides it.
- vs rian-kechi: A Thai monk medallion shows a robed monk with Thai text; a Bo Min Gaung medallion shows a layman with Burmese text.
- vs rup-lo: Thai cast figures are of monks; a cast Bo Min Gaung is a seated layman, often with Bo Bo Aung beside.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/67081ea16d6cd0c438591548e5bf215f35c86ae19e6229ad071dbdf32c04bb5b.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Ladybesttruthful at Burmese Wikipedia · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=73561897
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/fa0aab5655fcba6d08a33427ae5d636c782e3f6d9338679393b9cdc87cf2a398.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · YashiWong · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=4739848
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/c672d047c02b490acb399b35ad9918f110776c6a587e13ca56ffc85696280388.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · YashiWong · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=4740037
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/f352dd88d6956cc32d42091e32ac22cbaf9e78b2f84cfb02ccf17c425609e439.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Emily Khine · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=72214358
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/b088990d90171583774a93b21080849311103ccb44a96b3950a8bb76a4d8b95b.jpg · CC BY 4.0 · Ladybesttruthful · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=143216569
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/c36f4b2d2c807a3bacd4814a3f64035d077e02a9220d1624008e5b784bbf2f70.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 ·  · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=157549862

## พระพุทธเจ้าประจำปีนักษัตรจีน · Phật bản mệnh · Birth-year guardian Buddha pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phat-ban-menh/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phat-ban-menh.json
id: phat-ban-menh · level: kind
native: Phật bản mệnh (vi) · 本命佛 · 八大守護神 (zh) · 十二支守護本尊 (ja)
aliases: พระประจำปีเกิด ๘ พระโพธิสัตว์ · พระ ๑๒ นักษัตรจีน · phat ban menh · ben ming fo · ba da shou hu shen · life-Buddha pendant · eight zodiac guardians · natal Buddha
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: medallion · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: vn, diaspora
origin:  · โรงงานเครื่องประดับและร้านค้าออนไลน์ ไม่ผูกกับวัดใด Jewellery workshops and online sellers; not tied to a temple or a named maker · The twelve-branch guardian set is Japanese Shingon practice; Chinese Wikipedia notes it appears in no sutra. Its spread as a Chinese and Vietnamese retail pendant is recent and undated in the sources · Japan, then China and Vietnam
what (th): จี้พระพุทธเจ้าหรือพระโพธิสัตว์ ๑ ใน ๘ องค์ เลือกตามปีนักษัตรจีนของผู้ใส่ ชุดนี้มาจากนิกายชินงอนญี่ปุ่น ขายเป็นเครื่องประดับในจีนและเวียดนาม ไทยมีขายบ้างในชื่อ 'พระประจำปีเกิด นักษัตรจีน' ไม่ใช่พระประจำวันเกิดแบบไทย
what (en): A pendant of one of eight Buddhas and bodhisattvas, chosen by the wearer's Chinese zodiac year. The eight-figure set is Japanese Shingon practice, sold today as jewellery across China and Vietnam and, thinly, in Thailand under 'Chinese zodiac birth-year Buddha'. It is not the Thai weekday birthday Buddha.
story: Japanese esoteric Buddhism assigns eight guardian figures to the twelve branches. China took the set over as the 本命佛 'natal Buddha' and Vietnam as Phật bản mệnh; Chinese Wikipedia records that the pairing appears in no scripture, and that Tibetan-style sellers swap four of the figures. Today it is a retail pendant in jade, obsidian or silver, sold with a card giving the zodiac table. On Lazada Thailand one listing offers the set as 'Buddha of the 12 signs, Chinese zodiac, 8 bodhisattvas'.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed: a Buddha-image pendant in the vault's phra_khrueang sense, adoptable with no history. Whether it was ever consecrated is a question about the seller, not the class.
- look at: Eight figures share twelve animals (rat / ox-tiger / rabbit / dragon-snake / horse / goat-monkey / rooster / dog-pig); the figure must match the wearer's birth year, which is the first thing a reader checks [cited]
- look at: The set is Japanese Shingon in origin and absent from the canonical texts; a seller's claim of antiquity has no support in the tradition's own literature [cited]
- look at: Chinese lists differ from the Japanese table on two animals (monkey given to Acala, rooster to Amitābha in the zh table); check which table the seller follows [cited]
- look at: Not the Thai พระประจำวันเกิด: that system is by weekday (Sunday ปางถวายเนตร … Saturday ปางนาคปรก) and uses Buddha postures, not bodhisattvas [cited]
- look at: Sold as jewellery (jade, obsidian, silver, plated alloy) with no standing consecration rite; Chinese Wikipedia lists cards, jewellery, thangka and amulets among the commercial forms [cited]
- vs kuan-im: A Guanyin pendant is for anyone; the natal-Buddha pendant is keyed to the birth year, and its Rat figure happens to be the thousand-armed Guanyin, so count the arms.
- vs jade-buddha-burmese: A Burmese jade Buddha is a seated Buddha in meditation or earth-touching posture with no zodiac key; the same jade carries a bodhisattva here.
- vs locket: A Thai locket is a photograph of a monk under resin; this is a carved or cast bodhisattva.
sources: s:ja-wiki-shugo-honzon — 守護本尊 — ウィキペディア; s:zh-wiki-ba-da-shou-hu-shen — 八大守護神 — 維基百科; s:th-wiki-pang-phra-phuttharup — ปางพระพุทธรูป — วิกิพีเดีย; s:catalog-db — manuscript-crawler catalog.db — items table, 13,020 Lazada TH listings (method=commerce) + 6,990 manuscripts; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ตั่วแปะกง · Tua Pek Kong · Tua Pek Kong medallion
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/tua-pek-kong/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/tua-pek-kong.json
id: tua-pek-kong · level: kind
native: 大伯公 · 福德正神 (zh) · Ông Bổn · Bổn Đầu Công (vi) · Tokong Tua Pek Kong (ms)
aliases: ต่าวเป๊กกง · ต้าป๋อกง · ฮกเต็กเจี่ยสิ้ง · ปึงเถ่ากง (ญาติใกล้) · Dabogong · Toa Pek Kong · Topekong · Tepekong · Fude Zhengshen · Ông Bổn · Grand Uncle · God of Prosperity · Southeast Asian earth god
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: medallion · materials: — · functions: ค้าขาย (trade, selling), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: my, sg, th, id, vn, diaspora
origin:  · ศาลเจ้าตั่วแปะกงในปีนัง สิงคโปร์ มาเลเซีย อินโดนีเซีย และศาลเจ้าปึงเถ่ากงในไทย Tua Pek Kong temples in Penang, Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia; in Thailand the related Pun Thao Kong shrines · The Tanjung Tokong temple in Penang was established by 1792, the oldest site · Penang, then West and East Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and parts of Thailand
what (th): เทพผู้คุ้มครองของชาวจีนโพ้นทะเลในปีนัง สิงคโปร์ มาเลเซีย อินโดนีเซีย และบางส่วนของไทย รูปชายชราเครายาวถือไม้เท้าและก้อนทอง ทำเป็นเหรียญห้อยคอและรูปตั้งบูชา ให้ค้าขายรุ่งเรืองและปลอดภัย เป็นเทพที่บูชาผ่านวัตถุ ไม่ใช่ผี ในไทยญาติใกล้คือปึงเถ่ากง
what (en): The tutelary god of Southeast Asian Chinese communities, 'Grand Uncle': an old bearded man with staff and ingot, worn as a temple medallion or kept as an altar figure for trade and safety. A deva-tier resident venerated through the object, in the vault's sense, not a raised spirit. Thailand's Pun Thao Kong (本頭公) is the near relative.
story: The oldest temple, at Tanjung Tokong in Penang, was there by 1792. Who he was is argued: Zhang Li, a Hakka who reached Penang before Francis Light; Fu of the Fu Lu Shou triad; a Fujian sailor who gave his life for a companion. The cult grew with sworn-brotherhood societies and followed the diaspora to Sarawak, where Kuching and Sibu have landmark temples, to Singapore's Kusu Island and Pulau Ubin, to Batam, and to Chợ Lớn as Ông Bổn. Because his image is Tudigong's, the two are routinely merged, and in Penang the Nine Emperor rites include him.
keeping: Veneration, not feeding: incense, fruit and tea on the altar at the festivals and when asking, as for any deva-tier object in the vault. A worn medallion needs nothing beyond respect. Provenance sensitivity is medium, the class's own figure, and mostly a question of which temple issued it.
- look at: Seated old man with a long white beard, staff and ingot; the iconography is the earth god Tudigong's, which is why the two are conflated [cited]
- look at: Read the characters: 大伯公 or 福德正神 marks Tua Pek Kong; Thai shrines mostly carry 本頭公 (ปึงเถ่ากง), a related but distinct name Thai Wikipedia treats separately [cited]
- look at: Identity is contested: a Hakka settler Zhang Li who reached Penang before Francis Light, or Fu of the Fu Lu Shou triad, or a Fujian sailor; a medallion's inscription may pick one [cited]
- look at: In Vietnam the same figure is Ông Bổn / Bổn Đầu Công at Miếu Nhị Phủ in Chợ Lớn: a 1.5 m wooden statue, festival on the 15th of the 8th lunar month [cited]
- look at: Tudigong's birthday is the 2nd day of the 2nd lunar month; temple issues cluster on the festival, which the trade holds [cited]
- look at: No Lazada Thailand title carries the name in any spelling as of 2026-09-02; the medallions move through temples and Penang and Singapore shops, not Thai online retail [catalogue]
- vs rup-lersi: Both are bearded old men. The lersi wears a tiger skin and a hair knot and is a hermit; Tua Pek Kong wears a Chinese official's hat and robe and holds an ingot.
- vs chuchok: Chuchok is a gaunt beggar-brahmin with a staff and a begging bag; Tua Pek Kong is plump, smiling and holding gold. Same staff, opposite man.
- vs phra-siwali: Phra Siwali is a monk with an umbrella and bowl, no beard; Tua Pek Kong is a layman with a beard and a hat.
- vs rian-kechi: A Thai monk medallion shows a shaven-headed bhikkhu; here the head has hair and a hat and the face a beard.

## ไอ้ไข่ · ai khai · Ai Khai (the temple boy of Wat Chedi)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/ai-khai/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/ai-khai.json
id: ai-khai · level: kind
aliases: ไอ้ไข่ เด็กวัดเจดีย์ · ไอ้ไข่วัดเจดีย์ · ตาไข่ · ai kai · i khai · ta khai · ai khai wat chedi · Ai Khai of Wat Chedi · the Wat Chedi boy
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-south, th
origin: วัดเจดีย์ (ไอ้ไข่) ตำบลฉลอง อำเภอสิชล จังหวัดนครศรีธรรมราช Wat Chedi (Ai Khai), Tambon Chalong, Amphoe Sichon, Nakhon Si Thammarat · รูปไม้ทองหลางแกะโดยผู้ใหญ่เที่ยงก่อน พ.ศ. ๒๕๒๕ · รูปไม้ตะเคียนแกะ พ.ศ. ๒๕๒๔–๒๕๒๕ · วัตถุมงคลรุ่นแรกออกโดยเจ้าอาวาส พ.ศ. ๒๕๒๖ First figure carved from soft thonglang wood by a village headman named Thiang before B.E. 2525; a second in takhian wood in 2524–2525; the abbot issued the first amulet run in B.E. 2526 (1983), per Thai Wikipedia · Carvings before 1982, first run 1983; the national wave is the 2020s and the trade counts it the biggest since Jatukham · Sichon, Nakhon Si Thammarat, then nationwide; Thai Wikipedia's temple articles show copies housed at temples in Pathum Thani, Chachoengsao and elsewhere
what (th): วิญญาณเด็กวัดเจดีย์ อำเภอสิชล กระแสศรัทธาใหญ่ที่สุดนับแต่จตุคาม ขอเรื่องหวยแล้วแก้บนด้วยประทัดและของเล่นทหาร วัตถุมงคลเป็นพาหะของศรัทธา การรักษาคำบนคือการเลี้ยง
what (en): The boy-spirit of Wat Chedi in Sichon, the biggest devotional wave since Jatukham — asked for lottery luck and repaid in firecrackers and toy soldiers. The amulet carries the devotion; the vow-keeping is the keeping.
story: The temple's story makes Ai Khai a boy of nine or ten who followed Luang Pu Thuat from Songkhla toward Ayutthaya, was left to guard Wat Chedi, vowed to stay, and went into the temple pond to remain as its guardian; villagers asked him to find lost cattle. A soft thonglang-wood carving by a headman named Thiang, made before 1982, rotted; a takhian-wood figure carved in 1981–82 fixed the pose, right fist to the chest. The abbot issued the first amulet run in 1983. Firecrackers by the truckload and moulded cocks filling the grounds are the vows being paid; the 2020s wave carried copies to temples across the country.
keeping: Class unassigned: the largest new devotion of the era is not yet in the vault's class vocabulary. Kept mostly as a votive relationship — ask, promise, and deliver what you promised — rather than as a fed dependent; a knower may file it more precisely. A piece with unknown history carries an unpaid vow only if its keeper made one.
- look at: A boy figure, never a Buddha or a monk portrait [catalogue]
- look at: Right fist to chest, left arm down: the reference pose from the 1982 takhian carving [cited]
- look at: Sold with its own yantra cloth and incense; fighting cocks and firecrackers are the vow's signature. A listing bundling them is selling the devotion, not the object [catalogue]
- look at: Everything hangs on the name Wat Chedi, Sichon; a piece that names no issuing temple is a generic boy figure [inference]
- look at: Bodies run cast metal, fired earth and powder; the material fixes nothing here, the temple and run do [tradition]
- vs kuman-thong: Both are child figures. A kuman thong houses a raised child-spirit fed as family (class kuman); Ai Khai is kept as a vow — ask, promise, pay with firecrackers — and the vault has not placed him. The keeping is the tell, not the shape
- vs jatukham: The previous Nakhon Si Thammarat wave: a large disc medallion of a deva-king (class thep_thewada). Ai Khai is a boy, cast or pressed, from Sichon
- vs luang-pu-thuat: The legend makes Ai Khai the boy who followed Luang Pu Thuat; a Luang Pu Thuat piece shows a robed monk (class phra_khrueang), Ai Khai a shirtless boy

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/6af9c6ce3ca63a56e3225be84d7c0c182f278d101b8246e8d2fe0472c7c5b9f3.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Eqqpwppr · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=92121218

## เบี้ยแก้ · bia kae · Bia kae (warding cowrie)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/bia-kae/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/bia-kae.json
id: bia-kae · level: kind
aliases: เบี้ยจั่น · เบี้ยแก้หลวงปู่บุญ · bia gae · bia kae · mercury cowrie · counter-charm cowrie
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: shell · materials: ตะกั่ว (lead) · functions: มหาอุด (stopping projectiles / misfire), กันผี (warding spirits), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-central
origin: วัดกลางบางแก้ว Wat Klang Bang Kaeo · ท่านเจ้าคุณพุทธวิถีนายก (หลวงปู่บุญ) ตามที่ตำราระบุ Chao Khun Phutthawithinayok, Luang Pu Bun, per the treatise's own ascription · Undated treatise; the ascription is the treatise's, not verified here · Central Thailand
what (th): หอยเบี้ยบรรจุปรอทผนึกไว้ ถักเชือกหรือหุ้มโลหะ เครื่องราง แก้ คลาสสิกที่หันภัยและคุณไสยออกไป ตำราในคลังนี้มีวิธีสร้างที่ระบุว่าเป็นของหลวงปู่บุญ วัดกลางบางแก้ว
what (en): A cowrie shell loaded with sealed mercury and bound in cord or foil — the classic 'undoer' that turns aside harm and bad medicine. The formulary in this corpus carries a making ascribed to Luang Pu Bun of Wat Klang Bang Kaew.
story: The treatise consecrates one baht-weight of mercury with the asisati-thanu formula 108 times, pours it into the cowrie, seals it with a closing katha 108 times, stops the mouth with underground stingless-bee resin while reciting tho-utthang 108 times, sheets it in beaten lead inscribed with the na maha-ut glyph, plaits, lacquers and gilds it, and wakes it with the eight-direction Itipiso 108 times. It is for maha-ut, against sorcery-workings, and against pob and forest ghosts. Thai Wikipedia adds the trade's condition: the keeper must think and act well or it may not hold.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; mercury inside, so do not open it.
- look at: A real cowrie, not a casting: the shell's toothed lip may show at the edge of the lead [cited]
- look at: Mouth stopped with underground stingless-bee resin, then sheeted over with beaten lead [catalogue]
- look at: Finished by cord plaiting, lacquer and gilding; the outer skin reads as dark lacquered cord with worn gold [catalogue]
- look at: The recipe loads one baht-weight of mercury; a bia kae is heavy for its size next to an empty shell [catalogue]
- vs takrut: Both get the plaited-cord finish; a takrut is a rolled sheet with a cord channel, a bia kae a shell with no channel and a domed back.
- vs khot-kala: A khot kala is a natural concretion kept as found, its class natural talisman; a bia kae is manufactured and consecrated, its class inscribed object.
- vs lek-lai: Lek lai is a dark lustrous metal held to be alive; a bia kae is a shell whose weight is mercury. Different class, different story.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:th-wiki-bia-kae — เบี้ยแก้ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## กระจกยันต์แปดทิศ · bát quái · Bagua mirror
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/bat-quai/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/bat-quai.json
id: bat-quai · level: kind
native: gương bát quái (vi) · 八卦鏡 (zh)
aliases: ยันต์แปดทิศ · กระจกแปดเหลี่ยม · โป๊ยข่วย · ปากว้า · gương bát quái · bagua jing · pat kwa · poi kwai · eight-trigram mirror · feng shui mirror · pa kua mirror
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: vn, diaspora
origin:  · ร้านฮวงจุ้ยและโรงงาน ไม่ผูกวัด Feng shui shops and factories; no temple or maker attached · The trigrams are attributed in legend to Fuxi; the door mirror as an inexpensive self-administered remedy is modern and undated in the sources · China, spread wherever Chinese houses are
what (th): กระจกในกรอบแปดเหลี่ยมมีตรีลักษณ์ ๘ ล้อม แขวนเหนือประตูด้านนอกหันออกเพื่อสะท้อนสิ่งไม่ดี ไม่ใช่ของใส่ตัว เวียดนามเรียก gương bát quái ไทยเรียกกระจกยันต์แปดทิศหรือโป๊ยข่วย พลังอยู่ที่แผนภาพ ไม่มีผู้สถิต
what (en): A mirror in an octagonal frame of the eight trigrams, hung outside above the door and facing away, to turn back harmful qi from a road or a building edge. Not worn, not venerated: an impersonal diagram doing a job at the threshold. Vietnamese gương bát quái, Thai กระจกยันต์แปดทิศ.
story: The trigrams come from the Yijing and are credited in legend to Fuxi. The door mirror is the cheapest feng shui remedy there is, chosen and hung by the householder without a master: flat to reflect, convex to scatter, concave to absorb. It goes outside and only outside. Because it works by sending harm back where it came from, angling one at a neighbour is a provocation, and Hong Kong has recorded mirror feuds fought house against house. On Lazada Thailand it sells beside pendant versions of the same diagram, which are worn and are a different object.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. It hangs and is left alone; a cracked one is replaced. The only care the trade names is not to bring it indoors and not to aim it at people.
- look at: Three mirror types with three stated jobs: flat reflects, convex disperses, concave absorbs or converges [cited]
- look at: Hung above the front door or window, facing out; never installed indoors. It is a feng shui remedy against sha qi from a road or a building corner, not an instrument [cited]
- look at: Octagonal for the eight directions; round examples exist [cited]
- look at: A newer variant is a square mirror printed with the trigrams and Daoist charm-script, cheaper to make than the true octagon; seen in a Commons photograph from Taipei [inference]
- look at: Pointing one at a neighbour's house reads as hostile; Hong Kong has documented mirror feuds. Useful for reading why one is angled the way it is [cited]
- vs pha-yan: Both are impersonal inscribed objects, but a yantra cloth is worn or hung inside; the bagua mirror is architectural, outside, facing away from the house.
- vs fu-talisman: A paper fu is pasted above the same door, but it is written paper, burnable and replaceable; the mirror is a permanent fixture.
- vs pixiu: A pixiu is a beast figure at the shop door or on the wrist and receives offerings; nobody makes offerings to a mirror.

## ยันต์กระดาษเวียดนาม · bùa · Vietnamese talisman (bùa)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/bua/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/bua.json
id: bua · level: kind
native: bùa · bùa hộ mệnh (vi) · 符 (zh)
aliases: บั่ว · บั่วโห่เหม่ง · เครื่องรางเวียดนาม · bua · bùa hộ mệnh · bùa bình an · phù · Vietnamese amulet · protective charm (bùa hộ mệnh) · peace charm (bùa bình an)
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: vn
origin:  · วัด (chùa) ศาลเจ้า (đền) พระสงฆ์ หรือหมอผี (thầy) Buddhist temples (chùa), shrines (đền), monks and ritual specialists (thầy pháp, thầy cúng); parents bought them for children · Continuing practice; early-twentieth-century accounts describe them commonly given to children for health · Vietnam
what (th): เครื่องรางเวียดนาม คำว่า bùa ครอบคลุมยันต์กระดาษแบบจีน เหรียญยันต์ และ bùa hộ mệnh ที่พกติดตัว ส่วนใหญ่เป็นกระดาษเขียนอักษรจีนหรือโนม พับใส่ถุงผ้าห้อยคอ พลังอยู่ที่อักษรและพิธี ไม่มีผู้สถิต
what (en): The Vietnamese talisman: a paper written with Chinese or Nôm characters and talismanic strokes, folded into a cloth pouch and worn, or pasted in the house. The word bùa also covers coin charms, jade and metal pieces, and spoken spells; power sits in the writing and the rite, nobody is home.
story: Early-twentieth-century accounts have parents buying a bùa hộ mệnh at a temple or from a thầy for a sick or vulnerable child. The writers are Taoist priests (đạo sĩ), exorcists and monks; the stated purposes are warding a place (trấn yểm) and driving off harm (trừ tà). Older Vietnamese protective practice, tattooing water-spirit designs, sits behind the paper form. Vietnamese speakers often call every Chinese-model paper talisman a bùa Lỗ Ban.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed: an inscribed object in the vault's yantra_wattu sense. When worn out it is burned or returned to the temple rather than thrown away, which the trade holds and the record does not verify. Bùa ngải and bùa yêu, made with herbs and directed at a person, are a different matter that shares the word.
- look at: A small paper written with incantations or Classical-Chinese characters, folded and wrapped in a coloured cloth pouch at the neck: the standard bùa hộ mệnh form [cited]
- look at: Where the paper follows the Chinese fu model it reads in three parts, header, body and foot, with a seal; the Vietnamese name for that model is phù lục [cited]
- look at: Metal (coins, rings), jade, stone and small figures are also called bùa hộ mệnh; the form does not settle what the object is [cited]
- look at: Temple-issued bình an charms handed out around Tết are usually printed; a hand-brushed sheet usually points to an individual master. The trade holds this; not verified against a source [tradition]
- look at: Vietnamese speakers commonly lump all fu-type talismans under the name bùa Lỗ Ban (Lu Ban charms), so a seller's label may be broader than the object [cited]
- vs fu-talisman: Same class, same paper model. The fu is the Taoist sheet itself, yellow paper and red ink; bùa is the Vietnamese frame around it, which also takes Nôm script, the sewn cloth pouch, and metal or jade objects under one word.
- vs pha-yan: Thai yantra cloth is a printed cloth sheet in Khom script, hung or folded in a wallet; a bùa is paper sewn into a small cloth pouch.
- vs takrut: A takrut is rolled metal foil in a tube; a bùa is folded paper in cloth. Both impersonal, both worn.
- vs jimat: A Malay jimat carries Arabic or Jawi writing; a bùa carries Chinese or Nôm.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/1f0a327725bff846413d292e9dea72460c485e922d3124ce16b372829124d8b9.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Phương Huy · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=103384983
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/699695d7aba91c8366a7dbb184a8f4182f35ecc7426717f3ca7355f6cd61eab3.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Vietnamese Women's Museum · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=32119047
sources: s:vi-wiki-bua-ho-menh — Bùa hộ mệnh — Wikipedia tiếng Việt; s:vi-wiki-phu-luc — Phù lục — Wikipedia tiếng Việt; s:zh-wiki-fulu — 符籙 — 維基百科; s:en-wiki-vietnamese-folk-religion — Vietnamese folk religion — Wikipedia; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## จะปิ้ง · cha ping · Cha ping (child's modesty plate)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/cha-ping/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/cha-ping.json
id: cha-ping · level: kind
aliases: จับปิ้ง · ตะปิ้ง · กระจับปิ้ง · chaping · jabping · tapping · modesty shield · child's genital cover · araimudi (Tamil cognate)
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: other · materials: กะลา (coconut shell), เนื้อเงิน (silver), เนื้อนาค (copper-gold alloy (rose gold)), เนื้อทองคำ (gold) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th, my, id
origin:  · ช่างทอง ช่างเงินตามฐานะครอบครัว Household jewellers; the metal follows the family's standing · Attested from the Srivijaya centuries through early Bangkok; museum examples bought in Bangkok in 1887; rare on children today · Siam, the Malay world, Java, and Tamil south India (araimudi)
what (th): แผ่นปิดของลับสำหรับเด็กเล็ก ผูกเชือกคาดเอว ทำจากทองเหลือง เงิน นาก ทอง หรือกะลา รูปหัวใจหรือใบไม้สำหรับเด็กหญิง โล่สำหรับเด็กชาย พิพิธภัณฑ์สตอกโฮล์มที่ซื้อจากบางกอกใน พ.ศ. ๒๔๓๐ จดว่าเป็น “เครื่องราง”
what (en): A child's modesty plate worn on a waist cord — brass, silver, nak, gold or coconut shell; heart or leaf for girls, shield for boys. The Stockholm museum that bought a set in Bangkok in 1887 catalogued them as amulets, and the Thai article notes the Tamil cousin is a talisman against spirits.
story: The Swedish frigate Vanadis called at Bangkok in 1885 and the Museum of Ethnography catalogued the purchases in 1887: among them a run of brass cha ping, larger and smaller, hearts for girls and shields for boys, each labelled 'ornament (amulet)'. They are the only museum-quality free photographs of a Thai child's protection we have found.
keeping: Nobody home and no rite: a worn protection, not a consecrated one. The vault vocabulary has no class for it and that refusal is recorded.
- look at: A thin plate with a loop or holes at the top edge for the waist cord — never a bail for a neck chain [catalogue]
- look at: Heart or leaf outline for girls, shield outline for boys — the museum's own 1887 labels make the split [cited]
- look at: Brass is the common body; silver, nak and gold mark wealth; coconut shell the poorest [cited]
- look at: No Buddha, no yantra, no temple: it is a worn protection, not a consecrated one, which is why the vault vocabulary has no class for it [inference]
- vs palad-khik: Both hang at a child's waist for protection, but a palad khik is a consecrated phallus and a cha ping is an unconsecrated plate that covers
- vs kala-ta-diao: A one-eyed coconut is found and kept whole; a coconut-shell cha ping is cut and shaped
- vs locket: A locket hangs at the neck and carries a monk's picture; a cha ping hangs at the waist and carries a pattern

## ฉันหมาก · chan mak · Chan mak (a monk's chewed betel quid)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/chan-mak/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/chan-mak.json
id: chan-mak · level: kind
aliases: ชานหมาก · ชานหมากหลวงปู่ · ลูกอมชานหมาก · สมเด็จชานหมาก · chan maak · charn mark · chaan mak · betel-quid relic · chewed betel amulet · the master's chewed betel
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: natural · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th
origin: ไม่มีวัดเดียว · วิกิพีเดียไทย: วัดจันทาวาส ตำบลท่าทอง อำเภอกาญจนดิษฐ์ สุราษฎร์ธานี (พระครูคลาย คนฺธสุธมฺโม) · วัดราชโยธา กรุงเทพฯ (หลวงปู่ทอง อายะนะ) · วัดชำปะง่าม (สมเด็จชานหมาก) No single temple. Thai Wikipedia names Wat Chanthawat, Kanchanadit, Surat Thani (Phra Khru Khlai, abbot from 1972, whose famous item it is); Wat Ratchayotha, Bangkok (Luang Pu Thong Ayana, 1820–1937); and Wat Champa-ngam (สมเด็จชานหมาก tablets) · พระเกจิที่ฉันหมาก ผู้ใดก็ได้ที่ศิษย์เก็บชานหมากของท่านไว้ การ์ดอ้างอิงเอ่ยหลวงปู่สี และหลวงพ่อทบ ว่าราคาสูงสุด Any revered betel-chewing monk whose disciples kept the quid; the reference card names Luang Pu See and Luang Pho Thob as the top of the price range · Betel chewing was campaigned against from 1940 and faded from the cities, so the supply is mostly monks of that generation and rural elders since — an inference from the betel article, not a dated claim · Nationwide
what (th): ชานหมากที่พระเกจิผู้เป็นที่เคารพเคี้ยวเอง ตากแห้งเก็บไว้ — พระธาตุจากร่างกายในความหมายตรงที่สุด ราคาในตลาดเป็นไปตามนั้น พลังคือบารมีของท่าน การเลี้ยงคือความเคารพธรรมดา
what (en): A quid of betel a revered monk himself chewed, dried and kept — a bodily relic in the most literal sense, priced accordingly in the living market. Power is the master's barami; keeping is plain respect.
story: A Thai quid is betel leaf, areca nut and red lime, sometimes tobacco; chewed, it leaves a red-brown residue. Disciples kept what a master spat out, dried it, lacquered or wrapped it, and cased it. Thai Wikipedia records the quid as the famous item of Phra Khru Khlai of Wat Chanthawat in Surat Thani, and among the objects of Luang Pu Thong Ayana of Wat Ratchayotha, beside ลูกอม balls and somdet-form powder tablets. The state's 1940 campaign against betel made the habit, and so the supply, rarer. Nothing is inscribed and nothing is consecrated in the usual sense: the object is the monk's own body's trace, which is why the trade prices it above every manufactured category.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; class phra_khrueang per the holding key. Handled with the respect due a master's bodily trace. Its provenance question is attribution and price, never spiritual safety — and attribution is the whole object, so the record that says whose it was is worth more than the lump.
- look at: Not made for the wearer: a residue, not a mould product. No press marks, no seams [catalogue]
- look at: Areca fibre and lime, red-brown from the reaction of nut, leaf and red lime — the same stain that reddened chewers' teeth [cited]
- look at: Usually lacquered, gilded, foil-wrapped or thread-bound and cased. The attribution cannot be read off the object; only the temple's own record supports it — the same logic the materials axis applies to hair and robe relics [catalogue]
- look at: ลูกอมชานหมาก balls and สมเด็จชานหมาก tablets are derivatives: a pressed tablet with the word in its name is a powder amulet with quid as an ingredient, not the relic itself [cited]
- look at: Highest average listing price of any category surveyed (฿30–15,500, average ฿785), so the pressure to fabricate is high — a statement about the category, never about an object [catalogue]
- vs phra-somdet: A สมเด็จชานหมาก is a pressed rectangular powder tablet with the quid as one ingredient; the relic proper is an unmoulded lump. Same class, different object
- vs rian-kechi: A monk medallion is struck metal bearing his likeness — the same barami, but a made thing; the quid came from his own mouth. Portrait versus residue
- vs takrut: A takrut is an inscribed metal sheet rolled into a tube (class yantra_wattu); a foil-wrapped quid can look alike, but inside is residue, not a yantra, and the power claimed is the monk's body, not an inscription
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:th-wiki-wat-chanthawat — วัดจันทาวาส — วิกิพีเดีย; s:th-wiki-luang-pu-thong-ayana — หลวงปู่ทอง อายะนะ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:th-wiki-betel-chewing — การเคี้ยวหมากในประเทศไทย — วิกิพีเดีย; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited

## จตุคามรามเทพ · chatukham ramthep · Jatukham Rammathep
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/jatukham/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/jatukham.json
id: jatukham · level: kind
aliases: จตุคาม · องค์จตุคาม · ท้าวจตุคาม ท้าวรามเทพ · jatukam ramathep · jatukham · chatukham · Jatukam Ramathep · the wealth guardian
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: medallion · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-south
origin: วัดพระมหาธาตุวรมหาวิหาร นครศรีธรรมราช Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan, Nakhon Si Thammarat · พล.ต.ต. ขุนพันธรักษ์ราชเดช เป็นผู้มีบทบาทหลักในรุ่นแรก Pol. Maj. Gen. Khun Phantharak Ratchadet had the central role in the first run · First run 1987 (BE 2530) at the city-horoscope ceremony; the boom peaked in 2006–07 after Khun Phantharak's cremation · Nakhon Si Thammarat, southern Thailand
what (th): เหรียญกลมใหญ่รูปเทพผู้รักษาวัดพระมหาธาตุ นครศรีธรรมราช — ท้าวจตุคามและท้าวรามเทพ ภายหลังนับเป็นองค์เดียว กระแส พ.ศ. ๒๕๕๐ ทำให้เป็นวัตถุมงคลแห่งชาติชั่วคราว เป็นเทพที่บูชา ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): A large disc bearing the guardian devas of Wat Phra Mahathat, Nakhon Si Thammarat — Thao Jatukham and Thao Rammathep, later read as one being. The 2007 boom made it a national wealth phenomenon for a season; a deva venerated through the object, nothing to feed.
story: Jatukham and Rammathep are the guardian devas of the Great Relic at Nakhon Si Thammarat, held in legend to be a Srivijaya king who became a bodhisattva; the four in the name (จตุ) were once four directional guardians. The first run was pressed in 1987 for the city-horoscope ceremony with the police general Khun Phantharak Ratchadet at its centre: a sun-moon powder disc ringed by eight Rahus. When he was cremated early in 2007 the country bought everything with the name on it — the 49-baht first-run disc was quoted in the tens of millions, nearly a thousand variations were issued, an estimated 22 billion baht changed hands, a woman died in a crush at a temple release, and there were killings over pieces. Then it cooled, which is the part of the story a buyer should know.
keeping: Deva tier: veneration, not feeding; can be set down. Its provenance question is which run and what it cost, not who kept it.
- look at: Size: a disc around 5 cm, larger than ordinary amulets; a small Jatukham is a later variant or a locket [cited]
- look at: A seated deva at the centre with a ring: eight Rahus on the first type, zodiac animals on many later ones [cited]
- look at: City pillar on the reverse [cited]
- look at: Herbal powder and metal bodies across nearly a thousand variations, so the run name on the disc carries more than the form [cited]
- look at: Srivijaya-style modelling of the figure [cited]
- vs phra-rahu: A Rahu amulet is one head swallowing a disc, usually in shell; the Jatukham is a big disc where eight small Rahus ring a seated deva.
- vs thao-wessuwan: Wessuwan is a standing giant with a club; Jatukham is a seated four-armed deva on a disc.
- vs rian-kechi: A monk medallion shows a monk at coin size; the Jatukham shows a deva at twice that.
- vs luang-pu-thuat: Both are southern; Luang Pu Thuat is a monk in robes, Jatukham a crowned deva.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:en-wiki-jatukham — Jatukham Rammathep — Wikipedia; s:th-wiki-jatukham — จตุคามรามเทพ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## จิ้งจกสองหาง · chingchok song hang · Two-tailed gecko
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/chingchok-song-hang/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/chingchok-song-hang.json
id: chingchok-song-hang · level: kind
aliases: จิ้งจก ๒ หาง · จิ้งจกหางแฉก · jingjok song hang · jing jok 2 hang · forked-tail gecko charm · double-tailed house gecko
class: เครื่องรางธรรมชาติ (natural talisman) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: natural · materials: — · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th
origin: วัดโพธิ์รัตนาราม ราชบุรี (พระสมเด็จหลังจิ้งจกสองหาง พ.ศ. ๒๕๒๐) Wat Pho Rattanaram, Ratchaburi — the one named issue, a somdet with the gecko on the reverse, c. B.E. 2520 (th.wikipedia) · พระอธิการคง จิตตคโม (พระสมเด็จหลังจิ้งจก) Phra Athikan Khong Chittakhamo for that issue; the natural charm has no maker · The belief is undated folk knowledge; one named issue is 1977 · Thailand
what (th): จิ้งจกบ้านที่หางงอกใหม่เป็นสองแฉก ถือเป็นของหายากตามธรรมชาติ เก็บแห้งไว้เพื่อโชคลาภเมตตา ไม่ต้องเสก ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง ของแกะเลียนแบบมีมาก
what (en): A house gecko whose regrown tail forked in two, kept dried as a natural rarity for luck and favour. Nothing conferred and nothing to feed; carved imitations far outnumber the real thing.
story: A gecko drops its tail to escape and regrows it in two to six weeks; now and then the regrowth forks. That animal, found dead or kept, is dried and boxed as a windfall charm. A temple in Ratchaburi put the two-tailed gecko on the back of a somdet around 1977 — evidence the belief was common enough to borrow. Ms 6983 does not mention it; this is folk knowledge, not treatise.
keeping: Kept dry in its box. No offerings owed, nobody home. Safe to adopt with unknown history, the same as any natural talisman.
- look at: On a real specimen the regrown fork is duller and coarser-scaled than the body and lacks the original tail's segment lines — regrowth, not a second tail [tradition]
- look at: A dried gecko is brittle, shrunken, eye-sockets sunk; a glossy plump one is resin [tradition]
- look at: A carved or cast gecko is an image, not the anomaly; class shifts from natural talisman to consecrated object and the seller should say which [catalogue]
- look at: No consecration is required for the natural piece; its claim rests on the anomaly, as with the one-eyed coconut [catalogue]
- vs kala-ta-diao: Same class, different anomaly: a coconut shell with one eye versus a lizard with two tails.
- vs salika: A salika is a carved or cast bird for speech-charm, never a real animal; a two-tailed gecko in its natural form is the animal itself.
- vs khot-kala: A khot kala is a concretion, formless; the gecko is a creature with a legible anomaly.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/7b8e296f0331eb24a1b8f2616de4ba052f0c6422d3e12e0865082feb23ff986f.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Albert kok · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=10059777

confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ชูชก · chuchok · Chuchok (the beggar of the Vessantara Jataka)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/chuchok/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/chuchok.json
id: chuchok · level: kind
aliases: พ่อปู่ชูชก · ตาชูชก · พราหมณ์ชูชก · chujok · choochok · jujaka · Jujaka · the beggar brahmin
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass) · functions: ค้าขาย (trade, selling), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-central, th
origin: ไม่มีวัดต้นกำเนิดเดียว · วิกิพีเดียไทยเอ่ยถึงมณฑปพ่อปู่ชูชกและรูปชูชก “ใหญ่ที่สุดในโลก” ที่วัดป้อมรามัญ ตำบลสวนพริก อยุธยา No single origin temple. Thai Wikipedia names a Chuchok pavilion (มณฑปพ่อปู่ชูชก) and a claimed world's-largest Chuchok at Wat Pom Raman, Tambon Suan Phrik, Ayutthaya · หลายวัดหลายเกจิ ไม่มีผู้สร้างต้นแบบ Many temples and monks; no founding maker · The character is canonical — kan 5 of the thirteen kan of the Maha Wessandon Jataka is his. The charm is modern; the trade treats it as a recent devotion, and no dated first issue is named here · Central Thailand, then nationwide
what (th): พราหมณ์ขอทานผู้ไม่รู้จักเหนื่อยในชาดก คนขายและคนขอพกไว้ด้วยตรรกะว่าไม่มีใครเคยปฏิเสธเขา เป็นศรัทธาของตลาด ทั้งรูปบูชาและจี้ห้อยคอ
what (en): The jataka's tireless beggar, carried by sellers and askers on the logic that no one ever refused him. A statue-and-pendant devotion of the marketplace.
story: In the Vessantara Jataka Chuchok is an ugly old brahmin beggar with a young wife, Amittada; mocked by the village women, she refuses to fetch water until he finds her servants. He walks to the forest hermitage, asks Vessantara for the children Kanha and Jali, is given them, and drags them off on a cord; at King Sanjaya's court the grandchildren are redeemed for a fortune, and at his first meal as a rich man he eats until he bursts. The thirteen kan of the story are preached every year in the Thet Mahachat, and kan 5 is his. The market keeps one line of it — he asked and was given — and a temple in Ayutthaya now houses what it calls the world's largest Chuchok. Describing the devotion is not endorsing it: the story's own verdict on him is the belly.
keeping: Class unassigned: not in the vault's vocabulary. Traders keep him as an asking-figure — venerated with respect and offerings, not fed as a dependent — and this record files him that way ahead of a knower's ruling. Nobody is raised in the figure, so history matters less than with a kuman.
- look at: An old man with a beggar's kit, never a monk portrait or a Buddha; the figure is the tell [catalogue]
- look at: Hunched and pot-bellied: the jataka kills him by overeating, so the belly is the signature [cited]
- look at: Often with the two children on a cord, or bag and staff — scenes from kan 5 and kan 8 [tradition]
- look at: The logic is 'asked and was never refused' — a seller's figure. Nothing is fed [catalogue]
- look at: Cast brass or resin statuettes and small cast pendants; the material adds nothing to the kind [tradition]
- vs rup-lersi: Both are bearded old men. A lersi wears a tiger skin and topknot and is venerated as a teacher; Chuchok carries a beggar's bag and staff and is asked for the asking-luck of the story's villain
- vs phra-siwali: Phra Sivali is a robed arahant with umbrella and bowl to whom gains come unasked (class phra_khrueang); Chuchok is a lay brahmin who asks. Robe versus rags settles it
- vs nang-kwak: Both sit on shop shrines. Nang Kwak is a beckoning woman venerated as a deva; Chuchok is an old male beggar the vault has not placed
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/65f937b0d59520f64f03aea9f65a19c5ac4a1a5718edae7148252824a2ad8cb3.jpg · CC BY 4.0 · Chin Jirayu · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=146439230

## ลูกแก้วธาตุ · dat-lone · Dat-lone (weikza alchemical ball)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/dat-lone/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/dat-lone.json
id: dat-lone · level: kind
native: ဓာတ်လုံး (my)
aliases: ดั๊ตโลน · ลูกธาตุพม่า · เหล็กไหลพม่า · dat lone · datlone · dhat lone · pyada lone · alchemical ball · weizza ball · Burmese philosopher's stone
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: bead · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: mm
origin:  · วิชชาสายปรอทและสายเหล็ก Weikza of the mercury (pyada) and iron (than) paths · Undated; the weikza movement as now known is placed in the Konbaung period · Myanmar
what (th): ลูกกลมโลหะที่วิชชาพม่าหุงขึ้นจากปรอทหรือเหล็ก เชื่อกันว่าเมื่อสำเร็จจะให้คงกระพัน อายุยืน และเป็นบันไดสู่ความเป็นวิชชา เป็นคู่เทียบของเหล็กไหลไทย แต่เหล็กไหลเป็นของที่ไปเอามา ส่วนดั๊ตโลนเป็นของที่ทำขึ้น
what (en): The alchemical ball of the Burmese weikza tradition: mercury or iron fired through the stages until it is held to be finished. Carried for invulnerability and long life, and for the adept a step toward becoming a weikza. The Burmese counterpart of Thai lek lai — but lek lai is fetched from a cave and a dat-lone is made in a fire.
story: The mercury-path weikza study transmutation, producing gold and silver from common metals; the finished ball is the dat-lone. The tradition holds that the accomplished adept keeps or swallows the ball and does not die as others do, but withdraws to wait for Maitreya — which is how many Burmese speak of Bo Bo Aung and Bo Min Gaung today. Six paths are named in the Burmese article: mercury, iron, medicine, in, mantra and the spirit-infused blade.
keeping: Nobody home and nothing owed. The Thai class vocabulary leaves it unplaced: not a natural talisman (it is made), not a yantra object (no inscription), not a Buddha image. That refusal is the record.
- look at: A worked, polished ball rather than a rough fragment; the object was made, not found [tradition]
- look at: No inscription and no figure — unlike a takrut or a Buddha, its claim rests on the material alone [catalogue]
- look at: An iron-path ball answers a magnet; a mercury-path ball does not. The magnet separates the two paths and exposes a plated substitute [inference]
- look at: Dense and cold, and it does not stretch under flame; the Thai lek lai story is of a metal that softens and draws like thread when heated with honey [cited]
- look at: Thai listings have no fixed word for it; anything sold as 'Burmese lek lai' should be asked whether it was made or dug, because that is the whole difference [tradition]
- vs lek-lai: Lek lai is a natural metal fetched from a cave by rite; its power is held to be inherent, and the Thai class calls it a natural talisman. A dat-lone is made: a weikza fires mercury or iron up through the stages until the ball is finished, so the power is in the work. Same look in the hand — a dark lustrous lump — opposite provenance question. Both have nobody home. Ask 'found or fired?' in either direction.
- vs luk-om: A Thai luk om is a ball of pressed powder or wax, light and soft; a dat-lone is dense metal.
- vs mustika: A Malay-Indonesian mustika is a stone or pearl found inside an animal or plant, a natural object; a dat-lone is manufactured metal.
- vs khot-kala: A khot kala is a concretion found in a coconut shell, not metal, and not made.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/f352dd88d6956cc32d42091e32ac22cbaf9e78b2f84cfb02ccf17c425609e439.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Emily Khine · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=72214358
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/5e076cab0e951c7edd6491df9fcaa6b357ea616a2299cb2a37974ce2cd0fd13b.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Hintha · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=11340616
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/1bc676c37f85754345f88fca0f807472ea2d3dc36424df5df542995818777dce.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Lionslayer · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=39768471

## ยันต์ฮู้จีน · fu · Taoist paper talisman (fu)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/fu-talisman/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/fu-talisman.json
id: fu-talisman · level: kind
native: 符 · 符籙 (zh) · phù lục · bùa (vi)
aliases: ฮู้ · ฮู้จีน · ยันต์จีน · ยันต์กระดาษจีน · ยันต์เซียนจีน · fulu · hu · hu-a · phù · phù lục · fulu · Chinese paper charm · Daoist talisman
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: diaspora, th, my, sg
origin:  · ดาวสือ (道士) หรือหมอพิธี (法師) และศาลเจ้าจีน Daoist priests (daoshi) and ritual masters (fashi); in Southeast Asia also spirit mediums and shrine counters · Han-dynasty fu survive on bamboo slips; the practice is continuous · China, carried by Chinese communities into Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam
what (th): กระดาษเหลืองเขียนหมึกแดงหรือดำเป็นอักษรคำสั่งและเส้นยันต์ตามแบบเต๋า ประทับตรา ใช้ติดบ้าน พกติดตัว หรือเผาละลายน้ำดื่ม ศาลเจ้าจีนในไทย มาเลเซีย สิงคโปร์ออกให้ ไทยเรียกยันต์ฮู้จีน พลังอยู่ที่อักษรและตรา ไม่มีผู้สถิต
what (en): The Taoist paper talisman: a yellow strip written in red or black with commands to spirits and asemic strokes, sealed, and then pasted over a door, carried folded, or burned into water and drunk. Chinese shrines in Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore issue them; Thai retail calls them ยันต์ฮู้จีน. Power in the writing and the seal, nobody home.
story: A daoshi or fashi who has received the craft writes it, and the writing is meant to be unreadable: instructions to deities, exorcistic signs, occasionally a recipe. The type names the job: 平安符 for safety, 鎮宅符 to settle a house, 護身符 to guard the body, 五雷符 the five thunders. Han-dynasty examples survive on bamboo. In Bangkok the Chao Pho Suea shrine sells printed sheets; online, Thai sellers list ยันต์ฮู้จีน as already blessed, to carry or post at home, and a cloth version printed with Nezha.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. When it has done its year or is torn it is burned, not binned, which the trade holds and the record does not verify. A fu that a medium wrote for a named person is still impersonal in class; the personalisation is in the writing, not in a resident.
- look at: Yellow paper, cinnabar-red or black ink; the colours are the first read [cited]
- look at: Three parts, header with three ticks, body, foot, plus a seal impression; a sheet missing the seal is unfinished by the tradition's own account [cited]
- look at: Three uses: pasted, carried, or burned into 符水 talisman water; the type name (平安符, 鎮宅符, 護身符, 五雷符) says which [cited]
- look at: Irregular strokes that stretch or stack characters and mix in non-characters; deliberately unreadable to the uninitiated [cited]
- look at: Thai retail sells it as ยันต์ฮู้จีน for carrying or posting at home, and also a cloth version printed with a deity (ฮู้ยันต์ผ้า); the cloth form is a Thai-market crossover with ผ้ายันต์ [catalogue]
- look at: Fu issued by spirit mediums at the Nine Emperor / vegetarian festival are said to be written in trance, sometimes with the medium's blood. The trade holds this; not verified against a source here [tradition]
- vs bua: Bùa is the Vietnamese word around the same paper, extended to cloth pouches and metal; the fu is the Taoist yellow strip itself.
- vs pha-yan: Thai yantra cloth is cloth, in Khom script, in grids; the fu is yellow paper in stretched Chinese script. Thai shops now sell a cloth ฮู้ that sits between the two.
- vs takrut: A takrut is rolled metal; a fu is folded paper. Both carried, both impersonal.
- vs khmer-yantra-cloth: Khmer yantra is cloth in Khmer script; the fu is paper in Chinese.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/3a04f38f9fc07c5a779b273fcb23b093841f282c442d6f2818dae4adcf0f3ef8.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · HMGiovanniV · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=133835109
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/305b550d860a27eba462fae7074e0090ba49cb9cce42a7bd0bfebebfb46f86b1.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Mkckim · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=7901081
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/bdf82950b4b7bd7ed2c0b4ae586da868826588352b6dd03eac8f0847b9f266de.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Taiwankengo · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=69524929
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/c628bbfe5dc745f5d6c57c56aed026f4f812260b507ab4ce533877a5fbd790ea.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Nomad112 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=101261192

## หนุมาน · hanuman · Hanuman figure
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/hanuman/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/hanuman.json
id: hanuman · level: kind
aliases: พระหนุมาน · หนุมานเชิญธง · หนุมานแกะ · hanuman · phra hanuman · Hanuman amulet · monkey-general charm
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), มหาอุด (stopping projectiles / misfire), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), ล่องหน (invisibility), สะกด (subduing, binding, putting to sleep), ถ้อยความ (legal dispute — made to retreat), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างหนุมาน 8 แบบ ใน ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ms 6983) · ปัจจุบันหลายวัด Eight recipes in ms 6983; modern pieces from many wats · The Ramakien Hanuman of the Thai court tradition; the treatise is a nineteenth-to-twentieth-century compilation of older formulas (tradition) · Central Thailand for the treatise tradition; nationwide today
what (th): รูปหนุมาน ทหารเอกลิงเผือกของพระรามในรามเกียรติ์ ทำเป็นเครื่องราง ตำราเก่าให้แกะจากรากไม้หรือปั้นจากว่านแล้วอมไว้ในปาก ปัจจุบันเป็นรูปหล่อและเหรียญห้อยคอ
what (en): A figure of Hanuman, Rama's white-monkey general of the Ramakien, made as a charm. The old treatise carves him from root or moulds him from herbs and has the bearer hold him in the mouth; today he is a cast figure or medallion at the neck.
story: Ms 6983 gives eight recipes. Method 1 carves double-jasmine root into a seated Hanuman, inscribes syllables on legs, chest and back, consecrates it 108 times; held in the mouth after seven recitations, blade and spear cannot strike, and the text prices it at one chang of gold. Method 3 is a squatting Hanuman with hands over his eyes, kneaded in lac and consecrated a thousand times; the treatise gives a making-recipe; its ingredients are not reproduced here. The household he enters falls asleep. Method 7 is another making whose ingredients are likewise not reproduced; it promises that held in the mouth 'all disputes withdraw' and lords fear the bearer. Method 8 is made in the ubosot and, steeped in scented oil, shuts the eyes, ears and mouths of a house.
keeping: The modern cast Hanuman is kept as a deity: respect, no feeding. The treatise Hanuman is commanded and carried in the mouth, and classes.md places that courtroom Hanuman with the hun phayon; several recipes use ingredients this catalogue does not reproduce, so its making and maker are the provenance question. Class here follows the market object; the making, not the shape, decides any given piece.
- look at: Treatise figures are one finger-breadth tall, carved from double-jasmine root or moulded from diamond-herbs and nyctinastic leaves in lac, then lacquered and gilded [catalogue]
- look at: Method 1 places อะกะถะตะสะ on both legs, นะมะการา on the chest, อุปัทธะเว on the back — a loupe finds the inscription where the text says [catalogue]
- look at: Postures the recipes name: seated cross-legged, squatting, eyes covered, kneeling with palms joined [catalogue]
- look at: Market pieces are cast metal, the 'Hanuman raising the banner' pose standing with a flag, the wat on the base [tradition]
- look at: The Hanuman as a yantra design (tattoo or cloth) is read for คงกระพัน and เมตตามหานิยม [cited]
- vs hun-phayon: A hun phayon is a man-shaped effigy animated to guard, fed daily. The treatise Hanuman, held in the mouth and commanded, belongs with it per classes.md; the market Hanuman is a venerated deity figure. The making settles the class, not the shape.
- vs rup-lersi: A hermit figure is a bearded old man in tiger skin; Hanuman is a crowned monkey
- vs phaya-khrut: Garuda has wings and a beak; Hanuman has a monkey's face and no wings

## หุ่นพยนต์ · hun phayon · Hun Payon (animated effigy)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/hun-phayon/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/hun-phayon.json
id: hun-phayon · level: kind
aliases: พยนต์ · หุ่นพยนต์เฝ้าทรัพย์ · หุ่นฟาง · hun payon · hoon payon · hun payont · hun phayont · servant effigy · straw golem · guardian effigy
class: หุ่นพยนต์ (animated effigy / servant-golem) · resident: animated · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983 · Undated treatise; the practice is older than any surviving print of it · Central Thai tradition
what (th): หุ่นรูปคน — ดิน ฟาง ผ้า หรือโลหะ — ที่ถูกปลุกด้วยยันต์และคาถาให้ทำหน้าที่เป็นผู้รับใช้หรือผู้เฝ้า ผู้อยู่ในหุ่นคือสิ่งที่ถูกบังคับให้ขยับ ไม่ใช่ผีที่มีชื่อหรือเทพที่บูชา จึงเป็นหมวดของตัวเอง
what (en): An effigy — figure, cloth, or metal — animated by yantra and spell to act as a servant or guardian. The occupant is a compelled animation rather than a named ghost or venerated deva, which is what makes it its own class.
story: The treatise gives two recipes. In the first, earth is moulded into a man holding a club; a yantra wrapped round a fueang of quicksilver goes into the belly, and the maker resolves aloud that it should watch for thieves and cause them only hardship, never death. In the second, thirty-two stalks of rice straw are bound with splints, wrapped in cloth, given a spear, and the maker meditates through the thirty-two parts of the body while binding, then wakes it with a katha whose Thai words are simply 'wake, wake, wake'. For both, the treatise gives a making-recipe; its ingredients are not reproduced here. It goes into a small shrine, gets liquor and rice every day, and is told its instructions. Thieves, the text says, see it as a living person.
keeping: Kept with respect: offerings and regard, and told its job. Worth asking who kept it before you.
- look at: It is a person-shaped figure, never a Buddha image or a medallion [catalogue]
- look at: Body is earth, straw, cloth or cast metal, not pressed powder [catalogue]
- look at: Look for a yantra wrapping and a sealed cavity in the belly where the charge sits [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise houses it in a small shrine and feeds it liquor and rice daily. A kept-and-fed object is a hun payon or a kuman, never a phra khrueang [catalogue]
- vs phra-somdet: A hun payon is a figure compelled to serve and fed; a somdej is a pressed Buddha tablet with nobody home. Ask what the object is shaped like and whether its keeper feeds it — both answers separate them.
- vs kuman-thong: A kuman thong is a child figure housing a raised child-spirit, kept as family; a hun payon is an armed adult figure whose occupant is an animation, not a named ghost. Class and upkeep differ.
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak is a beckoning woman venerated for trade; a hun payon guards property and frightens thieves
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/aeb7c0f63953dc29d01809edd868cb3b8a2d0e09f15eb116c5e31c6cdc3d91f4.jpg · CC0 · วิถีชนเผ่า · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=149191229
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/fb763138a73c75022118f4b710b4b82493cd83cd0f1be0ec9691bcf2974e7dc9.jpg · CC0 · วิถีชนเผ่า · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=149191240

## ยันต์พม่า · in · In (Burmese cabalistic square)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/in-yantra/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/in-yantra.json
id: in-yantra · level: kind
native: အင်း (my)
aliases: อินพม่า · ยันต์อิน · ตารางยันต์พม่า · inn · in yantra · in-saya work · Burmese yantra · Burmese magic square · cabalistic square
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: cloth · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), กันผี (warding spirits), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: mm, shan
origin:  · ครูอิน (in-saya) และวิชชา (weikza) สายอิน In-saya (square-masters) and weikza of the in path; the tradition holds the in path the most powerful beside the iron path · Undated; the weikza movement as now known is placed in the Konbaung period · Myanmar and Shan State
what (th): ตารางยันต์ของพม่า เรียกว่า อิน แบ่งเป็นช่องใส่เลขและอักษร คำนวณจากวันเวลาเกิดของผู้รับ เขียนบนกระดาษหรือผ้า สลักบนโลหะ หรือสักลงบนผิว ถือกันว่าคุ้มครอง กันภัย และให้เมตตา
what (en): The Burmese in: a cabalistic square whose cells hold numerals and letters, cast from the recipient's birth date and time by an in-saya or weikza of the in path. Drawn on paper or cloth, engraved on metal, or tattooed. The Burmese counterpart of the Thai yantra, with a grid where the Thai sheet has figures.
story: The weikza paths divide by medium: mercury, iron, medicine, and the in. The in path and the iron path are held the most powerful. The square is calculated from the wearer's birth date and time, and the tradition credits a square scratched on a house or tree with drawing lightning to it. That cuts both ways: an in protects, and an in written wrong is a hazard, which is why the square-master is a specialist.
keeping: Nobody home and nothing owed: an inscribed object, kept clean and high like any blessed thing. What matters is who wrote it and whether it was written for you.
- look at: A grid of numerals in Burmese script. Thai yantra carry Khom or Tham letters around figures; the script alone places the sheet [cited]
- look at: Drawn, engraved in stone or metal, or tattooed; the same square travels across media [cited]
- look at: Cast from the recipient's birth date and time, so two squares of the same purpose need not match cell for cell [cited]
- look at: Cotton shirts written edge to edge with squares, attributed to Mandalay in the nineteenth century, sit in the Textile Museum at George Washington University (Commons file titles below) [inference]
- look at: Burmese tattooing is htoe kwin; the yantra-tattooing article names it apart from Thai sak yant [cited]
- vs pha-yan: Both are impersonal inscribed objects. A Thai pha yan draws lines and Khom letters round a Buddha, lersi or animal; a Burmese in is a numbered grid in Burmese script with no central figure.
- vs yan-lanna: A Lanna yan is written in Tham script; an in is written in Burmese script and numerals. Shan cloths sit between the two, so read the letters.
- vs takrut: A takrut is a rolled tube; an in stays flat on paper, cloth or skin.
- vs khmer-yantra-cloth: Khmer yantra cloth is Khom letters and figures; the in is a grid of numbers.

## ยันต์มลายู · jimat · Jimat / azimat (Islamic-Malay written amulet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/jimat/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/jimat.json
id: jimat · level: kind
native: جيمت / عزيمة (Jawi) · jimat / azimat (ms) · jimat / azimat (id) · عزيمة (ar)
aliases: จิมัต · อาซิมัต · ตะกรุดมลายู · azimat · azimah · tamimah · ta'wiz · Malay talisman · Quranic amulet · taweez
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure) · region: my, id, sg
origin:  · โต๊ะครู / ดุกุน / กียาอี Written by a religious teacher (tok guru, kyai), a bomoh or a dukun; the writer's standing is the object's credential · Arrived with Islam in the Malay world; the paper-and-Arabic form is continuous with the ta'wiz of the wider Muslim world · Malay peninsula, Sumatra, Java
what (th): เครื่องรางเขียนของโลกมลายู: กระดาษหรือผ้าจารอายะฮ์อัลกุรอาน พระนามพระเจ้า หรือตารางเลข พับเล็กพกติดตัว ผูกรถ หรือแขวนบ้าน พลังอยู่ที่ตัวเขียนและผู้เขียน ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): The written amulet of the Malay world: Quranic verses, names of God or a numbered square, set down in Arabic on paper or cloth by a teacher or bomoh, folded small and carried, tied to a vehicle or hung in a house. Power sits in the writing and the hand that wrote it; nobody is home.
story: Azimat is Arabic ʿazīma; jimat is what Malay made of it, and ta'wiz is the same thing in South Asia. Indonesian Wikipedia defines it as an object or writing hung on a body, a vehicle or a building to turn aside sickness and misfortune (tolak bala). The theological fight is part of the object: stricter schools call it shirk — seeking protection from other than God — while others accept it when the text is Quran alone. The Malay trade also sells it for kebal (invulnerability), pelaris (custom for a shop) and pengasihan (attraction); those three are what the vault's function keys are doing here.
keeping: Impersonal — nothing is owed and nothing is fed. Keepers treat the writing as scripture: kept dry, kept out of unclean places, and the trade holds that the fold is not opened.
- look at: It is writing, not an image: Arabic or Jawi letters and Arabic numerals. A figure means it is something else [cited]
- look at: A grid of numbers or letters whose rows sum alike — the wafq al-a'dad, in occult use since the 13th century [cited]
- look at: Folded flat into a pouch, locket, armband or sewn into clothing — not rolled into a tube like a takrut [cited]
- look at: Hung on a person, a vehicle or a building — the same object serves all three [cited]
- look at: A baju rajah is a whole shirt written over as one jimat; the Commons example belonged to a 1948–49 fighter [cited]
- vs takrut: Same class, different script and fold: a takrut is a metal sheet in Khom letters rolled into a tube; a jimat is paper or cloth in Arabic folded flat. Neither is fed.
- vs rajah: Rajah is the written formula; jimat is the carried object that holds it. Indonesian usage lets rajah stand alone on skin or a shirt, and jimat cover unwritten charms too.
- vs in-yantra: A Burmese in is a grid yantra in Burmese letters from a Buddhist weikza lineage; a jimat is Arabic in an Islamic one. Same idea of a squared diagram, different script and sacred language.
- vs pha-yan: A Thai pha yan is a large cloth carrying figures — Buddha, hermit, animals; a jimat is aniconic, text only.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/708d408beae22908cfd4dafb34e554dfa61cbe33e83a09895abe1d5173f148bb.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Muhamad Izzul Fiqih · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=156701516
