confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## กะลาตาเดียว · kala ta diao · One-eyed coconut shell
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/kala-ta-diao/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/kala-ta-diao.json
id: kala-ta-diao · level: kind
aliases: กะลามะพร้าวตาเดียว · มะพร้าวตาเดียว · กะลาตาเดียวแกะราหู · kala ta diew · kala tah diao · single-eyed coconut · one-eyed coconut Rahu
class: เครื่องรางธรรมชาติ (natural talisman) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: natural · materials: กะลา (coconut shell) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall) · region: th-central, th
origin: วัดศีรษะทอง นครปฐม (ตามการ์ด) Wat Sisa Thong, Nakhon Pathom, per the reference card · หลวงพ่อน้อย วัดศีรษะทอง (ตามการ์ด) Luang Pho Noi of Wat Sisa Thong, per the reference card — the Rahu-carving lineage the trade names · · Central Thailand
what (th): กะลามะพร้าวที่มีตาเดียวแทนที่จะมีสาม ของหายากตามธรรมชาติ ไม่ใช่ของทำ เก็บทั้งลูกหรือแกะเป็นราหู ความหายากนั่นเองคือของขลัง
what (en): A coconut shell with a single eye where every normal shell has three — a natural anomaly, not a crafted thing, carved (often into Rahu) or kept whole. The rarity IS the charm.
story: The treatise's Rahu chapter tells of two hermits on Mount Yugandhara who made the Suriyaprapha and Chanthaprapha yantra to relieve human poverty, and its first instruction is to find a one-eyed coconut shell and carve from it a Rahu swallowing the moon and a Rahu swallowing the sun. Offerings run to the planets' numbers — six of each for the sun, fifteen for the moon — the work is done on a full moon or an eclipse day, and the finished plaques go into gold and silver cases. The trade's best-known lineage is Wat Sisa Thong in Nakhon Pathom; uncarved rings and pendants are the commoner, cheaper form.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Once carved into Rahu it takes Rahu's veneration — the deva class, not the shell's; the tradition's black offerings on Rahu's days are the Rahu record's business.
- look at: A normal shell has three eyes; this one has one. The anomaly is the charm; nothing was carved to make it [tradition]
- look at: The treatise's Rahu recipe starts by finding a one-eyed shell and carving two Rahu from it — one swallowing the moon, one the sun — then inscribing the Chanthaprapha and Suriyaprapha yantra [catalogue]
- look at: Shell ages by wear, not patina. A true eye is a germination pore with a fibrous rim; a bored hole is round and clean — a statement about coconuts, not a verdict on a piece [tradition]
- look at: In listings กะลา is mostly the carved palad khik; form settles it [catalogue]
- look at: The card counts it the most-attested of the market's newer terms, at low retail prices; counts are rebuilt from catalog.db at build time [catalogue]
- vs khot-kala: A khot kala is a stone-hard nodule found inside the nut; a kala ta diao is the shell itself with one eye. Same tree, two different finds, both natural class.
- vs phra-rahu: Phra Rahu is a venerated deva, carved from a one-eyed shell by preference but from anything at hand; the uncarved shell is a natural object with no resident. Once carved and inscribed the object is both.
- vs palad-khik: A palad khik carved from shell is a phallus; the one-eyed shell is kept whole or carved as Rahu. The material term กะลา covers both, which is why the search uses the compound.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ตะกรุดเขมร · katha (Khmer takrut) · Khmer katha scroll (rolled inscribed talisman)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/khmer-katha/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/khmer-katha.json
id: khmer-katha · level: kind
native: គាថា (km)
aliases: ตะกรุดขอม · คาถาเขมร · ตะกรุดกัมพูชา · kathâ · kata khmer · gatha scroll · takrut khmer · Cambodian takrut · rolled gatha amulet · Khmer scroll charm
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tube · materials: ตะกั่ว (lead), ทองแดง (copper), เนื้อเงิน (silver), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: kh
origin:  · ครูขแมร์ / อาจารย์ (อาจาร) Made and blessed by kru khmer and achar — lay ritual specialists of the yogavacara line — and by monks · Undated tradition; the script and formula practice descend from the Angkor and post-Angkor Theravada world, damaged under the Khmer Rouge · Cambodia
what (th): แผ่นโลหะจารคาถาบาลีด้วยตัวขอม ม้วนเป็นหลอด ของขลังเขมรที่ตะกรุดไทยสืบมา พลังอยู่ที่อักขระและพิธี ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): A metal sheet inscribed with a Pali gatha in Khmer letters and rolled into a tube: the Cambodian ancestor of the Thai takrut. Power sits in the inscription and the rite; nobody is home and nothing is owed.
story: In Cambodia a gatha (គាថា) is a Pali formula chanted, inscribed on amulets and cloth, and tattooed on skin, always in the Khom hand that is reserved for sacred text and held to carry power of its own. The Khmer Wikipedia article on the gatha names amulets, yantra cloth and sak yant as its three carriers. Makers are kru khmer and achar, lay specialists of the yogavacara line that François Bizot documented at Angkor; the same esoteric Theravada that gives Thailand its katha and takrut. Under the Khmer Rouge nearly every temple and library was destroyed and the monkhood fell from tens of thousands to under three thousand, so surviving lineages are thin and much of what is sold as Khmer today was made afterwards.
keeping: Impersonal: carried with respect, nothing fed, nothing owed. Ask which kru wrote it; that is the whole provenance question.
- look at: The letters are the Khmer Mul / Khom hand used for Pali and yantra on cloth, paper and brass in both Cambodia and Thailand, not modern Khmer print [cited]
- look at: Khom Thai is the Khmer script adopted in Thailand around the 10th century with letterforms added around the 15th; the hand alone rarely settles whether a tube is Cambodian or Thai [cited]
- look at: Thai, Khmer and Lao practice share the form — Pali mixed with the local language, seldom Sanskrit — so language of the formula does not separate them either [cited]
- look at: Sheet is gold, silver, nak, lead or an alloy, incised with a steel stylus; the same metals the Thai takrut article lists [cited]
- look at: In the Thai trade 'takrut khmer' usually names a maker's lineage (southern Isan or a Cambodian kru) rather than a form; no Lazada TH listing title in catalog.db carries เขมร or ขอม at all [catalogue]
- vs takrut: Same class, same rolled-tube form: the Thai takrut descends from this tradition and the Khom letters on it are the Khmer script. What separates them is the maker's lineage and hand, never the shape.
- vs khmer-yantra-cloth: A Khmer yantra cloth is a drawn square of fabric hung or folded; the katha is a rolled metal tube. Same class, different form.
- vs in-yantra: A Burmese in is a square sheet in Burmese letters, folded or flat; the katha is rolled and written in Khmer.
- vs lao-yan: Lao yantra is written in Tham letters of the Lanna family; the Khmer katha in Khom. Round Tham versus angular Khom is visible under a loupe.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/abc5a5c5ec6233e9c92673a67fe27ff295826828a63f67b02c5abd024c196c4c.jpg · CC0 · Unknown artistUnknown artist · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=106114895
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/42da48bcb5d896d53fc5aa9a6787d61e78a751b4046867aacc23cd11fbb26032.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Majmunka · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=18277331
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/54c6ea9374217c2da09eab3968255fc90f04176c23a3aa705099dd1ffeef76f2.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Ms Sarah Welch · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=73992293
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:en-wiki-khmer-script — Khmer script — Wikipedia; s:en-wiki-khom-thai-script — Khom Thai script — Wikipedia; s:th-wiki-khom-thai — อักษรขอมไทย — วิกิพีเดีย; s:km-wiki-gatha — គាថា — វិគីភីឌា; s:en-wiki-southern-esoteric-buddhism — Southern Esoteric Buddhism — Wikipedia; s:en-wiki-achar-khmer — Achar (Khmer lay ritualist) — Wikipedia; s:en-wiki-kru-khmer — Kru Khmer (traditional healers) — Wikipedia; s:en-wiki-buddhism-cambodia — Buddhism in Cambodia — Wikipedia; s:th-wiki-saiyasat — ไสยศาสตร์ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:th-wiki-takrut — ตะกรุด — วิกิพีเดีย; s:en-wiki-yantra-tattooing — Yantra tattooing — Wikipedia; s:catalog-db — manuscript-crawler catalog.db — items table, 13,020 Lazada TH listings (method=commerce) + 6,990 manuscripts; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited

## กริช · keris · Keris / kris (the heirloom dagger)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/keris/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/keris.json
id: keris · level: kind
native: كريس (Jawi) · keris (ms) · keris (id) · ꦏꦼꦫꦶꦱ꧀ · keris (ngoko) / dhuwung (krama) (jv)
aliases: กริชมลายู · กริชชวา · กริชปัตตานี · kris · kriss · creese · dhuwung · wangkingan · karih · kris dagger · pusaka blade
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: blade · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: — · region: id, my, th-south, sg
origin:  · เอิมปู (empu) ช่างตีที่ต้องมีทั้งฝีมือและบารมี The empu, a smith expected to hold technical skill and spiritual standing together; Javanese tradition credits him with literature, history and the occult besides · Old Java: inscriptions of 901–904 CE name keris among offerings (id.wikipedia); the recognisable form is attested by 1361 under Majapahit (en.wikipedia). UNESCO intangible heritage list, 2008. · Java, then across the archipelago, the peninsula and southern Thailand
what (th): มีดสั้นสองคมของโลกมลายู-ชวา โคนไม่สมมาตร ใบตรงหรือคดเลขคี่ ลายพามอร์จากเหล็กซ้อนชั้น ถือเป็นปูซากา (มรดกศักดิ์สิทธิ์) ที่มีทัวะห์หรือ “ผู้อยู่” ในเล่ม ล้างน้ำมันปีละครั้ง ห้ามชักเล่น ห้ามชี้
what (en): The double-edged dagger of the Malay-Javanese world: asymmetric base, straight or odd-waved blade, pattern-welded pamor. Kept as pusaka — a sanctified heirloom held to carry tuah, and in Javanese belief an isi or presence of its own — washed and oiled once a year, never drawn idly, never pointed.
story: Javanese legend has keris that move of their own will and kill at will; an owner tested the match by sleeping with the blade under the pillow and reading the dream — bad dreams meant the blade should go. Every year in Sura (Muharram) the jamasan strips old oil and rust with lime, noni or coconut water, re-etches the pamor with warangan, and lays down fresh jasmine or sandalwood oil. The empu who forged it was expected to be a spiritual as much as a technical master; pamor once used meteoric iron, now nickel. Pointing a keris at someone is held to foretell their death, which is why silat players touch the tip to the ground before a demonstration. UNESCO listed it in 2008.
keeping: Class null: the vault has no pusaka category — the keris is neither a venerated deva, a fed ghost, nor an animated servant, and khong_thammachat (inherent power) misses the isi belief. What the keeper owes is nonetheless specific: a high resting place, the yearly jamasan wash and oiling, never drawn for show, never pointed, and passed on if the dreams say the match is wrong. A keris whose history is unknown is, in its own tradition, a keris you sleep on before you keep.
- look at: The base is asymmetric — one side flares wider — with the ganja as a separate crosspiece [cited]
- look at: Count the waves: always odd, usually 3 to 13, rarely up to 29. An even count is a mark against the type [cited]
- look at: Pamor is laminated iron and nickelous iron, brought up by etching with warangan (arsenic) and lime juice; a painted-on pattern has no depth under a loupe [cited]
- look at: The tang (pesi) seats in the hilt and comes apart; hilt and sheath are routinely younger than the blade, so date the blade alone [cited]
- look at: Tangguh is the trade's dating of a blade by period and region; the categories overlap and the source says so [cited]
- look at: Worn at the back in Java and Bali, at the front by Bugis and Malays — how it is worn in a photograph places it [cited]
- vs mit-mo: A mit mo is a Thai ritual knife the maker uses on other objects — straight blade, yantra on the hilt; a keris is an heirloom in its own right, asymmetric base, pamor, an odd count of waves.
- vs jimat: A jimat is carried writing; a keris is a blade held to carry its own tuah. One is scripture, the other is a pusaka.
- vs mustika: A mustika stone is sometimes set into a keris hilt or ring; the stone is the mustika, the blade is the keris, and each carries its own claim.

## คดกะลา · khot kala · Coconut-shell concretion
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/khot-kala/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/khot-kala.json
id: khot-kala · level: kind
aliases: คด · คต · คดมะพร้าว · khod kala · kod kala · coconut bezoar · khot stone
class: เครื่องรางธรรมชาติ (natural talisman) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: natural · materials: กะลา (coconut shell) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades) · region: th
origin:  ·  · · Thailand generally
what (th): ก้อนแข็งเหมือนหินที่พบเกิดในลูกมะพร้าว หนึ่งในตระกูลคด — หินที่ไม่น่าจะมีในสิ่งมีชีวิต เก็บทั้งก้อนตามที่พบ ฤทธิ์อยู่ในตัว ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): A stone-hard concretion found grown inside a coconut — one of the คด family of impossible stones found in living things. Kept whole as found; power inherent, none to feed.
story: There is no recipe for a khot and cannot be: it is found, not made. The treatise's preface files คต with fangs, horns and minerals as the self-potent natural objects people carried before anyone inscribed anything. The trade names each by its host — a khot kala grew inside a coconut — and holds it for protection and hardness against blades; those functions are the tradition's claim, not the treatise's, which says only that the thing has power in itself.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Keep it as it was found; safe to adopt with no history at all, since it never had a maker.
- look at: The treatise's own classification puts คต among the self-potent natural objects (ของทนสิทธิ์) beside fangs, horns and minerals — the first amulets humans used, it says [catalogue]
- look at: คด is a family named by host — coconut, stone, shell, termite mound and more; the trade holds that the host names the virtue [tradition]
- look at: Hard, dense, matte or glassy, with no tool marks; a nodule that shows carving is something else [catalogue]
- look at: A nodule still carrying a fragment of shell carries its own provenance; the material axis dates shell by wear [inference]
- look at: The bare word cannot be searched: 474 of 484 corpus hits were other words, so only the compound is carried [catalogue]
- vs kala-ta-diao: The one-eyed shell is the husk with a single eye; the khot is a stone-hard nodule from inside the nut. Same tree, two finds.
- vs lek-lai: Lek lai is a lustrous dark metal claimed from caves; a khot has no metallic sheen and a named plant or animal host.
- vs bia-kae: A bia kae is a cowrie a monk fills and seals — made; a khot is found. Both small, hard and cased.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: low · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ขุนแผน · khun phaen · Khun Phaen tablet
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/khun-phaen/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/khun-phaen.json
id: khun-phaen · level: kind
aliases: พระขุนแผน · ขุนแผนพลายกุมาร · khun paen · khun pan · khun phaen phlai kuman · Khun Paen amulet
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th-central
origin:  · ตั้งชื่อตามขุนแผน ตัวเอกเสภาขุนช้างขุนแผน; สายที่วงการยกให้: หลวงพ่อกวย วัดโฆสิตาราม ชัยนาท (พลายกุมาร) และหลวงปู่ทิม วัดละหารไร่ Named for Khun Phaen, the epic's charm-master. The reference cards single out Luang Pho Kuai of Wat Khositaram, Chainat (Khun Phaen Phlai Kuman) and Luang Pu Thim of Wat Lahan Rai as the trade's benchmark lines · Epic first printed 1872; the trade holds that the tablet form predates the name, from Ayutthaya-period caches in the Suphanburi area — unverified here · Suphanburi, Chainat, Rayong by line
what (th): พระพิมพ์ในซุ้มเรือนแก้ว ตั้งชื่อตามขุนแผนผู้เชี่ยวชาญวิชาในเสภา — พระเครื่ององค์เดียวที่เรื่องมวลสารสำคัญเท่ากับพิมพ์ทรง บางองค์เป็นผงล้วน บางองค์ผสมมวลสารอื่น และผิวไม่บอก
what (en): A pressed tablet in the classic arch — named for the epic's charm-master, and the one amulet whose material story matters as much as its form. Some are pure powder; some are worked with other material, and the difference does not show on the surface.
story: Khun Phaen in the epic is the master of yantra and katha who raises a kuman thong from his own stillborn son; the tablet that borrows his name is made as a charm of attraction, and some lines state that 'prai kuman' material went into the body — that single fact is the seam between classes. The vault counted the seam rather than deciding it: of 389 listings naming กุมาร, 106 are ขุนแผน. The reference cards name Luang Pho Kuai's Khun Phaen Phlai Kuman as the trade's benchmark line. The hybrid is measured, not forced; a future class that splits form from material would resolve it, and this record does not pre-empt that.
keeping: Kept as an amulet: nobody to feed. But ask what went into the batch — the vault rates its provenance sensitivity medium to high because of the material, even though its upkeep is an amulet's.
- look at: A five-sided ruean kaeo arch, not the straight-edged rectangle and bell-glass arch of a somdet [tradition]
- look at: Some moulds show a kuman figure with the Buddha — the epic's Golden Child on the tablet [cited]
- look at: Powder or fired-clay body; the trade looks for a distinct-coloured plug at the back or flecks in the body, but what went in does not reliably show on the surface [catalogue]
- look at: Reverse often carries an embedded takrut or a hand-incised yantra [tradition]
- look at: The line name declares the material: the words in the title are the seller's own statement of what went in. Read the name before the surface [catalogue]
- vs phra-somdet: A somdet is a straight-edged rectangle with a bell-glass arch and a white body; a khun phaen is five-sided with a ruean kaeo arch. Same class by form, different provenance question.
- vs kuman-thong: A kuman thong is a child figure you feed; a khun phaen is a Buddha tablet kept like any amulet. The scanner tags both 'kuman' because the word is present; the class is not the same.
- vs phra-phong-suphan: Phra Phong Suphan is a triangular fired-clay cache tablet without the ruean kaeo arch; both are Suphanburi names, which is the confusion
- vs phra-kru: A cache-find khun phaen is old fired clay with nobody home; a modern temple khun phaen is powder with its own material story — the name is shared, the material story is not

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/d512b7fcc15c598fb79a105e145746fbc0897a4c813868e6da99ab9f1e9174c4.png · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Somdej.watrakang · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=99853135

## เจ้าแม่กวนอิม · kuan im · Guanyin pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/kuan-im/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/kuan-im.json
id: kuan-im · level: kind
native: 觀音 (zh)
aliases: กวนอิม · พระโพธิสัตว์กวนอิม · พระอวโลกิเตศวร · kuan yin · guan yin · chao mae kuan im · Kuan Yin · Avalokitesvara · Goddess of Mercy
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), เนื้อเงิน (silver) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th, diaspora
origin:  · ศาลเจ้าจีนและวัดพุทธหลายแห่ง Chinese shrines and Buddhist wats alike; no single maker · Avalokitesvara became female in East Asia by about the twelfth century; the Thai cult is Thai-Chinese and Mahayana in origin · Thai-Chinese communities, Yaowarat and nationwide
what (th): จี้หรือรูปเจ้าแม่กวนอิม พระโพธิสัตว์อวโลกิเตศวรในร่างหญิงชุดขาว เทพแห่งความเมตตาของคนไทยเชื้อสายจีน นิยมทำเป็นหยกแกะ
what (en): A pendant or small image of Guanyin, Avalokitesvara in her white-robed female form, the compassion figure of Thai-Chinese households. The classic body is carved jade, worn on a cord.
story: Avalokitesvara was male in India and became female in China, merged with the legend of Princess Miaoshan. Thai-Chinese families venerate her as Chao Mae, keep vegetarian days and skip beef; big images stand at Wat Yannawa and Wat Huai Pla Kang. Jade pendants were worn long before Thai wats began issuing Guanyin medallions.
keeping: Kept by veneration: flowers, water, precepts kept on her days. Not fed, not a ghost. The vault class is deva-tier though she is a bodhisattva; the keeping is the same.
- look at: A white-robed woman with vase and willow: not a beckoning Nang Kwak, not a Buddha [cited]
- look at: Thousand-armed form reads as a fan of arms round the figure [cited]
- look at: Carved jade pendants are cool in the hand and translucent at the edge; many are never consecrated at a wat at all, which is a class note, not a flaw [tradition]
- look at: Devotees commonly keep vegetarian days and abstain from beef; a keeper asking about diet is a tell for the cult, not the object [cited]
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak kneels in Thai dress with one hand beckoning; Guanyin stands or sits in a white robe with a vase. Both deva-tier.
- vs phra-phrom: Brahma has four faces; Guanyin one, and female
- vs phra-siwali: Sivali is a monk with umbrella and bowl, class phra_khrueang; Guanyin is a bodhisattva in lay white

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/c8cd073818d3d4aa4a8b9fb33fa2ab919229837bcd30a7c9711d9cc1f86bb696.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · กสิณธร ราชโอรส · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=35525150
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/26286243c73b98a2635c11b6d828d0d9f1221ffc71cdaecf9eb48b0ab8215ef4.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · กสิณธร ราชโอรส · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=35535268

## กุมารทอง · kuman thong · Kuman Thong (raised child-spirit)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/kuman-thong/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/kuman-thong.json
id: kuman-thong · level: kind
aliases: กุมาร · พรายกุมาร · ลูกเทพ · kuman tong · guman thong · kumanthong · phrai kuman · golden boy · golden child · spirit-child effigy
class: กุมารทอง (raised child-spirit) · resident: raised_spirit · upkeep: feeding · provenance sensitivity: high
form: figure · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: ค้าขาย (trade, selling), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983; modern figures are temple issues by many makers · Already in the Khun Chang Khun Phaen epic (first printed 1872; Prince Damrong's standard edition 1917–18); the practice is older than the print · Central Thai tradition
what (th): รูปเด็กที่ไม่ใช่รูปแทน แต่เป็นบ้าน — วิญญาณเด็กถูกผูกไว้แล้วเลี้ยงอย่างลูก ให้น้ำแดง ข้าว ของเล่น ตั้งชื่อ พูดด้วย ขอให้ช่วย ตำรา ๖๙๘๓ บันทึกวิธีสร้างแบบโบราณไว้เต็ม ในฐานะบันทึกประเพณี
what (en): A child figure that is not a depiction but a home: a bound child-spirit, raised as family — fed sweet red drink and rice, named, spoken to, asked for help. The corpus holds the historical making in full, framed as ethnography, at manuscript 6983.
story: In the Khun Chang Khun Phaen epic the hero cuts the stillborn son from his murdered wife Bua Khli and dries the body over a fire at a temple; the spirit becomes his scout and defender. Manuscript 6983 (pp. 84–86) records the same making as a recipe: seek the ghost of a mother who died with child, best on a Saturday or Tuesday; propitiate with spicy shrimp and fish salad; consecrate the knife; carry the child to the ordination hall, set a seven-turn sai sin enclosure under a white canopy hung with eight yantras; roast the body on a chaiyaphruek frame by night until dry before dawn; lacquer and gild it. Thereafter rice every day, woken and called before it eats, sent out with one katha and closed with another when put away. Thai Wikipedia says the old method gave way to moulded clay, wood or metal figures into which a spirit is invited, and that from 2015 the luk thep doll is the newest form.
keeping: Feeding. Rice, red drink and toys; a name; conversation. Neglect is the failure mode — a hungry, ignored kuman turns mischievous or leaves. Who raised it and what it was taught travels with it, so the history is the first question, not the price.
- look at: It is a child figure — never a Buddha image, never an armed adult (that is a hun phayon) [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise lacquers and gilds the whole body: a dark lacquer skin under gold leaf is the type mark and the reason for the name [catalogue]
- look at: Modern bodies are moulded clay, carved wood or cast metal, dressed as a Thai boy in a chong kraben [cited]
- look at: Look for a sealed cavity at the base or back where the filling sits; what went in is the provenance question [tradition]
- look at: Red drink, sweets and toys set before it mark a fed object; a kept-and-fed child figure is a kuman, not a phra khrueang [catalogue]
- vs hun-phayon: A kuman is a child figure raised as family; a hun phayon is an armed adult effigy animated to serve. Both are fed, but one is a named child and the other a compelled animation.
- vs khun-phaen: A khun phaen is a pressed Buddha tablet kept like any amulet even when its material carries prai-kuman powder; a kuman thong is a child figure you feed.
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak is a beckoning woman venerated as a deva; a kuman is a bound child-spirit fed as family
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/8c7c8424b560376523ed967ee6382af09e90449d2603aea911bf3d523e6ceeeb.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Greg Field · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=30448412
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/79c1567c4d4186f483845577b56bafb4947f1a2e76259168825f88cf71612050.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Michelle von Bärlin · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=30950388
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/1c92dd8a0692c3be2fdaa69634209ee5dac7a07715a9bc8150ab3164cdf83f4f.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Xufanc · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=39735042
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/5e2b56e5fb176b4d94ba824c0d5adf0d364f90cf736a140b00773fa31976bb29.jpg · CC BY 3.0 · Sailko · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=54861211

## พระหยกพม่า · kyauk sein hpaya · Burmese jadeite Buddha pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/jade-buddha-burmese/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/jade-buddha-burmese.json
id: jade-buddha-burmese · level: kind
native: ကျောက်စိမ်းဘုရား (my)
aliases: จี้หยกพม่า · พระหยก · หยกพม่าแท้ · พระหยกเจไดต์ · phra yok phama · jade Buddha · Burma jade Buddha · jadeite Buddha pendant · jade Buddha pendant · Burma jade amulet · jadeite Buddha
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: mm
origin:  · ช่างแกะหยกมัณฑะเลย์และตลาดหยก Mandalay lapidaries and the Mandalay jade market; King Mindon (1857–78) let Chinese lapidaries set up there to work stone between Burma and China · Stone from the Hpakant mines, Kachin State, 350 km north of Mandalay on the Uyu River; Chinese sources note Burmese jadeite from the 10th century · Hpakant (stone) and Mandalay (carving and trade)
what (th): จี้พระพุทธรูปแกะจากหยกเจไดต์พม่า หินจากเหมืองผากันต์ในรัฐกะฉิ่น แกะและขายที่มัณฑะเลย์ ตลาดไทยขายในชื่อ 'หยกพม่าแท้' เรื่องสำคัญคือเนื้อหิน — เจไดต์หรือเนไฟรต์ ธรรมชาติหรือย้อม
what (en): A Buddha pendant carved from Burmese jadeite: stone from the Hpakant mines in Kachin State, cut and traded in Mandalay, sold in Thailand as 'genuine Burma jade'. A Buddha image with nobody home; the whole question is the stone — jadeite or nephrite, untreated or bleached and dyed.
story: Myanmar supplies around seventy per cent of the world's high-quality jadeite. Chinese sources note Burmese stone from the tenth century; the Qianlong Emperor went to war for green jade; King Mindon let Chinese lapidaries set up in Mandalay, and the market there still grinds, polishes and inspects it by UV torch. Hpakant's landslides killed more than a hundred in 2015 and more than 170 in 2020. The Myanma Gems Enterprise grades imperial, commercial and utility jade, the last for carving. The pendant on a cord carries all of that.
keeping: Nobody home and nothing owed: a Buddha image, kept as any phra khrueang. The provenance question is authenticity and stone grade, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Jadeite polishes to a vitreous lustre; nephrite polishes oily. Jadeite is denser and has the higher refractive index [cited]
- look at: Imperial green comes from traces of chromium, and colour in a single stone is usually uneven; a flat, even green across the whole pendant is the thing to look at twice [cited]
- look at: A untreated; B bleached and polymer-impregnated; C dyed; B+C both. Under a loupe dye pools in fractures, and polymer dulls the lustre [cited]
- look at: Mandalay traders inspect rough with a portable UV torch; polymer in B jade fluoresces where natural stone stays dull [inference]
- look at: Carved, not pressed: no mould seam, and tool marks read under the loupe. A moulded 'jade' with a seam is glass or resin [inference]
- vs kuan-im: Jade Guanyin pendants show a standing woman with a vase; a Burmese jade Buddha is a Buddha. Same stone, same trade, different figure and class.
- vs pixiu: A pixiu is a jade beast for wealth; this is a Buddha for veneration.
- vs rup-lo: A cast figure is metal with a seam; a jade Buddha is carved stone with tool marks.

## เหล็กไหล · lek lai · Lek lai (living iron)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/lek-lai/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/lek-lai.json
id: lek-lai · level: kind
native: batu serandak (ms)
aliases: เหล็กไหลเงินยวง · เหล็กไหลเพชรดำ · เหล็กไหลท้องปลาไหล · เหล็กไหลปีกแมลงทับ · รังเหล็กไหล · ขี้เหล็กไหล · leklai · lek-lai · lekhlai · living metal · cave iron · batu serandak (Malay)
class: เครื่องรางธรรมชาติ (natural talisman) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: natural · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), มหาอุด (stopping projectiles / misfire), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th, my
origin:  ·  · · Caves, per the belief; Thailand and Malaysia (Malay batu serandak)
what (th): โลหะดำมันวาวที่เชื่อว่ามีชีวิต ตัดจากถ้ำด้วยพิธี ว่ากินน้ำผึ้งและกันคมอาวุธ ฤทธิ์อยู่ในตัวของมันเอง เป็นหมวดที่ของปลอมชอบที่สุด ซึ่งเป็นคำเตือนในตัว
what (en): A dark lustrous metal the tradition holds to be alive — drawn from caves by rite, said to drink honey and turn aside blades. Power inherent in the thing itself; the category every faker loves, which is its own caution.
story: The lore puts it in caves under the guard of devas, forest spirits, naga or giants; only merit or wichaa lets a person take it, and the harvest is done with honey smeared nearby and fire played on the mass until it stretches to the honey as a thread and parts. Near its keeper, the belief goes, blades, guns and gunpowder fail. Thai Wikipedia grades it — the metal, its 'nest', its 'residue' — names varieties by colour, dates the dictionary entry to B.E. 2525, and then explains the samples as low-melting metals or alloys, meteorite or silicate, with the rainbow sheen as thin-film interference. Both halves belong in the record.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed by the class. Some keepers offer honey because the lore says it drinks it; that is a courtesy from the story, not an upkeep the vocabulary records. Safe to adopt with unknown history; the risk is the price, not the spirit.
- look at: Thai Wikipedia grades three tiers: lek lai proper (lustrous, drawn out by fire), rang lek lai 'the nest' (duller, does not draw), and khi lek lai 'the residue' (wax-like, matte black, brittle) [cited]
- look at: Named varieties by colour: เงินยวง silver, เพชรดำ black diamond, ท้องปลาไหล eel-belly, ปีกแมลงทับ beetle-wing, among others in the article [cited]
- look at: An iridescent rainbow sheen is thin-film interference, per the article's sceptical section, which names low-melting metals and alloys (gallium, mercury), meteorite and silicates as what samples turn out to be [cited]
- look at: The lore's harvest: honey is smeared near it and fire played on it until it stretches to the honey as a thread and parts; ordinary people cannot take it, and it shocks the hand [cited]
- look at: The Royal Institute Dictionary lists lek lai beside takrut and yantra cloth as its examples of เครื่องราง; the treatise quotes that definition, and its tiger-waking katha wakes 'the lek lai and copper things' too [catalogue]
- look at: The holding key calls it the category every faker loves; a caution about the category, never about a piece [catalogue]
- vs khot-kala: A khot is a stone-hard nodule from inside a coconut with no metallic sheen; lek lai is a lustrous dark metal. Both natural class, found not made.
- vs bia-kae: A bia kae is a cowrie sealed over quicksilver by a monk — a made object; lek lai claims to be found. Listings pair them because both are 'living' fillings for a case.
- vs dat-lone: Lek lai is found — harvested from cave rock with honey and fire, class khong_thammachat; the Burmese dat-lone is made — fired by a weikza practitioner from metals and mercury. Found or fired is the question that separates them.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:th-wiki-lek-lai — เหล็กไหล — วิกิพีเดีย; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ล็อกเก็ต · locket · photograph locket
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/locket/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/locket.json
id: locket · level: kind
aliases: ล็อกเกต · ล็อคเก็ต · ล็อกเก็ตรูปถ่าย · รูปถ่ายติดกระจก · locket · lockget · rup thai tit krachok · monk photo locket · glass-fronted photo amulet
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: locket · materials: เกศา (hair of the master), จีวร (robe cloth), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), ผงพุทธคุณ (powder of the Buddha's qualities) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th
origin:  · วัดและสำนักทั่วประเทศ Temples nationwide · Follows the spread of photography; the oldest free Commons example is a photo-under-glass of Phra Phimontham (Nak), Wat Arun, dated BE 2475 · Nationwide
what (th): รูปถ่ายพระเกจิผนึกใต้กระจกหรือเรซิน หลังอุดผง เกศา หรือจีวร — คือที่บรรจุพระธาตุแบบพกพาในรูปของเครื่องประดับ พลังอยู่ที่มวลสารและพิธี ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A monk's photograph sealed under glass or resin, often with powder, hair, or robe-cloth packed behind the image — a portable reliquary in costume jewellery's clothes.
story: The older form is a photograph mounted under glass; the free Commons example is a diamond-shaped one of Phra Phimontham (Nak) of Wat Arun dated BE 2475. The modern form is a colour print under clear resin with the reverse packed with sacred powder, hair, robe cloth or a takrut and usually stamped with a code. The trade names the finishes by background — gold or plain — and the large sizes as jumbo.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; a blessed object. What is behind the picture is a relic of the monk, not a resident.
- look at: The front is a photograph, not struck or cast relief [catalogue]
- look at: The reverse is a sealed packing; look for powder, hair, robe threads, a takrut [catalogue]
- look at: Glass or a domed resin front in a metal bezel [tradition]
- look at: The vault files it under blessed objects, not Buddha-amulets: power is in the relic packing and the rite, and nobody is home [catalogue]
- vs rian-kechi: A medallion is solid struck metal; a locket is a photograph under glass with material behind it
- vs takrut: A takrut is a rolled tube and may be one of the things packed inside a locket's back; the locket is the housing, the takrut the charge
- vs phra-somdet: A somdej is pressed powder through and through; a locket only has powder as packing behind a picture

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/36684723491f017bfbd66a3d1baf13c81c193c1c2795c5a1e93d7ab8a3369bd9.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Witwatarun · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=90905313

## หลวงปู่ทวด · luang pu thuat · Luang Pu Thuat amulet
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/luang-pu-thuat/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/luang-pu-thuat.json
id: luang-pu-thuat · level: kind
aliases: หลวงพ่อทวด · หลวงปู่ทวดเหยียบน้ำทะเลจืด · หลวงพ่อทวดวัดช้างให้ · หลังเตารีด · luang phor thuad · luang pu tuad · lp thuad · Luang Phor Thuad · the monk who walked on water
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), เนื้อเงิน (silver) · functions: แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades) · region: th-south, th
origin: วัดช้างให้ จังหวัดปัตตานี Wat Chang Hai, Pattani · พระอาจารย์ทิม ธมฺมธโร เจ้าอาวาสวัดช้างให้ Phra Ajahn Tim Dhammadharo, abbot of Wat Chang Hai · The monk is Ayutthaya-period (1582–1682); the amulets begin in 1954 · Southern Thailand
what (th): พระเครื่องรูปหลวงปู่ทวด พระเถระสมัยอยุธยาแห่งภาคใต้ ผู้เหยียบน้ำทะเลจืด รุ่นแรกเนื้อว่านจากวัดช้างให้ พ.ศ. ๒๔๙๗ รุ่นหลังเป็นเหรียญและหลังเตารีด นับถือทางแคล้วคลาด
what (en): Amulets bearing Luang Pu Thuat, the Ayutthaya-period southern monk who is said to have turned seawater fresh. The first run is a wan-powder tablet from Wat Chang Hai in 1954; later runs are medallions and cast figures, carried for narrow escape.
story: Phra Ajahn Tim, abbot of Wat Chang Hai in Pattani, made the first batch in 1954 entirely of wan herbal material; medallions followed, and the cast flat-iron-back form from 1962. Devotees credit the amulet with surviving fatal road accidents, which is why it rides on dashboards nationwide. The tradition holds that the bearer cannot die a violent or untimely death.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; a phra khrueang of a monk.
- look at: A seated bald monk, not a Buddha [cited]
- look at: The first batch is wan (herbal) material through and through: a brown vegetable body, not white powder and not metal [cited]
- look at: The flat-iron back is a metal casting with a raised reverse and exists only from 2505 on [cited]
- look at: The medallions read Wat Chang Hai and a year, like any rian kechi [tradition]
- vs rian-kechi: A Luang Pu Thuat medallion is a rian kechi of him; this kind also covers the wan tablets and castings the medallion form does not
- vs rup-lo: A cast Luang Pu Thuat is a rup lo with its own canonical form, the flat-iron back; other monks' castings do not have it
- vs jatukham: Both are southern; Jatukham is a large deity medallion from Nakhon Si Thammarat, Luang Pu Thuat a monk from Pattani

## ลูกอม · luk om · Luk om (mouth-held charm ball)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/luk-om/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/luk-om.json
id: luk-om · level: kind
aliases: ลูกอมผง · ลูกอมเนื้อผง · ลูกอมดำ · ลูกอมหมากทุย · look om · luk-om · amulet ball · sucking charm
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: bead · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), ผงพุทธคุณ (powder of the Buddha's qualities), เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste), ตะกั่ว (lead) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง); วัดบางปะกอก (หลวงปู่พริ้ง) ทำลูกอมดำ; วัดหนองบัว กาญจนบุรี มีลูกอมหมากทุย Anonymous treatise ms 6983; th.wikipedia names Luang Pu Phring of Wat Bang Pakok (ลูกอมดำ) and the Wat Nong Bua line of Luang Pu Yim (ลูกอมหมากทุย) as makers, without recipe · Undated treatise; the named temple issues are 20th century by their makers' lives · Central Thai tradition
what (th): ลูกกลมเล็กที่ปั้นจากผงว่าน ม้วนจากกระดาษยันต์พันด้าย หรือกล่อมจากแผ่นตะกั่วลงยันต์ เสกแล้วอมไว้ในปากหรือพกติดตัว ตำราให้เพื่อคงกระพันแคล้วคลาด ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A small consecrated ball — herb-and-powder paste, a thread-wound paper yantra, or an inscribed lead sheet worked round — held in the mouth or carried, for invulnerability and evasion. Power in the yantra and the chant; nobody home.
story: Five recipes. In the first, two 'diamond' herbs, lodestone, laterite and phet sangkhat are ground with a yantra drawn on the grinding stone, moulded, chanted 108 times, buried three days, dug up, chanted a thousand times and then held in the mouth against spear, sword, gun, thorns and fangs. In the second the Samphutthe yantra is drawn on paper, rolled round, wound with thread and held under the tongue. The third writes the Sixteen Buddhas formula on a slate and erases it to powder 108 times, mixing that with stupa lichen and pencil dust in lacquer — the same erased-chalk method that makes ผงพุทธคุณ. The fifth beats lead thin, inscribes it, works it into a ball and says a traveller who holds it can go without water. Named temple issues — the black luk om of Wat Bang Pakok, the ลูกอมหมากทุย of the Wat Nong Bua line — are on th.wikipedia by name only.
keeping: Nothing to feed. Kept like a takrut. The treatise's fourth recipe boasts the ball still works if swallowed; a lead one should not be.
- look at: A solid ball with no string hole; a pierced ball is a rosary bead or a luk sakot [catalogue]
- look at: Body tells the recipe: dull shrunken herb-paste, thread wound over paper, or lead with fold seams where the sheet was worked round [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise has it held in the mouth, so it is small; a fist-sized ball is an altar piece, not a luk om [catalogue]
- look at: The word is also 'candy' in Thai; listing counts under the bare term are mostly sweets [inference]
- vs luk-sakot: Luk sakot are several small pierced lead beads on a cord; a luk om is one solid ball. The lead luk om of recipe 5 is the closest — it has no hole.
- vs si-phueng: Si phueng is wax in a box, smeared on the lips; a luk om is a hard ball.
sources: s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:th-wiki-wat-bang-pakok — วัดบางปะกอก — วิกิพีเดีย; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07)
confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## ลูกสะกด · luk sakot · Luk sakot (lead subduing beads)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/luk-sakot/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/luk-sakot.json
id: luk-sakot · level: kind
aliases: ลูกสะกดตะกั่ว · สะกด · look sakot · luk sakod · sakot beads · binding beads
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: bead · materials: ตะกั่ว (lead) · functions: สะกด (subduing, binding, putting to sleep), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th
origin:  ·  · No dated attestation found; the function is in the undated treatise, the bead form is not · 
what (th): เม็ดตะกั่วเล็กจารอักขระ เจาะรูร้อยเชือก ชื่อมาจากหน้าที่ 'สะกด' — ทำให้คนหรือสัตว์นิ่งหรือหลับ ปัจจุบันขายคู่ตะกรุดในความหมายคงกระพันแคล้วคลาด ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): Small incised lead beads, pierced and strung, named for the function สะกด — subduing, putting to sleep — and now sold beside takrut as invulnerability-and-evasion beads. Power in the letters and the chant; nobody home.
story: Ms 6983 has no luk sakot recipe; it has the function. To subdue, hold the image under the tongue; wrap a rosary in paper and seven turns of a thread the treatise specifies and chant 108 times, and the whole house sleeps; steep a takrut in oil in a bronze bowl with the Trinisinghe formula. The strung lead beads of the modern market take the name of that function. What is on them, and who first strung them, this catalogue cannot cite.
keeping: Nothing to feed. Same keeping as a takrut on the same cord. Vault class is an inference from form and making; no source places ลูกสะกด by name.
- look at: Pierced for stringing; a solid ball is a luk om [tradition]
- look at: Lead is soft enough to take a fingernail and greys in the incisions; a bright hard bead is an alloy or a modern cast [catalogue]
- look at: Hand-incised single-line grooves, not raised stamped letters [tradition]
- look at: The name is the function, not the shape; the trade applies it to any small strung metal bead sold for that purpose [catalogue]
- vs luk-om: One solid ball you can hold in the mouth versus several pierced beads on a string.
- vs takrut: A takrut is a rolled sheet tube; a luk sakot is a solid pierced bead. They share a cord so often that a bead on a takrut string is the usual find.
- vs waen-phirot: A phirot is a plaited ring you put on; nothing is strung.
sources: s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: low · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## มีดหมอ · mit mo · Mit mo (ritual knife)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/mit-mo/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/mit-mo.json
id: mit-mo · level: kind
aliases: มีดครู · meed mor · mid mo · mit mor · exorcist's knife · doctor's knife · spirit knife
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: blade · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: กันผี (warding spirits), จังงัง (stupefaction, being frozen), สะกด (subduing, binding, putting to sleep), กำบัง (concealment, going unseen), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades) · region: th-central, th
origin: วัดประดู่ทรงธรรม Wat Pradu Song Tham, Ayutthaya · หลวงพ่อม่วง ตราพระขรรค์เพชร ตามที่ตำราระบุ Luang Pho Muang, 'seal of the Diamond Sword', per the treatise's ascription of Method 1 · Undated treatise; the knife appears in the poem Krai Thong among the hero's weapons per Thai Wikipedia · Ayutthaya, Central Thailand
what (th): มีดที่ตีและลงอักขระเป็นเครื่องมือของหมอผี ใช้ตัดสิ่งที่ผูกมัด ไม่ใช่ตัดให้เลือดออก ตำรา ๖๙๘๓ ในคลังนี้บันทึกตำรับเหล็กสิบชนิดจากวัดประดู่ทรงธรรม
what (en): A knife forged and inscribed as an instrument of the doctor-of-spirits — for cutting what binds, not what bleeds. Manuscript 6983 in this corpus records a ten-iron forge recipe from Wat Pradu Song Tham.
story: Method 1, ascribed to Luang Pho Muang, alloys ten irons from sources the treatise names — stupa, prang and prasat finials, Nam Phi iron, palace-gate iron and more — forged on a Saturday or Tuesday by a smith keeping the precepts, with bai-si trays left and right and monks chanting the Karaniya seven times, then quenched three and seven times and given a handle packed with consecrated powders; the treatise names the quenching liquid and it is not reproduced here. Method 2 forges old iron and broken blades, steeps the knife in scented oil in a bronze bowl and wakes it with a long vernacular rousing-katha. In use it scratches a line the enemy cannot cross, is planted at a hole to put a household to sleep, and is held before the face to pass unseen.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed, by class. The trade adds a custom Thai Wikipedia records: a dead practitioner's knife passes to someone able to command it. The treatise recipe packs the handle with consecrated powder and names other ingredients not reproduced here, so ask what went into it.
- look at: A curved lancet-like blade, neither a sword nor a kitchen knife [cited]
- look at: Glyphs on the blade and tang; an uninscribed blade is a knife, not a mit mo [catalogue]
- look at: The handle is usually a sealed cavity holding powder; look for the plug [catalogue]
- look at: A metal guard plate engraved with yantra numerals [cited]
- look at: The ten-iron alloy is not visible on the surface; nobody can read the forge from the skin [catalogue]
- vs hun-phayon: The treatise puts the knife beside the effigy recipes: the knife is the doctor's instrument with nobody home, the effigy is animated and fed.
- vs takrut: Same class, different form: a rolled tube versus a forged blade.
- vs wua-thanu: A wua thanu is a bull figure fed grass and water; the knife is fed nothing.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/be7f4a2af3f04275cf05d6a8a621648890dd8b56f7a80284b6a723b157fef794.jpg · CC0 · Gavin Symahanou · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=173338719
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:th-wiki-mit-mo — มีดหมอ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited

## หินมุสติกา · mustika · Batu mustika (stones and 'pearls' of inherent power)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/mustika/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/mustika.json
id: mustika · level: kind
native: موستيكا · batu mustika / geliga (ms) · batu mustika (id) · watu mustika (jv)
aliases: มุสติกา · หินเบซัวร์มลายู · เกอลิกา · batu mustika · mustika pearl · geliga · guliga · batu bertuah · bezoar · tuah stone · mustika pearl
class: เครื่องรางธรรมชาติ (natural talisman) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: natural · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall) · region: id, my
origin:  · ไม่มีผู้สร้าง — “พบ” หรือ “ถูกดึงมา” (tarikan gaib) โดยดุกุน Not made: found, cut from an animal, or 'drawn' (tarikan gaib) by a dukun — the finding story is the object's credential · The Asia–Europe bezoar trade of c. 1500–1700 valued Southeast Asian porcupine stones especially (en.wikipedia); the mustika cult on the modern Indonesian market is undated · Java, Sumatra, Borneo, the peninsula
what (th): หินหรือเม็ดธรรมชาติที่โลกมลายู-ชวาถือว่ามีทัวะห์ในตัว — หินแร่ หินเบซัวร์จากท้องสัตว์ (geliga) หรือ “ไข่มุก” จากพืชและสัตว์ — พบ ไม่ได้สร้าง มักเลี่ยมแหวน ตลาดอินโดนีเซียเติมความเชื่อเรื่อง khodam (ผู้อยู่) เข้าไป ซึ่งหมวดของ vault ไม่รองรับ
what (en): A natural stone or nodule the Malay-Javanese world holds to carry its own tuah — a mineral, a bezoar cut from an animal (geliga), or a 'pearl' claimed from a plant or creature. Found, not made; usually ring-set. The Indonesian market adds a khodam, a resident spirit, which the vault's natural-talisman class does not carry — noted, not adopted.
story: The bezoar — Persian pād-zahr, 'antidote' — went out of this region to Europe between about 1500 and 1700 as a universal poison cure, Southeast Asian porcupine stones the most prized, and counterfeits followed until buyers tested them with poisoned needles. On the modern Indonesian market the word mustika has widened to any stone with a story: taken from a snake, found in the forest, seen in a dream, or 'drawn' from the unseen by a dukun. The story is what is sold; the stone is what you get.
keeping: Filed as khong_thammachat: power inherent, nobody home, nothing owed, and an unknown history is a value question rather than a safety one. Some sellers prescribe oiling or incense — shop custom, not upkeep. A seller who says the stone carries a khodam has moved it out of this class by his own claim; that claim is the thing to ask about.
- look at: A true bezoar is a gut concretion; cut or chipped it shows concentric layers round a nucleus [cited]
- look at: Counterfeits are as old as the trade: 16th–17th-century buyers tested stones with poisoned needles and animals. The category's whole history is a fraud history [cited]
- look at: Mineral mustika are ordinary agate, quartz or pebble; the word names the story attached, not the stone. Ask the mineral question separately [tradition]
- look at: Market 'mustika pearls' are smooth rounded nodules whose claimed source — coconut, snake, shell — cannot be read off the object [tradition]
- vs lek-lai: Lek lai is a dark lustrous metal held to be alive; a mustika is a stone, nodule or animal concretion. Same class — power inherent in the thing — and the same buyer's caution.
- vs dat-lone: A Burmese dat-lone is a metal ball a weikza practitioner casts and charges; a mustika is found, never made. Made-versus-found is the line.
- vs khot-kala: A Thai khot kala is the hard concretion found in a coconut; in Malay terms it is one kind of mustika. Same logic, different name.
- vs luk-om: A luk om is a bead a monk makes from powder or herb; a mustika has no maker.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/12abde9f172ecc417efad5bfd467ef111b2a2fabac1509c53684cacc6e54c9fa.jpg · CC0 ·  · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=141695901
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/792c4dafef115fd6181962a681b1740c35e0e806e3226714ae48fe9410ff584b.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Bjoertvedt · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=93474788

## นางกวัก · nang kwak · Nang Kwak (the beckoning lady)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/nang-kwak/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/nang-kwak.json
id: nang-kwak · level: kind
aliases: แม่นางกวัก · นางสุภาวดี · nang kwak · nang gwak · mae nang kwak · beckoning lady · Lady Kwak · shopkeeper's goddess
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), เนื้อดิน (clay body), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste) · functions: ค้าขาย (trade, selling), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure) · region: th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) ให้ ๖ วิธี Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, six methods · Undated treatise; the figure is older than any dated print · Nationwide
what (th): นางกวัก หญิงนั่งยกมือกวักเรียกลูกค้า — ทั้งรูปตั้งหิ้งและจี้ เป็นเทพที่บูชาด้วยความเคารพและเครื่องสักการะเล็กน้อย ตลาดทุกแห่งในประเทศทำมาค้าขายใต้มือของนาง
what (en): The shop-keeper's lady, hand raised in the customer-calling gesture — shelf statue and pendant both. Venerated with respect and small offerings; every market in the country works under her hand.
story: Manuscript 6983 gives six recipes. Carve her from rak-son root, the nang-kwak tuber, or the mistletoe of a fig tree taken from the branch that points east, after offering puffed rice, flowers, banana and sugarcane to the tree; the carver dresses in white, keeps the five precepts, sets a bai-si, and finishes in one day at a good hour. Then inscribe ทุ สะ มะ นิ on forehead and back (or breasts) and ธะนัง โภคัง on the arms, consecrate 108 times, and keep her in a money bag (method 1) or in a case of lip-wax with fragrant oil and krajae paste, a silver plate bearing her yantra lining the bottom (methods 3–6). She is given rice and water daily, called to eat with the household, and in method 6 bathed so the water can be sprinkled on the goods and the boat's prow; the same bath water on your own skin makes her a love charm. The katha names her as the only daughter of Pu Chao Khao Khiao, the forest lord, which is the origin Thai Wikipedia also records beside the Indianised tale of Supawadee blessed by the arahants Kassapa and Sivali.
keeping: Deva tier — the vault says 'arguably'. Owed veneration: red drink, a garland, rice and water, and the treatise says without fail; still worship, not the parenting a kuman needs. Can be set down; the shop that keeps her feeds her out of courtesy.
- look at: A seated woman beckoning: never a Buddha, and not a ghost figure [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise inscribes ทุ-สะ-มะ-นิ on forehead, breasts and back, and ธะนัง / โภคัง on the right and left arms; look for syllables on the body of an old carved piece [catalogue]
- look at: Treatise pieces are carved wood kept in a wax case with a silver yantra plate lining the bottom; the case and plate are part of the object [catalogue]
- look at: Shop lore reads the hand height: above the mouth 'never full', below it 'never enough' [cited]
- look at: Shopfront statues are usually painted resin or plaster in red and gold; pendants are metal or pressed powder [tradition]
- vs hun-phayon: A hun phayon guards property and frightens thieves and is fed daily; Nang Kwak calls customers in. One is a servant, one a patroness.
- vs phra-siwali: Phra Siwali is a standing monk with staff, umbrella and bag; Nang Kwak is a seated woman. The legend has Sivali bless her, and some money bags carry his name.
- vs kuman-thong: A kuman thong is a boy figure raised as family; Nang Kwak is an adult woman venerated as a deva.

## นัต · nat · Nat figure (Burmese spirit-deity)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/nat-figure/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/nat-figure.json
id: nat-figure · level: kind
native: နတ် (my)
aliases: รูปนัต · เทพนัต · เทพทันใจ · โบโบจี · ตะจาหมิ่น · มหาคีรี · nat · nat rupa · Bo Bo Gyi · Thagyamin · Mahagiri · thep than chai · nat statue · Burmese spirit figure · Bo Bo Gyi · Thagyamin · Mahagiri
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), ค้าขาย (trade, selling) · region: mm, shan
origin:  ·  · King Anawrahta (r. 1044–1077) fixed the official pantheon of 37 Great Nats; Thagyamin was set at its head · Across Myanmar; Mount Popa is the centre of nat worship
what (th): รูปนัต เทพารักษ์ของพม่าที่บูชาควบคู่กับพุทธศาสนา มีนัตหลวง ๓๗ ตน นำโดยตะจาหมิ่น (ท้าวสักกะ) มีมหาคีรีเป็นนัตประจำบ้าน และโบโบจีเป็นนัตประจำเจดีย์ ตั้งในศาลที่บ้าน ร้าน และวัด เป็นเทพที่บูชา ไม่ใช่ผีที่เลี้ยง
what (en): Figures of the nats, the spirit-deities venerated in Myanmar alongside Buddhism: the 37 Great Nats headed by Thagyamin (Sakka), Mahagiri the house nat, and Bo Bo Gyi the guardian of each pagoda, kept in shrines at home, in shops and at pagodas. A deva-tier being venerated through the object — worship, not necromancy.
story: Anawrahta fixed the pantheon at 37; most were humans who died violently. Mahagiri was Maung Tint De, a blacksmith's son of Tagaung, burned alive bound to a champak tree by a suspicious king; his sister died with him and both haunted the tree, which was carried to Mount Popa and carved into their figures. Burmese houses still hang a coconut on a post for him. Bo Bo Gyi, an avatar of Indra in the Shwedagon story, pointed to where the pagoda should rise; Thai devotees call him thep than chai, the deity who grants at once, and offer scarves and paso.
keeping: Veneration: fruit, coconut, perfume, a scarf; respect at festivals. Worship, not parenting — nothing raised, nothing fed, nothing closed. The nat's own history (a violent death, a grievance) is the pantheon's, not the object's.
- look at: Three-headed white elephant, conch and fly-whisk: Thagyamin, the one nat who never died a violent death [cited]
- look at: Elderly man, curved cap, cane, pointing finger: Bo Bo Gyi, the pagoda guardian; the finger points to where Shwedagon should stand [cited]
- look at: Nats wear Burmese royal dress even when the pantheon records them as Thai or Shan; the dress does not say where the figure was made [cited]
- look at: In a house the figure is often replaced by a coconut hung at a corner or post and dressed with perfume; a coconut in a hanger is a nat shrine, not litter [cited]
- look at: Offerings are scarves and paso for Bo Bo Gyi, bananas and coconuts generally; a figure with a scarf tied on has been asked something [cited]
- vs thao-wessuwan: Thao Wessuwan is a yaksha with a club; a nat is a human figure in Burmese court dress. Same class — a venerated deva-tier being — different pantheon.
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak beckons with one raised hand; a female nat sits or stands enthroned and does not beckon.
- vs phra-phrom: Phra Phrom has four faces; every nat has one.
- vs tua-pek-kong: Tua Pek Kong is a Chinese elder in Chinese dress with a long beard; Bo Bo Gyi is an elder in Burmese dress with a pointing finger. Both are shop guardians, so the dress is the tell.

## ปลัดขิก · palat khik · Palad khik (phallic waist charm)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/palad-khik/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/palad-khik.json
id: palad-khik · level: kind
aliases: ปลัด · ขุนเพ็ด · อ้ายขิก · palad khik · palat khik · palad kik · pra lad khik · honourable surrogate · phallic amulet · Thai lingam charm
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: other · materials: กะลา (coconut shell), เขาสัตว์ (horn), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), กันผี (warding spirits), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), ค้าขาย (trade, selling) · region: th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) · วิกิพีเดียไทยเอ่ยชื่อหลวงพ่อเหลือ วัดสาวชะโงก เป็นผู้สร้างที่มีชื่อ Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, gives three recipes; Thai Wikipedia names Luang Pho Luea of Wat Sao Cha-ngok as a noted maker · Undated treatise. Both Wikipedias trace the form to the Shiva linga and Indian influence roughly two thousand years back; that is a lineage claim, not a date · Nationwide; the large in-situ shrine on Commons is Phra Nang cave, Krabi, and rocket-festival parades in the Northeast carry oversized ones
what (th): แท่งแกะหรือหล่อรูปอวัยวะเพศชาย พกติดตัวเพื่อโชค การค้า และคุ้มกัน เป็นเครื่องรางที่เก่าแก่ที่สุดแบบหนึ่งของแถบนี้ และเป็นแบบที่ประเพณีเองจัดไว้สองทาง — ของขลังไม่มีผู้อยู่ทางหนึ่ง ที่สถิตของผู้คุ้มครองอีกทางหนึ่ง
what (en): A carved or cast phallic rod, pocket-carried for luck, trade and protection — one of the oldest charm forms in the region, and one the tradition itself files two different ways.
story: The treatise gives three recipes. Method 1 carves golden-shower heartwood, inscribes อุ on the face and กันหะ เนหะ on the flanks, and consecrates with the two-word katha; it wards sorcery, the tip ground in liquor is drunk for poison or fever, it serves as a love charm, and it must not be on the body during intercourse or near a menstruating woman. Method 2 carves and inscribes the same way but consecrates with a long, bawdy vernacular incantation, and is tied at the waist of children against wasting fevers, spirits and the mae sue birth-spirit, or of adults for everything. Method 3 admits tamarind, muai heartwood or mistletoe as well, chants กันหะ เนหะ 108 times with a second short coarse formula, and is worn against sorcery, water-spirits and fangs and tusks, and for attraction. English Wikipedia adds the modern picture: men wear several on a waist cord, shopkeepers set large ones out, and the form is read back to the Shiva linga.
keeping: Class deliberately unassigned: the vault vocabulary leaves ปลัดขิก unplaced because some keepers hold it as an impersonal charm with nobody home and nothing owed, and others as a guardian-spirit vessel. It needs a knower, and this record says so rather than deciding. The treatise's own rules are the only ones on paper: not on the body during intercourse, not near a menstruating woman.
- look at: It is a phallic rod, never a Buddha or a medallion; the form alone names the kind [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise carves it from golden-shower heartwood (methods 1–2) or tamarind, muai heartwood or mistletoe (method 3) and inscribes อุ, กันหะ, เนหะ; look for the letters on face and flanks [catalogue]
- look at: Material reads by eye: wood, coconut shell, horn or cast metal. Wood ages by wear, not patina. Many coconut-shell hits in the corpus are carved palad khik [catalogue]
- look at: A riding figure — monkey, tiger, Nang Kwak — marks a variant; the base form is the plain rod [cited]
- look at: Pieces made from protected-animal material fall under Thai law and CITES; a legal notice, not a judgement [catalogue]
- vs takrut: Both hang at the waist. A takrut is a rolled metal tube with the yantra inside (class yantra_wattu); a palad khik is a solid carved or cast rod whose form is the charm and whose class the vault declines to fix
- vs kala-ta-diao: A one-eyed coconut shell is a natural talisman kept for what it is; a coconut-shell palad khik has been carved into the rod. Same material, different kind
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak is a beckoning woman venerated as a deva; when she rides a palad khik the rod is the object and she is its decoration

## พระบาง · pha bang · Phra Bang pendant (copies of the Lao palladium)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-bang-pendant/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-bang-pendant.json
id: phra-bang-pendant · level: kind
native: ພະບາງ (lo) · ព្រះបាង (km)
aliases: พระบางจำลอง · พระบางหลวงพระบาง · จี้พระบาง · พระบางพุทธลาวัณย์ · phra bang · prabang · pha bang chamlong · Phra Bang Buddhalavarna · Phra Bang replica · Pha Bang amulet · Luang Prabang Buddha pendant
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), เนื้อทองคำ (gold) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: la, th-isan
origin: หอพระบาง วังหลวง หลวงพระบาง (ต้นแบบ) Haw Pha Bang in the Royal Palace grounds, Luang Prabang, houses the original; copies are issued by Lao and Thai temples · ตำนานว่าหล่อที่ลังกา · นักวิชาการว่าศิลปะขอมปลายศตวรรษที่ 12–ต้น 13 Legend: cast in Ceylon; scholars read it as Khmer work of the late twelfth to early thirteenth century · Reached Lan Xang in 1359 as the Khmer king's gift to Fa Ngum; to Vientiane 1705; taken to Bangkok 1778 and returned 1782, taken again 1828 and returned 1867 under Rama IV; moved into the Haw Pha Bang in 2013 · Luang Prabang, which is named after it
what (th): จี้และรูปหล่อย่อส่วนของพระบาง พระพุทธรูปคู่บ้านคู่เมืองลาวที่หลวงพระบางได้ชื่อมาจาก ยืนยกสองพระหัตถ์ ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): Pendants and miniature casts of the Phra Bang, the standing two-palms-forward Buddha that is the palladium of Laos and gave Luang Prabang its name. Nobody home, nothing owed.
story: Legend casts it in Ceylon; scholars read Khmer work of the late twelfth century. The Khmer king gave it to his son-in-law Fa Ngum in 1359 to legitimise Lan Xang, and the city was renamed for it. It is 'thong', an alloy of bronze, gold and silver, in the fear-dispelling gesture with both palms forward. It went to Vientiane in 1705, was carried to Bangkok by Siamese armies in 1778 and again in 1828, and came home for good in 1867 under Rama IV; since 2013 it stands in the Haw Pha Bang on the palace grounds and is carried on the third day of Lao New Year to Wat Mai for bathing. The French Wikipedia adds that a copy is what the museum displays while the original sits in a vault, with rumours placing it elsewhere — so even in Luang Prabang the pilgrim venerates a copy, which is what every pendant is.
keeping: Impersonal: ordinary veneration. Bathing it at New Year echoes what Luang Prabang does with the original.
- look at: Standing, both palms forward: the gesture is the identity; a single raised hand is another image [cited]
- look at: Square face, wing-shaped ear lobes, a large smooth ushnisha, the lower garment's edge visible under the robe [cited]
- look at: The original is 'thong', a bronze-gold-silver alloy the Thai and Khmer articles call ninety percent gold; pendants are brass or plated, so colour proves nothing [cited]
- look at: Sources disagree on the original's height; pendant proportions vary with the model the caster copied, and a mismatch is not a fault [cited]
- look at: Thai temples hold their own Phra Bang replicas (Wat Trilokanat, Nakhon Phanom; Wat Phra Lao, Amnat Charoen), so Thai and Lao issues share the market and the reverse lettering is what places them [cited]
- look at: Every pendant is a modern cast; nothing about one is old. No Lazada TH listing title in catalog.db carries พระบาง [catalogue]
- vs lao-phra-khrueang: A Lao temple amulet may show any Lan Xang type; a Phra Bang pendant is only the standing two-palms-forward figure.
- vs phra-chiang-saen: Chiang Saen figures sit and carry the lotus-bud finial; the Phra Bang stands with a smooth ushnisha.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is a cast monk; this is a copy of one named Buddha image.

## พระเครื่องลาว · pha khueang lao · Lao Buddha amulet (Luang Prabang and Vientiane temple issues)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/lao-phra-khrueang/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/lao-phra-khrueang.json
id: lao-phra-khrueang · level: kind
native: ພະເຄື່ອງ (lo)
aliases: พระลาว · พระล้านช้าง · พระเครื่องหลวงพระบาง · พระเครื่องเวียงจันทน์ · phra khrueang lao · phra lao · Lan Xang amulet · Lao amulet · Lan Xang-style Buddha amulet
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: la, th-isan
origin: วัดในหลวงพระบางและเวียงจันทน์ (เชียงทอง วัดใหม่ วัดองค์ตื้อ) Temples of Luang Prabang and Vientiane — Wat Xieng Thong, Wat Mai, Wat Ong Teu among the named ones · วัดลาวออกให้ อ้างอิงพระบูชาล้านช้าง Issued by Lao temples; the models are the Lan Xang altar bronzes · Lan Xang altar images from the fourteenth century (the Vat Manorom colossus is held the oldest); the worn amulet as a Lao temple product is modern, on the Thai pattern · Luang Prabang and Vientiane
what (th): พระเครื่องที่วัดลาวออก — พระพิมพ์ เหรียญ รูปหล่อเล็ก — ต้นแบบคือพระบูชาล้านช้าง เช่นพระยืนปางขอฝนและพระบาง ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): Amulets issued by Lao temples — tablets, medallions, small casts — modelled on the Lan Xang altar bronzes: the rain-calling standing Buddha, the Phra Bang, the seated earth-toucher. Nobody home, nothing owed.
story: Lao Buddhist sculpture is mostly bronze with gold and silver beside it; the great images were cast in parts and assembled, and the Lao gave the Buddha gestures of their own, calling for rain and lying down to welcome death. The named palladia — the Phra Bang, the sixteenth-century gold Phra Sai now in Nong Khai, the colossal Phra Ong Teu in Vientiane — are the models. The worn amulet as a temple product is recent and follows the Thai industry's formats; after 1975 spirit practice was pressed by the state but stayed woven into Lao Buddhism, and the amulet lives in that weave.
keeping: Impersonal: ordinary veneration, nothing fed. The provenance question is which temple issued it and when.
- look at: Lao bronze, samrit, often carries precious metal; some images run high in copper and gold and read as a muted gold colour [cited]
- look at: A standing figure with arms falling straight and the robe flaring at the hem is the Lao rain-calling type; the Walters torso records exactly that outline [cited]
- look at: Colossal Lao bronzes were cast in parts and assembled; a small piece is one pour, so a seam on a pendant is a mould line, not a Lao construction mark [cited]
- look at: Reverse script, where present, is usually Tham rather than Khom — the Lao sacred hand [inference]
- look at: Medallion and powder formats follow the Thai amulet industry; no Lazada TH listing title in catalog.db carries ลาว, หลวงพระบาง or เวียงจันทน์ [catalogue]
- vs phra-bang-pendant: A Phra Bang pendant is one Lao amulet with a named model: standing, both palms forward. Anything else Lao is this broader kind.
- vs phra-chiang-saen: Chiang Saen is the Lanna bronze; Lan Xang descends from the same line but the face and the flared robe differ, and the rain-calling stance is Lao only.
- vs rian-kechi: A Thai monk medallion names a Thai monk and temple; a Lao issue is lettered in Lao or Tham script.
- vs phra-kru: An Isan cache find such as the Na Dun naga-sheltered tablets is old and excavated; a Lao temple amulet is a recent issue. Crust versus shine.

## ผ้าประเจียด · pha prachiat · Prachiat (yantra head-cloth / armband)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/prachiat/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/prachiat.json
id: prachiat · level: kind
aliases: ประเจียด · ผ้าประเจียดแขน · มงคล (ผ้าโพกหัวนักมวย) · pra jiad · prajiad · prajead · mongkhon · mongkol · yantra armband · muay thai armband · war head-cloth
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: cloth · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: th
origin:  · แจกโดยพระเจ้าตากสิน (พ.ศ. ๒๓๑๒) และ ร.๑ (พ.ศ. ๒๓๒๘) แก่แม่ทัพนายกองและทหาร ตามวิกิพีเดีย; ครูอาจารย์ทำให้ศิษย์ th.wikipedia records prachiat given by King Taksin (B.E. 2312) to commanders and by Rama I (B.E. 2328) to soldiers; later made by teachers for pupils and by monks · Thonburi and early Bangkok periods by the cited dates; the practice is older than the record · Thailand
what (th): ผ้าลงเลขยันต์ผืนเล็กที่ม้วนพันศีรษะ คอ หรือต้นแขน เชื่อว่ากันอันตราย แจกทหารตั้งแต่สมัยกรุงธนบุรี ปัจจุบันเห็นบนแขนนักมวย ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): A small inscribed cloth rolled and tied on the head, neck or upper arm against harm — given to soldiers from the Thonburi period, seen today on boxers' arms. Power in the inscription; nobody home.
story: th.wikipedia has the cloth as a recognised protection: King Taksin gave it to his commanders in B.E. 2312, Rama I to soldiers in 2328, teachers to pupils after; small pieces were sewn into shirts, and boxers took it up for morale. en.wikipedia adds the origin story told in the gyms — a strip of a mother's sarong tied on the arm before battle — and the ring rule that the head-ring comes off after the wai khru while the armbands stay on. Ms 6983 knows the word as the generic worn charm: a carved figure held in the mouth serves 'as a prachiat', and the waking chant rouses 'the prachiat cloths and mongkhon, to endure and evade'.
keeping: Nothing to feed. Kept high and clean like a pha yan; a boxer's is the gym's to bless and hand over, and en.wikipedia says the trainer keeps the mongkhon.
- look at: A band that ties: much longer than wide, or a small square folded to a strip; a large hanging sheet is a pha yan [cited]
- look at: Black ink or pencil on white, red or yellow cloth [cited]
- look at: The boxing armband is a soft tied band, ends left as tassels; the mongkhon is a stiff hoop for the head, removed after the wai khru [cited]
- look at: Some gyms colour-code armbands for rank; that is gym custom, not consecration [cited]
- vs pha-yan: A pha yan is a sheet to hang or fold; a prachiat is a band to tie on. Same class, same keeping; the name follows the use.
- vs suea-yan: A suea yan is prachiat cloths sewn into a shirt (th.wikipedia's own definition).
- vs sai-sin: Sai sin is bare thread at the wrist with no inscription.
- vs takrut: A takrut is a rolled metal sheet; the treatise also puts a takrut on the head for the same errands, so the place on the body does not tell them apart — the material does.
