## ผ้ายันต์ · pha yan · Pha yan (yantra cloth)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/pha-yan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/pha-yan.json
id: pha-yan · level: kind
aliases: ผ้าประเจียด · ประเจียด · เสื้อยันต์ · pha yant · pha prachiat · prajiad · yantra cloth · yant cloth · prajiad armband
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: cloth · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), กันผี (warding spirits), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th
origin:  ·  · Thai Wikipedia has King Taksin handing prachiat to his commanders around 1769 and Rama I to his soldiers around 1785; both dates unverified against a primary · Country-wide
what (th): ผ้าผืนสี่เหลี่ยมหรือธงที่เขียนตาราง รูป และอักขระ แขวนเหนือประตู พับใส่กระเป๋า หรือพันตัว ลายยันต์มีดัชนีของตัวเองที่ /yant
what (en): A cloth square or banner drawn with grids, figures and script — hung over a door, folded into a pocket, or worn. The drawn designs have their own index here: /yant.
story: The treatise has no recipe for the cloth itself; it uses one. A white cloth bearing the eight-direction yantra is stretched as a ceiling while a takrut is inscribed in the ordination hall, and the great waking-katha lists the prachiat among the things it rouses to endure and evade. Thai Wikipedia describes the prachiat as a white, red or yellow cloth tied at head, neck or arm, handed to soldiers by Taksin and Rama I before battle, and still worn by Muay Thai and krabi-krabong fighters. The temple-issue cloth hung over a shop door is the same object at rest.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Hang it or carry it with unknown history; its question is only whose hand drew it.
- look at: A flat cloth. Rolled into a tube it becomes a takrut; the medium is the tell [catalogue]
- look at: White, red or yellow ground with black ink or pencil per the prachiat article; the ground colour is not a rule [cited]
- look at: Script places it: Khom in the centre, Tham in the north and northeast, Thai script in the south [cited]
- look at: Modern temple issues are screen-printed in one colour with even lines; hand-drawn cloths show uneven strokes and ink pooling [tradition]
- look at: A yantra cloth wrapping an effigy is part of that object, and takes that object's class [catalogue]
- vs takrut: Flat versus rolled. Same class, same keeping; only the form differs.
- vs hun-phayon: A hun phayon is a figure that a yantra cloth may wrap, and it is fed; the bare cloth is not. If there is a body inside the cloth, it is not this record.

## พญาครุฑ · phaya khrut · Phaya Khrut (the garuda)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phaya-khrut/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phaya-khrut.json
id: phaya-khrut · level: kind
aliases: ครุฑ · พระครุฑ · ครุฑยุดนาค · phaya krut · khrut · garuda · Garuda · king of birds · mount of Vishnu
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th
origin:  ·  · The garuda is the royal and national emblem of Thailand and an old temple and palace motif; when it became a mass-market amulet is not something this record can date · Nationwide
what (th): พญาครุฑ ราชาแห่งนก กางปีก — อำนาจ แคล้วคลาด และหนี้ที่ไม่กล้าตามมา หล่อโลหะตั้งแต่จี้จนถึงรูปตั้ง เป็นเทพที่บูชาผ่านวัตถุ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): The king of birds, wings spread — authority, safe passage, and debt that dares not follow. Cast in metal from pendant to standard.
story: The garuda is Vishnu's mount and the emblem of the Thai state, which is why the same bird sits on a passport and on a pendant. In the trade it is sold for commanding presence, for commerce that moves, and — the claim listings repeat most — for warding off black magic and curses. The vault places it with Wessuwan and Rahu: a deva venerated through the object, owed respect, not a raised ghost that eats. What the tradition calls the garuda's power is authority; the keeper borrows the bird's rank.
keeping: Deva tier: veneration, not feeding. Respect and small offerings; can be set down. Provenance sensitivity medium — ask, but no history follows it the way a spirit-object's does.
- look at: Spread wings are the first mark; a yaksha has none [catalogue]
- look at: Cast metal as a rule: solid pendant, openwork pendant, or standing figure [catalogue]
- look at: The state garuda on documents and the royal-warrant garuda over a shop door are emblems, not amulets — same bird, no consecration [tradition]
- look at: Listings state warding off black magic and curses (กันคุณไสย), authority, and commerce; one of the highest-frequency motifs in the current market [catalogue]
- vs thao-wessuwan: The garuda has wings and often a naga underfoot; Wessuwan is a wingless giant leaning on a club. Both devas, both cast metal.
- vs salika: The salika is a small natural bird, a charm of sweet speech; the garuda is a crowned man-bird of authority.
- vs phra-rahu: Rahu is a bodiless head swallowing the moon, usually carved in coconut shell; the garuda is a whole winged figure in metal.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is a cast monk in robes; a garuda is a winged deva. Cast metal both, so the figure decides.

## พญานาค · phaya nak · Naga pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phaya-nak/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phaya-nak.json
id: phaya-nak · level: kind
aliases: นาค · นาคราช · พญาศรีสุทโธนาคราช · องค์นาคา · phaya naga · nak · nakkharat · Phaya Naga · Naga king · serpent-lord amulet
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th, th-isan
origin:  · หลายวัดและสำนัก โดยเฉพาะอีสานลุ่มน้ำโขง Many wats and shrines, above all along the Mekong in Isan · The present naga cult; the cabinet named the naga a national symbol in November 2022 · Kham Chanot (Udon Thani), Nong Khai, nationwide
what (th): จี้หรือรูปหล่อพญานาค เจ้าแห่งงูและน้ำในความเชื่อไทย-ลาว ผู้เฝ้าแม่น้ำโขง เป็นเครื่องรางที่นิยมที่สุดของยุคนี้ ขอโชคลาภและเมตตา
what (en): A pendant or small cast figure of the naga, serpent-lord of water in Thai-Lao belief and keeper of the Mekong. The most fashionable deity object of the present decade, asked for luck and favour.
story: Legend has two nagas carve the Mekong and the Nan with their bodies; Isan reads the Mekong fireballs as naga breath and Kham Chanot as a naga palace. In Buddhism the naga Mucalinda shields the Buddha from rain, the source of the นาคปรก image. In 2022 the cabinet named the naga a national symbol for cultural and creative-economy ends, and the pendant trade rode the same wave.
keeping: Kept by veneration: flowers, water, fruit, respect. Not fed like a kuman, not a ghost; deva-tier keeping.
- look at: A serpent with crest and hood; without the crest it is a plain snake, and a winged bird-man is Garuda [cited]
- look at: A naga hood over a seated Buddha is นาคปรก, class phra_khrueang (the Mucalinda episode); the naga alone is this kind [cited]
- look at: Modern casts are often painted or enamelled, with the shrine's name on the base [tradition]
- look at: Four naga families in four colours per the 2022 government prototype, with Nak Vasuki as the lead form [cited]
- vs phaya-khrut: Garuda is winged and beaked, the naga's enemy; the naga is a crested serpent. Same deva-tier class.
- vs phra-kru: A cache นาคปรก is a Buddha under the hood: phra_khrueang, nobody home. This kind is the serpent alone, venerated.
- vs phra-rahu: Rahu is a bodiless giant's face swallowing the moon; the naga has a coiled body
- vs jatukham: A Jatukham is a large round disc with a seated deity, sometimes ringed by nagas; the naga here is the whole figure

## พญาเต่าเรือน · phaya tao ruean · Phaya Tao Ruean (turtle-king charm)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phaya-tao-ruean/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phaya-tao-ruean.json
id: phaya-tao-ruean · level: kind
aliases: เต่าเรือน · พญาเต่า · เต่าหลวงปู่หลิว · phaya tao ruan · paya tao ruen · tao ruean · house-turtle amulet · Luang Pu Liu turtle
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-central
origin: วัดไร่แตงทอง นครปฐม · วัดไทรทองพัฒนา กาญจนบุรี (ตามการ์ด) Wat Rai Taeng Thong, Thung Luk Nok, Kamphaeng Saen, Nakhon Pathom (Thai Wikipedia); Wat Sai Thong Phatthana, Kanchanaburi (reference card) · หลวงปู่หลิว ปุณฺณโก Luang Pu Liu Punnako; the card also traces older turtles to Luang Pho Ngoen of Wat Bang Khlan · Wat Rai Taeng Thong was founded 17 March 1992 per Thai Wikipedia; the famous turtle issues are usually placed in the late 20th century (tradition) · Nakhon Pathom and Kanchanaburi
what (th): เต่าเรือนในสายหลวงปู่หลิว — ทรัพย์ที่ค่อยมาแล้วอยู่ อายุยืน บ้านมั่นคง วัตถุมงคลปลุกเสก ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): The house-turtle amulet in the line of Luang Pu Liu — slow money that stays, long life, a household that holds. Blessed object, no resident.
story: A turtle cast in the same bronze tradition as the monk figures: its slow, armoured persistence stands for wealth that accumulates and does not stop, and one edition names itself so. The lineage the trade names is Luang Pu Liu Punnako, at Wat Sai Thong Phatthana and then Wat Rai Taeng Thong in Nakhon Pathom, founded 1992, where an 8.1-metre image of the monk seated on the turtle draws people asking for health and long life. Older turtles are traced to Luang Pho Ngoen of Wat Bang Khlan, a claim that lives in issue records, not in the metal.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its question is which issue and whether it is genuine, never spiritual safety.
- look at: An animal figure, not a Buddha: the blessed-object class, power in the rite and the monk's barami [catalogue]
- look at: The strongest lineage is Luang Pu Liu; the card traces older pieces to Luang Pho Ngoen of Wat Bang Khlan — a lineage claim read from issue records, not from the metal [catalogue]
- look at: The shell carries a yantra or the monk's likeness; run names state the function outright — one listing's edition is รวยไม่หยุด, 'rich without stopping' [catalogue]
- look at: Cast metal dates by patina, earth body by shrinkage; the same turtle in two materials reads two ways [catalogue]
- look at: The temple's landmark image is Luang Pu Liu seated on the turtle, 8.1 m tall; visitors come for health and long life, which is the turtle's meaning [cited]
- vs rian-kechi: A struck Luang Pu Liu medallion in turtle outline is a monk medallion wearing a turtle; the cast turtle is the animal itself. Same monk, same class, different form.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is the monk cast in the round; the turtle is his animal. Both cast, both his issues.
- vs pla-taphian: The carp is woven or sheet metal, hung for trade; the turtle is cast and worn. Both animal wealth charms, different beasts and bodies.

## พระเชียงแสน · phra chiang saen · Chiang Saen (Lanna) bronze Buddha
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-chiang-saen/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-chiang-saen.json
id: phra-chiang-saen · level: kind
aliases: พระสิงห์ · เชียงแสนสิงห์หนึ่ง · เชียงแสนสิงห์สอง · พระพุทธรูปศิลปะล้านนา · phra singh · chiang saen sing nueng · chiangsaen · Chiengsen Buddha · Lanna Buddha image · Singha-style Buddha
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองแดง (copper) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-north
origin:  · ช่างหล่อล้านนา ไม่ระบุ Lanna bronze casters, unnamed · Lanna art, roughly the 13th to 18th centuries CE (Buddhist centuries 19–24) · Chiang Saen, Chiang Mai and the Lanna towns; the name comes from the art centre before Mangrai moved to Chiang Mai
what (th): พระพุทธรูปสำริดแบบล้านนาที่วงการเรียกรวมว่าพระเชียงแสน แบ่งเป็นสิงห์หนึ่ง สิงห์สอง สิงห์สาม ตามหน้า เกตุ และชายจีวร มีทั้งองค์บูชาและองค์จ้อยห้อยคอ
what (en): Lanna bronze Buddhas the trade groups as พระเชียงแสน, sorted into Sing 1, 2 and 3 by face, ushnisha and robe flap; from altar images down to wearable 'ong choi' pieces.
story: Lanna art centred on Chiang Saen before Mangrai moved to Chiang Mai, and the name stayed on the bronzes. Sing 1 has a round face, lotus-bud ushnisha and both soles up; Sing 2 takes Sukhothai's flame ushnisha and long robe flap; Sing 3 is the late style. 'Sing' refers to the Phra Sihing image whose Chiang Mai copy sits at Wat Phra Singh. Small casts and cache pieces enter the amulet trade under the same name.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. The provenance question is age, authenticity and price.
- look at: Seat: both soles showing (vajrasana) reads Sing 1; legs folded flat reads Sing 2 [cited]
- look at: Ushnisha: lotus bud for Sing 1, flame for Sing 2 and 3 [cited]
- look at: Robe flap: short above the nipple for Sing 1, down to the navel for Sing 2 [cited]
- look at: Bronze bodies the trade names gold-rich, nak-toned and black; patina and pitting are the age signal on cast metal [tradition]
- look at: The word 'Sing' in the style names points to the Phra Sihing image and its Chiang Mai copy, not to a lion on the piece [cited]
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is a cast monk portrait; a Chiang Saen is a cast Buddha. Both phra_khrueang.
- vs phra-kring: A phra kring is a small Buddha with a rattle inside in a Sino-Tibetan manner; a Chiang Saen is Lanna style, no rattle
- vs phra-kru: Most cache finds are pressed earth or chin tablets; a cache Chiang Saen is a cast bronze figure
- vs phra-khong: A พระคง is a Lamphun fired-earth tablet; a Chiang Saen is cast bronze. Both Lanna, both nobody-home.

## พระหูยาน · phra hu yan · Phra Hu Yan (Lopburi long-eared tablet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-hu-yan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-hu-yan.json
id: phra-hu-yan · level: kind
aliases: หูยาน · พระหูยานลพบุรี · phra huyan · phra hoo yarn · hu yan lopburi · long-eared Buddha tablet
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อชิน (tin-lead alloy), สนิมแดง (red rust patina), เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-central
origin: วัดพระศรีรัตนมหาธาตุ ลพบุรี (ปฐมกรุ) Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, Lopburi, the primary cache; also found at sites in Phetchaburi, Sukhothai, Chainat, Ayutthaya, Sing Buri and Uttaradit ·  · Late Lopburi period per Thai Wikipedia; the cache first opened about B.E. 2450 (the 'old cache') and again about B.E. 2508 (the 'new cache') · Lopburi
what (th): พระพิมพ์ศิลปะลพบุรีจากกรุวัดพระศรีรัตนมหาธาตุ ลพบุรี องค์พระนั่งสมาธิราบ พระกรรณยาวจรดบ่า จึงได้ชื่อ เนื้อชินเป็นหลัก เชื่อกันเรื่องคงกระพัน ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่
what (en): A Lopburi-style tablet from the cache at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, Lopburi: a Buddha seated flat in meditation whose ears run down to the shoulders, which is the name. Mostly chin alloy. Held for invulnerability. Nobody is home.
story: Thai Wikipedia places it in the Mahayana and Mantrayana current of the late Lopburi period, with the primary cache at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat. The cache opened first around B.E. 2450 and again around B.E. 2508, so the trade speaks of an old cache and a new one, and examples surfaced in several other provinces. The attributed powers are invulnerability and loving-kindness.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is age and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Ears reaching the shoulders: the defining mark [cited]
- look at: Hair curls in straight rows with a single-tier ushnisha [cited]
- look at: A grooved reverse on many pieces [cited]
- look at: Old-cache and new-cache pieces are separated by surface and crust, per the trade [cited]
- look at: Chin bodies date by patina, sorted as silvery, lead-heavy or red-rust; the patina is a surface state, not a verdict [catalogue]
- vs phra-kru: Hu Yan is one named cache-find; phra kru is the category. The long ears and the Lopburi style name this one.
- vs phra-nang-phaya: Nang Phaya is a fired-clay triangle of the Ayutthaya period; Hu Yan is a tall tablet, usually chin alloy, in Lopburi style. Same class, different material axis.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is a cast figure in the round; Hu Yan is a pressed or cast tablet with a back.
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:th-wiki-phra-khrueang — พระเครื่อง — วิกิพีเดีย; s:en-wiki-thai-amulet — Thai Buddha amulet — Wikipedia; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited; s:th-wiki-hu-yan — พระหูยาน — วิกิพีเดีย

## พระคะแนน · phra khanaen · Phra Khanaen (counting piece)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-khanaen/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-khanaen.json
id: phra-khanaen · level: kind
aliases: คะแนน · องค์คะแนน · phra kanaen · phra khanan · tally amulet · counter piece
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body), เนื้อชิน (tin-lead alloy), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: — · region: th
origin:  ·  · A counting convention used both in old caches and in later temple runs; Thai Wikipedia notes the practice is no longer widespread · 
what (th): พระเครื่ององค์เล็กที่สร้างไว้ใช้นับจำนวนพระในชุดเดียวกัน หนึ่งองค์แทนพระหลักจำนวนหนึ่ง ทำให้เล็กกว่าเพื่อแยกออกได้ชัด ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่
what (en): A small amulet made to tally a batch: one counting piece stands for a fixed number of main pieces, and it is made smaller so the two never mix. Nobody is home.
story: The Royal Institute Dictionary of B.E. 2542, as quoted by Thai Wikipedia, defines it as a small amulet used to fix the count of amulets made, one per hundred in the example. Because a batch yields far fewer counters than main pieces the trade prizes them, and because modern runs are counted by other means the practice has thinned out.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is which batch it counted and whether the size relation holds, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Visibly undersized against the main pieces of its batch; that difference is the whole definition [cited]
- look at: One piece stands for a fixed count of main pieces, a hundred in the dictionary example [cited]
- look at: Body and mould follow the batch; the category has no material of its own [tradition]
- look at: The trade prices them above the main pieces because there are fewer; a statement about the category, never about an object [tradition]
- vs phra-kru: Phra kru is anything recovered from a cache; a khanaen is an undersized counting piece, which may come from a cache or a modern run. Role and size, not crust.
- vs phra-somdet: A small somdej is not automatically a khanaen; it is one only if it stands in a counting relation to a batch. Same class, same material, different role.
- vs phra-pidta: Tiny Pidta are a mould type in their own right, not counters; a khanaen mirrors its batch's main mould.
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:th-wiki-phra-khrueang — พระเครื่อง — วิกิพีเดีย; s:en-wiki-thai-amulet — Thai Buddha amulet — Wikipedia; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited; s:th-wiki-khanaen — พระคะแนน — วิกิพีเดีย
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## พระคง · phra khong · Phra Khong (Lamphun cache tablet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-khong/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-khong.json
id: phra-khong · level: kind
aliases: พระคงลำพูน · พระคง กรุวัดพระคงฤๅษี · phra kong · phra khong lamphun · Phra Kong amulet
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th-north
origin: วัดพระคงฤๅษี Wat Phra Khong Ruesi, Mueang Lamphun · ตำนานยกให้ฤๅษีสมัยพระนางจามเทวี Legend assigns the tablets to the hermits (ฤๅษี) of Queen Chamadevi's Hariphunchai; no maker is named · Hariphunchai period; the wat's founding legend gives B.E. 1200, which is legend, not a date for the tablets · Lamphun
what (th): พระพิมพ์ดินเผาหริภุญชัยจากกรุวัดพระคงฤๅษี ลำพูน คู่แฝดของพระรอด องค์พระนั่งใต้ซุ้มใบโพธิ์ ชื่อ “คง” ทำให้คนถือเป็นพระคงกระพัน
what (en): A Hariphunchai fired-earth tablet from the cache at Wat Phra Khong Ruesi in Lamphun, the stockier twin of the พระรอด: a seated Buddha under bodhi leaves. The name คง (endure) is why the trade reads it as a คงกระพัน amulet.
story: The wat's legend has Queen Chamadevi build it where the hermit Vasudeva sketched the city plan with his staff, with hermit figures at the four gates. Its stupas held fired-earth tablets in black and red, and a restoration that opened the chedis turned up พระคง and พระบาง in quantity. The trade groups it with the other Lamphun cache finds and prices it well below the พระรอด.
keeping: Nobody home and nothing owed. The provenance question is authenticity and price, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Fired-earth body in black or red, Haripunchai-style; a metal or powder body is another kind [cited]
- look at: Cache-found in the wat's chedis together with พระบาง; the two share a body and are separated by mould [cited]
- look at: Stockier than a พระรอด, the bodhi leaves forming a canopy round the figure; the trade reads the leaf pattern first [tradition]
- look at: Age reads as cache crust and edge wear, never rust: the fired-earth dating signal on the material axis [catalogue]
- vs phra-rot: Same class, same fired-earth body, same city. A พระรอด is smaller and finer, from the Wat Mahawan cache; a พระคง is stockier, from the Wat Phra Khong Ruesi cache. Mould, not material, tells them apart.
- vs phra-kru: พระกรุ is the umbrella for any cache find; พระคง is one named member of it
- vs phra-sum-ko: A พระซุ้มกอ is fired earth from Kamphaeng Phet with a kanok-scroll arch; the พระคง arch is bodhi leaves
- vs phra-nang-phaya: A พระนางพญา is a Phitsanulok fired-earth triangle with no canopy at all
sources: s:th-wiki-wat-phra-khong-ruesi — วัดพระคงฤๅษี — วิกิพีเดีย; s:th-wiki-phra-khrueang — พระเครื่อง — วิกิพีเดีย; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## พระเครื่องเขมร · phra khrueang khmer · Khmer bronze amulet (Angkorian and post-Angkorian figurines)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/khmer-bronze-amulet/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/khmer-bronze-amulet.json
id: khmer-bronze-amulet · level: kind
native: ព្រះពុទ្ធរូប (km)
aliases: พระขอม · พระเขมรโบราณ · พระนาคปรกขอม · พระบูชาขอม · phra khom · Angkorian bronze · Lopburi-style bronze · Khmer bronze Buddha · Angkor bronze pendant · Khmer bronze figurine · Bayon-style bronze
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: kh, th-isan, th-central
origin:  · ช่างหล่อขอม (หล่อแบบสูญขี้ผึ้งแปดขั้น) และช่างรุ่นหลัง Khmer founders using the eight-step lost-wax method in use since at least the sixth century; modern casters in the same style · Hindu and Buddhist bronzes from the seventh century; Angkor period ninth to thirteenth; post-Angkor Theravada commissions of ancestors and Buddhist figures as merit · Cambodia and the Khmer-influenced Thai provinces — Lopburi, Phimai, and the 1964 Prakhon Chai find in Buriram
what (th): รูปหล่อสำริดขนาดเล็กศิลปะขอม — นาคปรก พระทรงเครื่อง หรือเทวรูป — ที่นำมาห้อยคอหรือบูชา ของแท้ยุคพระนครเป็นโบราณวัตถุที่มีปัญหากฎหมาย ของในตลาดส่วนมากหล่อใหม่
what (en): A small Khmer-style bronze — naga-enthroned Buddha, crowned Buddha, or deity — worn as an amulet or kept on the altar. Genuine Angkorian pieces are antiquities with a legal problem attached; most of what circulates is modern casting in the style.
story: Bronze was a noble material to the Khmer, tied to prosperity, and cast by lost wax since at least the sixth century. Angkor favoured the naga-sheltered Buddha, Lokeshvara and Prajnaparamita; Jayavarman VII sent twenty-three Avalokiteshvara images across the kingdom in 1191 and took the naga-enthroned Buddha as the form under which he would be honoured — the Cleveland bronze from Banteay Chhmar is that image. When Theravada prevailed after the thirteenth century, believers commissioned small metal figures for the home and as offerings to temples, and those home-size pieces are the ancestors of the worn amulet. In the twentieth century the same bronzes were looted and sold at scale, which is why an old one now carries a question that a consecration cannot answer.
keeping: Buddha figures: nobody home, ordinary veneration. Deity figures fall to the deva class — venerated, never fed. For any piece claimed as old, the keeper owes a paper trail before a prayer.
- look at: Lost-wax solid casting with fine detail at every size — the Khmer method since at least the sixth century, still demonstrated by Cambodian artisans today [cited]
- look at: Mucalinda marks: coils (canonically seven) and a spread cobra hood, usually seven heads [cited]
- look at: Post-Angkor believers commissioned metal figures of ancestors and Theravada divinities as merit; mid-size bronzes served rites and processions, small ones were kept at home — the home-size piece is the ancestor of the worn amulet [cited]
- look at: Angkorian bronzes were trafficked at scale from the 1970s (the Latchford case names bronzes and bells; museums returned pieces 2021–2026); for any old piece the provenance question is legal before it is spiritual [cited]
- look at: The 1964 Prakhon Chai find in Buriram — pre-Angkor bronzes including Avalokitesvara — is the Khmer-world parallel to a Thai cache find [cited]
- look at: Most of what the Thai trade calls phra khom is modern casting in Lopburi style, the trade holds; catalog.db has no Lazada TH title with ขอม or เขมร at all [catalogue]
- vs phra-kru: A phra kru is a flat pressed tablet of clay or chin from a sealed cache; this is a bronze in the round. The Prakhon Chai hoard shows bronzes can be cache finds too, so ask form first, findspot second.
- vs rup-lo: A Thai rup lo is a cast portrait of a named monk; the Khmer bronze is a Buddha or deity in Angkorian style. Same material, different figure.
- vs phra-hu-yan: Phra Hu Yan of Lopburi is Khmer-style too, but a flat chin tablet from a cache, not a figure in the round.
- vs phra-chiang-saen: Chiang Saen bronzes are Lanna: round face, lotus-bud finial. Khmer pieces show the naga throne, the crown and diadem, and the squarer Bayon face.

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/15fa79c449952f92d308ff5db75f9d8e1d22dda494353d134f3d4ae6dff06fa0.jpg · Public domain · Anonymous (Cambodia or Thailand)Unknown author · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=18763496

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/fa6a8c45df9c5fced0e6a1cc034da427da01a4fe791578d4e8c980760e75ab1b.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Siren-Com · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=76233715

## พระกริ่ง · phra kring · Phra Kring (rattling cast Buddha)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-kring/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-kring.json
id: phra-kring · level: kind
aliases: กริ่ง · พระกริ่งปวเรศ · พระกริ่งวัดสุทัศน์ · phra kring · phra gring · kring · Medicine Buddha amulet · ringing Buddha
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: นวโลหะ (nine-metal alloy), สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th-central, th
origin: วัดบวรนิเวศวิหาร · วัดสุทัศนเทพวราราม Wat Bowonniwet (Phra Kring Pawaret line) and Wat Suthat (Somdet Phra Sangkharat Pae line), Bangkok · สมเด็จพระมหาสมณเจ้า กรมพระยาปวเรศวริยาลงกรณ์ · สมเด็จพระสังฆราช (แพ ติสฺสเทโว) Somdet Phra Maha Samana Chao Krom Phraya Pawaret Wariyalongkon (Wat Bowon); Somdet Phra Sangkharat Pae Tissadevo (Wat Suthat) · Tibetan, Chinese and Khmer forms precede it; Thai evidence from Sukhothai–Ayutthaya, the collected lineages are Rattanakosin · Bangkok
what (th): พระพุทธรูปหล่อโลหะขนาดเล็ก ภายในกลวงบรรจุเม็ดกริ่ง เขย่าแล้วดัง สืบสายมาจากพระไภษัชยคุรุแบบจีน–ทิเบต หล่อด้วยนวโลหะหรือสัมฤทธิ์ พลังอยู่ที่ผู้สร้างและพิธี ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A small cast Buddha with a pellet sealed inside — shake it and it chimes. Cast in bronze or nawaloha in the Chinese-Tibetan medicine-Buddha line.
story: The model is the Medicine Buddha of Tibet and China, reaching Siam by way of Khmer castings; Thai evidence runs from Sukhothai onward. The lineages the trade collects are Rattanakosin: Wat Bowon's Phra Kring Pawaret and Wat Suthat's castings under Somdet Phra Sangkharat Pae, with a Phitsanulok Wat Wang Chan group (the Naresuan series) alongside. Nawaloha is a nine-metal alloy — gold, silver, copper, bronze, tin, zinc, lead, mercury and pewter are the ones named. The trade holds that the chime is used when blessing water and links the kind to healing and vitality, which is the Bhaisajyaguru dedication carried into Thai practice.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; a phra khrueang. Its only provenance question is authenticity and price.
- look at: Shaken, it chimes: the body is hollow with a pellet, and the base is plugged. A silent piece is some other kind of cast Buddha [cited]
- look at: Inverted-lotus base, right hand touching earth, left holding a pot or fruit [cited]
- look at: Cast in nawaloha or bronze, never struck; look for casting texture and the dark patina the trade calls กลับดำ on aged nawaloha [tradition]
- look at: Wat Suthat and Wat Bowon lineage pieces usually carry a code or Khom letters under the base; a type mark, not a proof of anything [tradition]
- vs rup-lo: A phra kring is a Buddha (ushnisha, lotus base, pellet inside); a rup lo is a cast monk, bald, in robes, and normally silent. Same class and material, different figure
- vs phra-pidta: A pidta covers its face with its hands; a kring's hands are in the earth-touching pose with a pot. Both can be cast metal, so read the hands
- vs phra-somdet: A somdej is a pressed powder tablet with the figure in relief; a kring is a free-standing metal casting

## พระกรุ · phra kru · Phra Kru (cache-find amulet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-kru/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-kru.json
id: phra-kru · level: kind
aliases: กรุเก่า · พระกรุเก่า · พระพิมพ์กรุ · phra kroo · kru amulet · stupa-deposit amulet · votive tablet from a cache
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body), เนื้อชิน (tin-lead alloy), สนิมแดง (red rust patina), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th
origin:  ·  · The practice of sealing votive tablets in a stupa's chamber to carry the religion forward, per Thai Wikipedia; the tablets surface when the structure fails or is opened · Throughout Thailand
what (th): พระพิมพ์ที่ได้จากกรุเจดีย์ที่ปิดไว้ — ดินเผาหรือชินมากกว่าผง มีคราบและแร่บานจากหลายร้อยปีในกรุ อายุคือคำถามทั้งหมด ผิวคือพยาน ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่
what (en): An amulet recovered from a sealed temple cache (กรุ) — fired earth or chin alloy more often than powder, with the crust and mineral bloom of centuries in the chamber. Age is the whole question; the surface is the testimony.
story: Thai Wikipedia records the custom of sealing valuables and large numbers of votive tablets in a stupa's chamber so that the religion would outlast the building. When the structure fails or is opened the tablets come out, which the trade calls a cache breaking (กรุแตก). Four of the Benjaphakhi five are cache-finds; the term พระเครื่อง itself, per the same article, only arrives in the reign of Rama IV and folds these older พระพิมพ์ into it.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is age and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Cache crust: earth, sediment and mineral bloom on the surface, the category's shared mark [catalogue]
- look at: Chin bodies read by patina (silvery, lead-heavy, red-rust); clay bodies read by shrinkage. Powder is the exception, not the rule, in a cache [catalogue]
- look at: Red rust is a surface state recorded as such, never a verdict on age [catalogue]
- look at: Shape names the kind and cache; surface testifies to time. Ask both questions separately [catalogue]
- look at: Heavily reproduced as a category; crust can be applied. A statement about the category, never about an object [catalogue]
- vs phra-rot: Phra Rod is one named member of this category: bodhi-leaf ring, Lamphun. Say the name when you can; say phra kru when you cannot.
- vs phra-hu-yan: Hu Yan is a named chin-alloy member: ears to the shoulders, Lopburi.
- vs phra-khanaen: A phra khanaen is an undersized counting piece; it may come from a cache or from a modern temple run, so size and purpose name it, not the crust.
- vs phra-somdet: A somdej is Rattanakosin pressed powder made to give out; a phra kru is earth or chin sealed in a stupa and recovered. Some somdej were later deposited (the trade calls those กรุ too), which is why the material is the first gate.

## พระนางพญา · phra nang phaya · Phra Nang Phaya (Phitsanulok triangular tablet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-nang-phaya/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-nang-phaya.json
id: phra-nang-phaya · level: kind
aliases: นางพญา · พระนางพญาพิษณุโลก · ราชินีแห่งพระเครื่อง · nang phaya · phra nang phya · nangphaya · Queen of Amulets
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-central
origin: วัดนางพญา พิษณุโลก Wat Nang Phaya, Phitsanulok · ผูกกับรัชสมัยสมเด็จพระนเรศวร (วิกิพีเดียไทย) หรือพระวิสุทธิกษัตรีย์ (วิกิพีเดียอังกฤษ) Thai Wikipedia ties the making to King Naresuan's era; English Wikipedia credits Queen Wisutkasat. Treat the attribution as tradition. · Ayutthaya period; the cache first opened around 1901 (B.E. 2444), with later finds in B.E. 2512, 2530 and 2553 per Thai Wikipedia · Phitsanulok
what (th): พระพิมพ์ดินเผาทรงสามเหลี่ยมจากกรุวัดนางพญา พิษณุโลก ปางมารวิชัย อกนูน แขนเรียว วงการเรียกราชินีแห่งพระเครื่อง เป็นหนึ่งในเบญจภาคี ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่
what (en): A triangular fired-clay tablet from the cache at Wat Nang Phaya, Phitsanulok: a Maravijaya Buddha with a full chest and slender arms, the queen of amulets and one of the Benjaphakhi five. Nobody is home.
story: Thai Wikipedia places the making in the Ayutthaya period, as morale for soldiers as much as merit, and dates the first opening of the cache to about 1901, when tens of thousands of tablets came out; further finds followed in 1969, 1987 and 2010. The body is coarse clay with mineral grit, herbs and flower pollen mixed in. The chest and arms earned it the queen's title, and Triyampavai's five of around 1947 fixed it there.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is age and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Principal moulds per Thai Wikipedia: Phim Yai (large chest), Khao Khong (curved knee), Khao Trong (straight knee, plain or hand-on-knee), Sangkhati (small) [cited]
- look at: The coarsest body of the five: mineral grit and coloured inclusions visible to the eye [cited]
- look at: Surface colour ranges from brick red through yellow to black and green; it follows kiln and cache, not mould [cited]
- look at: Reverse usually shows finger impressions and cache sediment (ไคลขี้กรุ) [cited]
- look at: Age reads as shrinkage and crust, never patina: the clay axis's dating signal [catalogue]
- vs phra-phong-suphan: Both are triangular fired-clay Maravijaya tablets. Phong Suphan has a finer body and comes from Suphan Buri; Nang Phaya is coarse and from Phitsanulok. Same class, nobody home in either.
- vs phra-rot: Phra Rod is tall and rounded, in meditation with bodhi leaves; Nang Phaya is a triangle in Maravijaya.
- vs phra-kru: Nang Phaya is one named cache-find; phra kru is the category. The triangle, the coarse body and the Phitsanulok cache name this one.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/2aa6655d66c82e150e70be286cb066b21ba8c614773d26f27a8fc915d58e0dfb.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Chainwit. · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=115850407
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/37d56a6ad13fc672512bdc311f05baf0cfcc860703a74fcadffef7e7210e486e.png · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Somdej.watrakang · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=102451956
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/ba6ab231dcb9f68b7436961e57c9d1b46ebc87e6a6fd0568a53df2ab820a2850.png · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Somdej.watrakang · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=102452146

## พระพิฆเนศ · phra phikkhanet · Ganesha pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-phikkhanet/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-phikkhanet.json
id: phra-phikkhanet · level: kind
aliases: พระพิฆเนศวร · พระคเณศ · องค์พิฆเนศ · phra phikanet · phra pikanet · phra kanet · Ganesh amulet · Phra Pikanet
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th
origin:  · หลายวัดและสำนัก Issued by many wats and shrines; no single maker · Modern popularity follows the Fine Arts Department and Silpakorn University adopting Ganesha as emblem, itself inherited from King Vajiravudh's literary society · Nationwide; major Bangkok shrines at Ratchaprasong (CentralWorld) and Huai Khwang
what (th): จี้หรือรูปหล่อพระพิฆเนศ เทพเศียรช้างผู้ขจัดอุปสรรค เจ้าแห่งศิลปวิทยา บูชากันในไทยทั้งในกรอบพุทธและพราหมณ์
what (en): A pendant or small cast image of Ganesha, the elephant-headed remover of obstacles and patron of the arts, venerated in Thailand inside Buddhist practice as much as Hindu.
story: Thailand's Ganesha is the god of the arts because King Vajiravudh built a Ganesha shrine at Sanam Chan Palace and made him the emblem of his literary society; the Fine Arts Department inherited the seal and Silpakorn University uses it still. Big city shrines at Ratchaprasong and Huai Khwang made him the everyday god of artists, traders and students, and the pendant trade followed the shrines.
keeping: Kept by veneration: flowers, fruit, sweets and respect. Not fed like a kuman and not a ghost; the cleanest resident class.
- look at: Elephant head, one tusk, four arms; the hands usually hold a sweet, a noose, an elephant goad and the broken tusk [cited]
- look at: A mouse at the base marks the vehicle; its absence is common on small pendants [cited]
- look at: Cast figures show file marks under the base; medallions show a struck edge — the material axis is the first gate [tradition]
- look at: Thai renderings follow the Hindu standard; there is no distinct Thai type the eye can separate, so the run and wat on the reverse carry the identity [tradition]
- vs phra-phrom: Both are deva-tier pendants kept by veneration. Brahma has four human faces; Ganesha has an elephant head. Different god, same class.
- vs thao-wessuwan: Wessuwan is a club-bearing giant; Ganesha is the elephant-headed god. Same class, different figure
- vs phaya-khrut: Garuda is a winged bird-man, usually shown wings out; Ganesha sits with an elephant's head

## พระผงใบลาน · phra phong bai lan · Palm-leaf-ash tablet
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-phong-bai-lan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-phong-bai-lan.json
id: phra-phong-bai-lan · level: kind
aliases: ผงใบลาน · เนื้อผงใบลาน · ใบลานเผา · phong bai lan · pong bai lan · nuea phong bai lan · burnt-manuscript-ash amulet · scripture-ash amulet
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: ผงใบลาน (burnt palm-leaf manuscript ash), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) ให้สูตรใบลานเผาผสมขี้รัก Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, gives the palm-leaf-ash-and-lac formula; tablets are issued by many temples · Undated treatise; the tablet form is a temple issue of many eras · 
what (th): พระพิมพ์อัดจากเถ้าใบลานเผา — ใบลานชุดเดียวกับที่คลังนี้จัดหมวดเป็นคัมภีร์ ในช่วงชีวิตถัดไป ตำราให้สูตรตรง: ลงคาถาใบลาน ๕ ใบ เผาเป็นสมุก ผสมขี้รัก ปั้น
what (en): Pressed from the ash of burnt palm-leaf manuscripts — the same leaves this archive catalogues, at a later moment of their life. A treatise here gives the recipe outright: inscribe five leaves with katha, burn, mix with lacquer, roll.
story: Manuscript 6983 (p. 97) gives the material its recipe, for favour before nobles, commanders, monks and brahmins: inscribe five palm leaves, one stanza per leaf, burn them to a black ash, mix with lac scrapings and roll into five prayer-beads; inscribe one syllable of Namo Phutthaya on each and empower it 108 times; tie the beads at the waist when going before a lord. That is a bead recipe, not a tablet, but the paste is the same paste. The vault's material axis calls phong bai lan the seam between the two corpora made literal — scripture consumed and re-embodied as an object of veneration. The tablet form is a temple issue; which temples, and when, this record cannot name.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; the provenance question is authenticity, and, if a listing names the manuscript, whether that claim holds.
- look at: Black to dark-grey body, never the white-to-cream of phong phutthakhun [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise burns inscribed palm leaves to a black ash and binds it with lac scrapings, so the body reads matte-dark with a slight resinous sheen [catalogue]
- look at: Age reads as a surface crust, never rust: the powder family's dating signal [catalogue]
- look at: Under a loupe the trade expects fine charred leaf flecks in the paste [tradition]
- look at: A listing that names which manuscript or temple the leaves came from is making a separate provenance claim, worth recording on its own [catalogue]
- vs phra-somdet: A somdet body is white to cream; a palm-leaf-ash body is black-grey. Same class, same keeping, different material
- vs phra-pidta: A pidta is often a dark lacquer-mixed powder too, but the figure covers its eyes; a bai lan tablet shows an ordinary Buddha and the dark comes from ash, not lacquer alone
- vs khun-phaen: Some khun phaen are dark from other material rather than ash; the colour is shared, the provenance question is not — ask what made it black
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## พระผงสุพรรณ · phra phong suphan · Phra Phong Suphan (Suphan Buri triangular tablet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-phong-suphan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-phong-suphan.json
id: phra-phong-suphan · level: kind
aliases: ผงสุพรรณ · พระผงสุพรรณบุรี · phra pong suphan · pong suphan · phong suphan · Phra Pong Suphan
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-central
origin: วัดพระศรีรัตนมหาธาตุ สุพรรณบุรี Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, Suphan Buri · ลานทองจารึกกล่าวถึงฤๅษีผู้สร้าง (ตามที่วงการเล่า) An inscribed gold plate from the prang is said to credit hermits with the making; the plate's text is not cited here · U Thong period; the prang was opened in 1913 (B.E. 2456) and yielded a gold plate inscribed in Pali in Khom script, per Thai Wikipedia · Suphan Buri
what (th): พระพิมพ์ดินเผาทรงสามเหลี่ยมจากกรุพระปรางค์วัดพระศรีรัตนมหาธาตุ สุพรรณบุรี ปางมารวิชัยศิลปะอู่ทอง ชื่อว่าผงแต่เป็นดินเผา หนึ่งในเบญจภาคี ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่
what (en): A triangular fired-clay tablet from the prang cache at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, Suphan Buri: a Maravijaya Buddha with a U Thong face. Called powder, made of earth. One of the Benjaphakhi five; nobody is home.
story: In 1913 the prang at Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat was opened and a gold plate inscribed in Pali in Khom script came out with the tablets; the trade holds that the inscription names hermits as makers and promises protection, but that text is not cited here. Thai Wikipedia dates the tablets to the U Thong period. Triyampavai's set of around 1947 placed it among the five.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is age and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Called phong but fired earth: the name is a trap the material axis names outright [catalogue]
- look at: Triangular field, Maravijaya, U Thong facial style [tradition]
- look at: Finer body than Nang Phaya; colour varies with the firing [tradition]
- look at: Age reads as shrinkage and cache crust, never patina [catalogue]
- look at: Reverse usually carries a finger impression from pressing [tradition]
- vs phra-nang-phaya: Both are triangular fired-clay Maravijaya tablets. Nang Phaya is coarse and from Phitsanulok; Phong Suphan is finer, U Thong-faced, from Suphan Buri.
- vs phra-somdet: A somdej is real white powder in a rectangle with an arch; Phong Suphan is fired clay in a triangle despite its name.
- vs phra-phong-bai-lan: Palm-leaf-ash tablets are black-grey pressed powder; Phong Suphan is fired earth. Only the word ผง links them.

- image: https://wichaa.net/img/ba6ab231dcb9f68b7436961e57c9d1b46ebc87e6a6fd0568a53df2ab820a2850.png · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Somdej.watrakang · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=102452146

## พระพรหม · phra phrom · Four-faced Brahma pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-phrom/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-phrom.json
id: phra-phrom · level: kind
aliases: ท้าวมหาพรหม · พรหมสี่หน้า · พระพรหมเอราวัณ · thao maha phrom · phra prom · phrom si na · Phra Phrom · Erawan Brahma · Four-Face Buddha (Chinese-market misnomer)
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th
origin:  · รูปต้นแบบ: กรมศิลปากร (ช่างปั้น จิตร พิมพ์โกวิท) สร้างให้ศาลท้าวมหาพรหม โรงแรมเอราวัณ พ.ศ. 2499 The template image was made by the Fine Arts Department (sculptor Chit Phimkowit) for the Erawan Hotel shrine, installed 9 November 1956; pendants are issued by many wats · Shrine founded 1956 after construction troubles at the hotel; nationwide popularity follows it · Ratchaprasong intersection, Bangkok
what (th): จี้หรือรูปหล่อพระพรหมสี่หน้า เทพผู้ลิขิตชะตาและประทานพร รูปแบบที่ทั้งประเทศทำตามคือองค์ท้าวมหาพรหมที่ศาลโรงแรมเอราวัณ
what (en): A pendant or small cast image of four-faced Brahma, the god Thais credit with writing destiny and granting wishes. The template nearly every pendant copies is the Erawan Hotel shrine image at Ratchaprasong.
story: The Erawan Hotel's construction went badly until an astrologer-admiral advised a Brahma shrine; the Fine Arts Department made a gilded plaster image, installed 9 November 1956. A man smashed it with a hammer in 2006 and a replacement went in that May; a bomb killed twenty at the shrine in August 2015 and it reopened in two days. Worshippers pay vows with hired dancers and wooden elephants, and the pendant trade copies that seated four-faced form.
keeping: Kept by veneration: flowers, incense, a vow kept. Not fed, not a ghost; offerings and respect are the whole relationship.
- look at: Four faces and eight arms; a single-faced seated deity is another god [cited]
- look at: Erawan-pattern: seated, tall pointed crown — the shape most pendants copy [cited]
- look at: The word พระพรหม also begins many monastic titles (พระพรหมมุนี, พระพรหมวชิร…); a listing with a monk's name after it is a monk medallion, not Brahma [inference]
- look at: Sold to Chinese-speaking buyers as 'Four-Face Buddha'; the object is Brahma regardless of the label [tradition]
- vs phra-phikkhanet: Ganesha has an elephant head; Brahma has four human faces. Same class, same keeping.
- vs thao-wessuwan: Wessuwan is a standing giant with a club; Brahma sits with four faces
- vs phra-kring: A phra kring is a small Buddha with a rattle inside, one face, class phra_khrueang — nobody home

## พระปิดตา · phra pidta · Phra Pidta (eyes-covered Buddha)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-pidta/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-pidta.json
id: phra-pidta · level: kind
aliases: ปิดตา · พระภควัม · พระภควัมบดี · ปิดทวารทั้งเก้า · พระปิดตามหาอุตม์ · phra pid ta · pidta · phakawam · phra pakawam · closed-eyes Buddha · Phra Pakawam
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ตะกั่ว (lead) · functions: กำบัง (concealment, going unseen), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), มหาอุด (stopping projectiles / misfire), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ตำราสร้างพระภควัมบดี ๙ แบบ) · สำนักที่วงการยกให้ เช่น หลวงพ่อแก้ว วัดเครือวัลย์ The amulet-making treatise gives nine Phakawambodi recipes; the trade's named lineages include Luang Pho Kaeo of Wat Khruea Wan (Chachoengsao) and Luang Pho To of Wat Thong, early Rattanakosin · Early pieces cast metal, later ones pressed powder · Central Thai tradition
what (th): รูปนั่งยกมือปิดตาหรือปิดหน้า — ปิดทวารไม่ให้กิเลสและอันตรายเข้า ถือกันว่าเป็นพระสังกัจจายน์ เนื้อผงคลุกรักหรือโลหะหล่อ ใช้ทางกำบัง คงกระพัน และโชคลาภที่มาเงียบๆ
what (en): A figure with hands over its eyes — the shut-away senses. Pressed powder or cast metal; worked for warding and for wealth that slips past notice.
story: The treatise calls it Phra Phakawambodi and gives nine recipes. The figure is carved from a solid pig's tusk, from the root of the rak-son vine on the east side, from mistletoe of a Bodhi or chumsaeng tree, or from a material not reproduced here, one finger-joint tall; the base is hollowed, a yantra and ground 'sleeping-leaf' medicine go in, stingless-bee resin seals it, and the piece is lacquered and gilded. One version wraps three figures — eyes, ears, mouth each covered — in thin lead inscribed nga-ya-na-ma; another lays the figure in fragrant oil in a bronze bowl and recites until it 'rises up and sits'. Uses named are concealment, invulnerability, evasion, and shutting the mouths of those who see you. Wikipedia's account is the gentler one: the figure is Phra Sangkachai entering cessation, the nine gates closed against defilement, later pressed in powder by named Rattanakosin masters.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed: a phra khrueang. Whatever the treatise carves it from is material, not a resident; the vault keeps the kind in the Buddha-amulet class.
- look at: The hands over the face are the kind's whole identity; a figure with a visible face is not a pidta [cited]
- look at: The nine-gate type has more than two arms; count them [cited]
- look at: Powder bodies are usually lacquer-bound and dark brown to black, unlike the white somdej powder; metal ones are cast lead, bronze or alloy [tradition]
- look at: The treatise hollows the base, packs in a yantra and ground medicine, seals it with stingless-bee resin and lacquers and gilds the piece; a plugged base and gilt-over-lacquer are the marks of that recipe [catalogue]
- look at: Carved treatise pieces are one finger-joint tall [catalogue]
- vs phra-somdet: A somdej shows its face inside an arch on a white tablet; a pidta hides its face and is usually a dark lacquered powder or a metal casting
- vs phra-kring: A kring's hands are in the earth-touching pose and it chimes; a pidta's hands are over its face
- vs rup-lersi: A lersi has a beard, a topknot or tiger skin and an open face; a pidta has none of these and covers its face
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/c24e2c3cc05df5b19fb1a264368e0f7f6b36dfdd98daaef969cc82ff69fe7b90.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · หลวงปู่วิเวียร · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=57309281

confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## พระราหู · phra rahu · Phra Rahu (the eclipse-swallower)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-rahu/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-rahu.json
id: phra-rahu · level: kind
aliases: ราหู · ราหูอมจันทร์ · ราหูอมอาทิตย์ · ราหูกะลาตาเดียว · rahu · phra rahoo · rahu om chan · Rahu amulet · Rahu swallowing the moon · eclipse demon
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: natural · materials: กะลา (coconut shell), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, for the yantra pair; temple issues are many and uncredited here · Undated treatise · Central Thai tradition
what (th): ราหูอมจันทร์ แกะจากกะลามะพร้าวตาเดียวเป็นหลัก — เครื่องแก้เคล็ดทางโหราศาสตร์ของผู้ที่อยู่ในช่วงพระราหูเสวยอายุ เป็นเทพที่บูชา ไม่ใช่ผีที่เลี้ยง
what (en): Rahu swallowing the moon, classically carved into a one-eyed coconut shell — the astrological remedy worn by those in a Rahu period. This site's almanac pages keep the sky half of the story.
story: In the myth Rahu's head was cut off by Vishnu's discus after he drank the amrita, so when he swallows the sun or moon it passes out through his throat: the eclipse. Manuscript 6983 gives the amulet as a pair. Two hermits on Mount Yugandhara, foreseeing a poor age, made the Suriyaprapha (solar) and Chanthaprapha (lunar) yantras; the maker finds a one-eyed coconut shell, carves one Rahu swallowing the moon and one swallowing the sun, and inscribes the solar yantra on the sun-figure and the lunar on the moon-figure, with homage verses to each. The treatise sells it for wealth; the modern trade sells it as the remedy for a Rahu period in the horoscope, and the Buddhist protective verses against Rahu from the Candima and Suriya suttas sit behind both.
keeping: Deva tier: veneration, not feeding; can be set down. The trade's rule of offering black things to Rahu is tradition, not in this treatise.
- look at: Shell body: dark, oily surface with the coconut's own grain; 'one-eyed' means a shell showing a single germination eye [catalogue]
- look at: Head only, no body: the one deva in the market with no torso [cited]
- look at: Treatise pieces carry a 4×4 numeral square on the chest and a six-sector circle on the back [catalogue]
- look at: Metal and medallion types are common; the image, not the material, names the kind [catalogue]
- vs kala-ta-diao: A plain one-eyed coconut shell is a natural talisman, nobody home; once carved into Rahu and inscribed it becomes a deva object. Same shell, different class.
- vs khot-kala: A khot kala is a natural concretion found inside a shell, uncarved; Rahu is a carved image.
- vs jatukham: A Jatukham disc rings its seated deva with eight small Rahu heads; a Rahu amulet is one head, one disc, and no one in the middle.
- vs phaya-khrut: The garuda is a whole winged figure; Rahu is a head alone.

## พระรอด · phra rot · Phra Rod (Lamphun votive tablet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-rot/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-rot.json
id: phra-rot · level: kind
aliases: พระรอดลำพูน · พระรอดมหาวัน · พระรอดวัดมหาวัน · phra rod · phra rod lamphun · phra rot mahawan · Phra Rod Lamphun · the surviving one
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-north
origin: วัดมหาวันวนาราม ลำพูน Wat Mahawan Wanaram, Lamphun · ตำนานผูกกับพระนางจามเทวีและฤๅษีผู้สร้างเมือง Legend ties the tablets to Queen Chamadevi and the hermits who founded Hariphunchai; no maker is documented · Hariphunchai period, late Dvaravati; the oldest of the Benjaphakhi five per Thai Wikipedia · Lamphun
what (th): พระพิมพ์ดินเผาองค์เล็กจากกรุวัดมหาวัน ลำพูน องค์พระนั่งสมาธิในวงใบโพธิ์ เก่าที่สุดในชุดเบญจภาคี ชื่อ “รอด” คือรอดพ้นภัย ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่ในองค์พระ
what (en): A small fired-clay tablet from the cache at Wat Mahawan, Lamphun: a seated Buddha inside a ring of bodhi leaves, the oldest of the Benjaphakhi five. The name means the one who escapes harm. Nobody is home.
story: The temple's own account ties the tablets to Queen Chamadevi and the Hariphunchai founding; the Wat Mahawan chedi is where they were deposited, and Thai Wikipedia places the making in the late Dvaravati period, older than anything else in the set. Triyampavai's Benjaphakhi of around 1947 put it beside the Somdej, and the trade has read the name as a promise ever since: escape from harm, safe passage, a body that cannot be cut. Genuine pieces are a controlled antiquity; what circulates openly is mostly the form re-pressed.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is age and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Fine, hard-fired clay; colour varies with the firing (green, pikun-yellow, red, white), so colour alone settles nothing [catalogue]
- look at: The bodhi-leaf field around the figure is the type's signature; count and spacing follow the mould [tradition]
- look at: Smaller than the other four Benjaphakhi kinds; fits inside a closed hand [tradition]
- look at: Age reads as shrinkage and cache crust (คราบกรุ), never as patina: the clay body's dating signal on the material axis [catalogue]
- look at: A controlled antiquity; the open retail market carries reproductions and temple re-issues of the form, which is a statement about the category [tradition]
- vs phra-kru: Phra Rod is one named cache-find; phra kru is the whole category. Same class, same fired clay; the bodhi-leaf field and the Lamphun provenance name this one.
- vs phra-sum-ko: Sum Ko sits under an arch shaped like the letter ก in Sukhothai style from Kamphaeng Phet; Phra Rod is ringed by bodhi leaves in Hariphunchai style. Both fired clay, both nobody home.
- vs phra-nang-phaya: Nang Phaya is a triangle in Maravijaya with a coarse body; Phra Rod is tall and rounded, in meditation, with a fine body.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/37d56a6ad13fc672512bdc311f05baf0cfcc860703a74fcadffef7e7210e486e.png · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Somdej.watrakang · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=102451956
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/ba6ab231dcb9f68b7436961e57c9d1b46ebc87e6a6fd0568a53df2ab820a2850.png · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Somdej.watrakang · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=102452146
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/6735a767acce1a0a8f40c557d4424b4d2b5532e4f6bf6225a8d482e6384684d8.png · Public domain · Fine Arts Department · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=197017930

## พระสีวลี · phra siwali · Phra Siwali (the never-hungry monk)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-siwali/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-siwali.json
id: phra-siwali · level: kind
aliases: พระสิวลี · พระฉิมพลี · สีวลีเถระ · phra sivali · phra siwalee · phra chimphali · Sivali · Sivali Thera · foremost in receiving offerings
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th, mm, la
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) — ตำราพระฉิมพลี Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, the Phra Chimphali manual, which traces its own lineage to King Naresuan's time · The treatise claims descent from the reigns of Naresuan and Narai — its own claim, not a dated attestation · Nationwide; also Myanmar, Laos and Sri Lanka
what (th): พระสีวลี พระอรหันต์ผู้เลิศทางลาภ — แบกไม้เท้า กลด และกาน้ำ — บูชาเพื่อให้ปัจจัยมาถึงทันเวลา รูปหล่อและจี้ บูชาอย่างพระเครื่องทั่วไป ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): The arahant who never lacked — staff over shoulder, umbrella and kettle — carried for provision that arrives on time. Statue and pendant, venerated as an ordinary amulet.
story: Sivali was foremost among the Buddha's disciples in receiving offerings; his mother Suppavasa carried him seven years, seven months and seven days. Manuscript 6983 knows him as Phra Chimphali and opens its whole collection with him, claiming a lineage back through King Narai to Naresuan. Carve a closed-face Phakawambodi figure from rak-son root, one finger-length and half an inch tall, hollow it, grind shoots of rak-son, sawat and ka-long, wrap the relics of Sariputta and of Chimphali in two yantras and seal them inside with underground stingless-bee resin; then a bai-si, a duck, a chicken, gold and silver rings on the bai-si's peak, and a three-day tham-khwan. Honour it morning and evening; a candle each dusk guards against thieves, fire and flood, and the text gives a katha of homage to be said before any katha asking for gain. The standing monk with umbrella and kettle is what the shops sell now; the treatise's Chimphali looks nothing like him.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; the treatise's morning-and-evening honours are devotion, not upkeep a resident demands.
- look at: A standing monk with umbrella, staff and bag: not a Buddha, and not the portrait of a named modern monk [cited]
- look at: Class phra khrueang: nobody home, unlike the deva and spirit kinds it is sold beside [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise type is a closed-face figure in rak-son root, hollowed, charged with relics wrapped in two yantras and sealed with stingless-bee resin — a cavity and a resin plug are its marks [catalogue]
- look at: Brass shelf figures and metal pendants are the current retail form [catalogue]
- vs luang-pu-thuat: Luang Pu Thuat is a portrait of a named monk, usually seated, no umbrella; Siwali stands under his umbrella with a staff.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is the likeness of a known teacher; Siwali is an arahant of the Buddha's time, marked by his pilgrim kit.
- vs phra-pidta: The treatise's Chimphali is itself a closed-face Phakawambodi figure charged with Sivali's relic, so an old wooden pidta with a resin-sealed cavity may be one; an ordinary pidta is pressed or cast and unfilled.
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak is a seated woman beckoning; Siwali is a standing monk. The legend links them — he blessed her — and her money bag may bear his name.

## พระสมเด็จ · phra somdet · Phra Somdej
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-somdet/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-somdet.json
id: phra-somdet · level: kind
aliases: สมเด็จ · พระสมเด็จวัดระฆัง · สมเด็จวัดระฆังโฆสิตาราม · phra somdej · somdej · somdet wat rakhang · Somdej amulet · King of Amulets · Somdej Wat Rakang
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), ผงพุทธคุณ (powder of the Buddha's qualities) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th-central
origin: วัดระฆังโฆสิตาราม Wat Rakhang Kositaram, Thonburi side of Bangkok · สมเด็จพระพุฒาจารย์ (โต พฺรหฺมรํสี) Somdet Phra Phutthachan (To Phromrangsi), 'Somdej To' · Made across roughly 1812–1872, in three periods per Thai Wikipedia; the famous runs fall in the 1860s · Bangkok
what (th): แผ่นผงพุทธคุณอัดพิมพ์ทรงสี่เหลี่ยม มีองค์พระประทับนั่งในซุ้มครอบแก้ว เป็นพระเครื่องที่ถูกสร้างตามและสะสมมากที่สุด พลังอยู่ที่บารมีของผู้สร้างและการปลุกเสก ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่ในองค์พระ
what (en): A rectangular pressed tablet of sacred powder bearing a seated Buddha in an arch — the most copied, most collected amulet form there is. Power is the maker's barami and the consecration; nobody is home.
story: Somdej To of Wat Rakhang pressed these tablets in the last years of Rama IV and the first of Rama V. The trade calls the Wat Rakhang pieces the emperor of amulets and counts them among the Benjaphakhi, the canonical five. Almost every temple issue since borrows the form, which is why the form alone tells you little and the material tells you more.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is price and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: Six Wat Rakhang mould-types per Thai Wikipedia: Phra Prathan / Phim Yai (large), Chedi, Than Saem, Ket Bua Tum, Prok Pho, Sian Bat Ok Khrut. The trade usually counts five, folding the last into the others [cited]
- look at: Body is calcined shell-lime bound with cooked rice, banana, oil and sand, carrying the five sacred powders (ผงวิเศษ ๕ ประการ) and 108 herbal ingredients [cited]
- look at: Off-white to yellowish powder body flecked with coloured inclusions; the material is the first gate, the mould the second [tradition]
- look at: Age reads as a surface crust, never as rust: the powder body's dating signal per the material axis [catalogue]
- look at: The most reproduced material category in the trade; a careful eye is the norm here, which is a statement about the category, never about an object [catalogue]
- vs hun-phayon: A somdej is a Buddha in an arch with nobody home and nothing owed; a hun payon is a man-shaped figure of earth, straw or cloth that has been animated and is fed daily. Different class, different keeping, different provenance question.
- vs khun-phaen: Khun Phaen tablets use an Ayutthaya-style pentagonal or ruean-kaeo arch; the somdej form is a straight-edged rectangle with a bell-glass arch
- vs phra-phong-bai-lan: Palm-leaf-ash tablets are black-grey; the somdej body is white to cream

## พระสมเด็จจิตรลดา · phra somdet chitralada · Phra Somdej Chitralada (the royal somdej)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/somdet-chitralada/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/somdet-chitralada.json
id: somdet-chitralada · level: variant · parent: phra-somdet
aliases: สมเด็จจิตรลดา · พระกำลังแผ่นดิน · somdej jitlada · somdet chitlada · phra kamlang phaendin · Jitlada amulet · King Rama IX somdej
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อผง (sacred-powder paste), ผงพุทธคุณ (powder of the Buddha's qualities), เกศา (hair of the master) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th-central
origin:  · พระบาทสมเด็จพระบรมชนกาธิเบศร มหาภูมิพลอดุลยเดชมหาราช (รัชกาลที่ ๙) ทรงกดพิมพ์ด้วยพระหัตถ์ King Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX), who pressed each piece by hand · BE 2508–2513 (1965–1970) · Chitralada Villa, Bangkok — the name says where
what (th): พระสมเด็จทรงสามเหลี่ยมที่รัชกาลที่ ๙ ทรงสร้างและกดพิมพ์ด้วยพระหัตถ์ พระราชทานแก่ทหาร ตำรวจ ข้าราชการ และประชาชน ระหว่าง พ.ศ. ๒๕๐๘–๒๕๑๓ พร้อมเอกสารกำกับ
what (en): The triangular somdej King Rama IX made and hand-pressed at Chitralada, given between 1965 and 1970 to soldiers, police, officials and civilians, each with a certificate.
story: The mass pressed into it lists powder from various votive tablets, dried flowers from garlands presented to the King, strands of the royal hair, flowers from the regalia, soil and herbs from the Buddhist sites of India and Sri Lanka, sacred material from every Thai province, and water from the auspicious sources used at the coronation. The King pressed each piece himself, often late into the evening. Forty small pieces were made for the royal children; the rest went out with a certificate naming recipient, date and number.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; a phra khrueang. The certificate travels with the piece and is its provenance.
- look at: An isosceles triangle, not the rectangle of the parent kind [cited]
- look at: A nine-petal lotus base; count the petals [cited]
- look at: Two sizes only: 20 × 30 mm and 12 × 19 mm [cited]
- look at: Brown to dark-green body with mixed inclusions, never the white somdej powder [cited]
- look at: Each recipient was given a certificate with name, date, serial number and photograph; the paper is part of the type [cited]
- vs phra-somdet: The parent kind is a white rectangle with the Buddha in an arch; the Chitralada is a dark triangle on a lotus with no arch
- vs phra-nang-phaya: Nang Phaya is also triangular but is a fired-clay cache find from Phitsanulok in the earth-touching pose; the Chitralada is a 1960s powder tablet in meditation
- vs phra-phong-suphan: Phong Suphan is a triangular clay cache tablet from Suphan Buri; the material and the century separate them
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/ec86160f5a0d760df7b111ea45505cab72d5966c7db42318d420173b8d89f39f.jpg · CC BY 3.0 · ผู้สร้างสรรค์ผลงาน/ส่งข้อมูลเก็บในคลังข้อมูลเสรีวิกิมีเดียคอมมอนส์ - เทวประภาส มากคล้าย · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=7819524
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:th-wiki-somdet-chitralada — พระสมเด็จจิตรลดา — วิกิพีเดีย; s:commons-amulets-th — Wikimedia Commons — Category:Amulets of Thailand (and subcategories)
confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## พระซุ้มกอ · phra sum ko · Phra Sum Ko (Kamphaeng Phet arched tablet)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/phra-sum-ko/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/phra-sum-ko.json
id: phra-sum-ko · level: kind
aliases: พระกำแพงซุ้มกอ · ซุ้มกอ · กำแพงซุ้มกอ · phra somkor · phra sum kor · kamphaeng sum ko · Phra Somkor · Phra Kamphaeng Sum Kor
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tablet · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body), เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th-central
origin: กรุทุ่งเศรษฐี นครชุม กำแพงเพชร (วัดพระบรมธาตุ วัดพิกุล และกรุใกล้เคียง) The Thung Setthi caches at Nakhon Chum, Kamphaeng Phet (Wat Phra Borommathat, Wat Phikun and neighbouring sites) ·  · Sukhothai period; English Wikipedia dates the find at Wat Phra Borommathat Nakhon Chum to 1849, the year Thai Wikipedia gives for Somdej To's visit to the temple · Kamphaeng Phet
what (th): พระพิมพ์ดินเผาจากกรุทุ่งเศรษฐี กำแพงเพชร องค์พระนั่งสมาธิในซุ้มโค้งรูปตัว ก ศิลปะสุโขทัย หายากที่สุดในเบญจภาคี วงการพูดว่า “มีกูไม่จน” ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิตอยู่
what (en): A fired-clay tablet from the Thung Setthi caches at Kamphaeng Phet: a seated Buddha under an arch curved like the letter ก, in Sukhothai style. The rarest of the Benjaphakhi five. The trade's saying for it is 'have me and you will not be poor'. Nobody is home.
story: English Wikipedia dates the find to 1849 at Wat Phra Borommathat, Nakhon Chum, the same year Thai Wikipedia gives for Somdej To's discovery of relics in that temple's chedis. The trade adds an inscription found with the tablets and reads from it the promise that the keeper will not be poor; that text is tradition here, not cited. The Sukhothai-style figure under its ก-shaped arch went into Triyampavai's five around 1947, and of the five it is the one least seen.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history; its provenance question is age and authenticity, never spiritual safety.
- look at: The ก-shaped arch is both the name and the first mark to check [tradition]
- look at: Fired clay carrying herb (ว่าน) material; the trade describes the body as fine and soft-looking [tradition]
- look at: The with-kanok and without-kanok moulds separate on the scrollwork beside the arch [tradition]
- look at: The rarest of the five to encounter per Thai Wikipedia; what the open market shows is mostly the form re-issued, a statement about the category [cited]
- look at: Age reads as shrinkage and cache crust, never patina [catalogue]
- vs phra-rot: Phra Rod is ringed by bodhi leaves in Hariphunchai style from Lamphun; Sum Ko sits under a ก-shaped arch in Sukhothai style from Kamphaeng Phet. Both fired clay, both nobody home.
- vs khun-phaen: Khun Phaen uses an Ayutthaya pentagonal ruean-kaeo arch and its material story belongs to the line; Sum Ko's arch is round-topped and the body is clay and herb. Class can differ; here it does not.
- vs phra-kru: Sum Ko is one named cache-find; phra kru is the category. The arch and the Kamphaeng Phet provenance name this one.

## ปี่เซียะ · pixiu · Pixiu (wealth beast) pendant
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/pixiu/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/pixiu.json
id: pixiu · level: kind
native: 貔貅 · 天祿 · 辟邪 (zh) · tỳ hưu (vi)
aliases: ปี่เซี๊ยะ · ปี่เซี้ย · ผีซิว · เผ่ย์เย้า · เทียนลู่ · เทียงลก · pi xiu · pei yao · tianlu · bixie · tỳ hưu · pi yao · wealth beast · heavenly deer
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: figure · materials: ทองเหลือง (brass), ทองแดง (copper) · functions: โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: diaspora, th, vn
origin:  · โรงงานหยกและโลหะ ร้านฮวงจุ้ย บางชิ้นผ่านพิธีเบิกเนตรที่ศาลเจ้า Jade and metal workshops and feng shui shops; some pieces are put through an eye-opening rite at a shrine, which the trade holds · Named in the Shangshu and the Shiji as a beast of war; Han-era stone tomb guardians survive; the pendant is modern · China; Thailand, Vietnam and the overseas Chinese trade
what (th): สัตว์ในตำนานจีน หัวมังกร ตัวสิงโต มีปีก เชื่อว่ากินทองแล้วไม่ถ่ายเพราะไม่มีรูทวาร จึงเป็นเครื่องรางเรียกทรัพย์และกันร้าย ทำเป็นจี้หยก กำไล แหวน และรูปตั้งคู่ ขายมากในตลาดไทย-จีน วิกิพีเดียไทยเรียก ปี่เซียะ ผีซิว เผ่ย์เย้า
what (en): The Chinese wealth beast: dragon head, lion body, wings, and no anus, so gold goes in and never out. Worn as a jade pendant, bracelet or ring, or set as a pair at a shop door, it is one of the biggest sellers in Thai-Chinese retail under ปี่เซียะ. The vault's class vocabulary does not place it.
story: Classical texts list it among the fierce beasts the Yellow Emperor drove into battle; the Han carved it in stone to guard tombs. The one-horned form is tianlu, the two-horned bixie, and the two names still label the two jobs, wealth and warding. Gamblers in Macau and Hong Kong venerate it. Thai listings sell it as a colour-changing pendant 'blessed in Hong Kong', a brass figure standing on an ingot, a silver ring, and a bracelet 'for the birth day', which grafts the Thai weekday system onto a Chinese beast.
keeping: The vault leaves this unplaced, on purpose. In Chinese feng shui logic it is an instrument with nobody home; in Thai-Chinese retail it gets an eye-opening rite, is spoken of as บูชา, and some keepers offer it water and touch it daily. That is the veneration upkeep of a resident class wearing an impersonal object's form, and a knower must draw the line. Until then: treat an unknown one as impersonal, and a rite-opened one as owed regard.
- look at: Dragon head on a lion body with wings; count the horns, one for tianlu, two for bixie. English Wikipedia says modern pieces are mostly one-horned, Chinese Wikipedia says two-horned now predominates: the two articles disagree, so look rather than assume [cited]
- look at: No anus by belief, so wealth enters and never leaves; the folk logic behind the whole class [cited]
- look at: Jade, glass, wood, ceramic, copper and cloth; the trade matches material to the owner's five-element chart [cited]
- look at: Set as a crouching pair, or worn one per wrist; a single figure facing into the room is what the trade warns against [cited]
- look at: Thai spellings vary, ปี่เซียะ / ผีซิว / เผ่ย์เย้า / เทียนลู่; Lazada Thailand titles use ปี่เซียะ [cited]
- vs phaya-khrut: Garuda is a bird-man, upright, with a beak; the pixiu is a four-legged dragon-headed beast. Both have wings, which is where the confusion starts on a small pendant.
- vs bat-quai: The bagua mirror guards the same door but is a diagram, not a beast, and nobody feeds it.
