## ปลาตะเพียน · pla taphian · Pla taphian (carp charm)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/pla-taphian/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/pla-taphian.json
id: pla-taphian · level: kind
aliases: ปลาตะเพียนเงินปลาตะเพียนทอง · ปลาตะเพียนสาน · ตะเพียนทอง · pla tapian · pla ta pian · taphian thong · silver-and-gold carp · woven palm-leaf fish · barb-fish charm
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: ทองแดง (copper), เนื้อเงิน (silver), เนื้อทองคำ (gold), เนื้อนาค (copper-gold alloy (rose gold)) · functions: ค้าขาย (trade, selling), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-central
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983 · Undated treatise. English Wikipedia places the woven form in Ayutthaya, citing the Description of the Topography of Ayutthaya's mention of woven pla taphian sold on Ton Market street · Ayutthaya and Central Thailand
what (th): ปลาตะเพียนคู่ตัดจากแผ่นโลหะบางลงยันต์ แขวนบูชาให้ซื้อง่ายขายดี ชื่อเดียวกับปลาสานใบลานที่แขวนเหนือเปลเด็กในงานฝีมืออยุธยา
what (en): A pair of carp cut from thin metal sheet and inscribed, hung up so that buying is easy and selling brisk — sharing its name with the woven palm-leaf fish mobile hung over Ayutthaya cradles.
story: The treatise beats copper or silver thin, cuts it into a carp, names one fish silver and one gold, and inscribes the syllables i, u and a central na with three metta-and-gain verses, one recitation per blowing. A second recipe allows gold, nak, silver or copper, makes the pair male and female, and sets out offerings for the teacher — a one-baht candle, five ordinary candles, five white flowers — before hanging them up. Two further kathas follow: one to worship the fish, one to consecrate rice fed to the fish every day. English Wikipedia's woven fish is a different object with the same name: palm-leaf strips woven into a mobile of nine, twelve or fifteen fish round a mother fish, hung over cradles in Ayutthaya and Thonburi.
keeping: Nobody home by class, nothing owed — with the treatise's own wrinkle: it feeds the fish consecrated rice daily. Read that as the trade's courtesy to a luck-object, not as a resident; a knower may rule otherwise.
- look at: Flat sheet metal cut to a fish outline, not a thick casting [catalogue]
- look at: Comes as a pair — male and female, or one 'silver' and one 'gold' [catalogue]
- look at: Syllables inside the body mark the inscribed kind; the woven palm-leaf fish carries none [catalogue]
- look at: Made to hang; the treatise gives it no pendant loop [catalogue]
- vs takrut: The trade takrut in the same treatise inscribes the same fish yantra and rolls it; the pla taphian stays flat and fish-shaped.
- vs phaya-tao-ruean: The house-turtle is the other trade animal: a thick cast pendant, where the fish is thin sheet made to hang.
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak is a deva venerated with offerings; the fish is an inscribed sheet — though the treatise does feed it consecrated rice daily, which blurs the line this record keeps.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/2313a07871fa1989ea73d564dd1a3eba691cb5dc5f05c3acc5a8cd1f20fd63fc.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Mr.Peerapong Prasutr · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=38176557
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/df3aa74cbe84182660b2736a0601d5f3eeec75e9bcd518d7f87e1e11859d93d6.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Mr.Peerapong Prasutr · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=38176556
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/8efba825d3c048d3d456f7b11d3802396e4ddbfa35feee6f4daaae0b2e38b853.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Mr.Peerapong Prasutr · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=38176674
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/97ccd8dbe2fa8b50411029083b5592c6dc09acbf13e3ad056a84e1d739e1e92d.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Mr.Peerapong Prasutr · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=85993935

## ราจาห์ · rajah · Rajah (Javanese-Malay written talisman)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/rajah/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/rajah.json
id: rajah · level: kind
native: rajah (id) · راجه · rajah (ms) · ꦫꦗꦃ · rajah (jv)
aliases: ยันต์ชวา · อักขระราจาห์ · rajah jawa · wafak · wifiq · isim · Javanese yantra · Islamic-Javanese magic diagram
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), ค้าขาย (trade, selling) · region: id, my
origin:  · กียาอี ดุกุน หรือผู้รู้ ilmu hikmah A kyai, a dukun, or anyone credited with ilmu hikmah; the Javanese primbon and Arabic manuals (Syamsul Ma'arif, al-Aufaq) are the trade's named books · Islamic Java, carried through pesantren and the primbon almanacs · Java; used across Indonesia and Malaysia
what (th): สูตรเขียนของชวา-มลายู: อักษรอาหรับ ตัวเลข ตารางวะฟัก และสัญลักษณ์ที่ผู้เขียนรู้ความหมาย ลงบนกระดาษ ผ้า หนัง โลหะ หรือผิวหนัง พลังอยู่ที่ตัวเขียนและผู้เขียน คือคู่ขนานของ “ยันต์” ในโลกอิสลาม
what (en): The Javanese-Malay written formula: Arabic letters, numerals, a wafaq square and symbols meaningful to the writer, set on paper, cloth, skin, metal or the body. Power sits in the writing and the writer — the Islamic-world counterpart of the Thai yan, and the thing a jimat usually carries.
story: In Javanese thinking a rajah is a jimat with power in it: used to treat the sick, to ward, to make the body kebal, to draw love or custom. The writer is someone with ilmu hikmah — a kyai or a dukun — and the books the trade names are the Syamsul Ma'arif, the al-Aufaq and the Javanese primbon. That the Indonesian word also means tattoo says the skin was always one of its media. Religious opinion calls it shirk when the writing itself is believed to act. Everything here beyond the id.wikipedia one-liner is trade knowledge and is hedged accordingly.
keeping: Filed with yantra_wattu: impersonal, nothing fed, nothing owed. The writing is treated as scripture — kept dry, never stepped over, kept out of unclean places.
- look at: Pure writing — Arabic letters, numerals, grids, symbols; never a Buddha, hermit or animal figure [cited]
- look at: A grid whose rows sum alike — the wafq — is the core of grid-type rajah, in occult use since the 13th century [cited]
- look at: The medium hints the maker: paper from a pesantren hand, skin or metal from a dukun, and on the body it is a tattoo — the same word in Indonesian [tradition]
- look at: Written over a whole shirt it is a baju rajah; the Commons example is one [cited]
- vs jimat: Rajah is the written formula, jimat the carried object: a rajah can sit inside a jimat, and a jimat need not contain one.
- vs pha-yan: A Thai pha yan carries figures and Khom letters; a rajah is Arabic and aniconic.
- vs yan-lanna: A Lanna yan is Tham script in a Buddhist grid; a rajah is Arabic in an Islamic one. Same squared logic, different scripture.
- vs in-yantra: A Burmese in is a weikza-lineage grid in Burmese letters; a rajah is an ilmu-hikmah grid in Arabic.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/708d408beae22908cfd4dafb34e554dfa61cbe33e83a09895abe1d5173f148bb.jpg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Muhamad Izzul Fiqih · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=156701516
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:id-wiki-tato — Tato — Wikipedia bahasa Indonesia (one-line definition of rajah); s:id-wiki-jimat — Jimat — Wikipedia bahasa Indonesia; s:en-wiki-magic-square — Magic square — Wikipedia (wafq al-a'dad section); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: low · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## เหรียญพระเกจิ · rian phra kechi · monk medallion
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/rian-kechi/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/rian-kechi.json
id: rian-kechi · level: kind
aliases: เหรียญหลวงพ่อ · เหรียญหลวงปู่ · เหรียญรุ่นแรก · เหรียญปั๊ม · เหรียญเสมา · rian · rian luang pho · rian roon raek · monk coin · guru monk medal · first-batch medal
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: medallion · materials: ทองแดง (copper), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อเงิน (silver), เนื้อทองคำ (gold), เนื้อนาค (copper-gold alloy (rose gold)), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th
origin:  · วัดและสำนักทั่วประเทศ ออกเป็นรุ่น Issued by temples nationwide in named batches (รุ่น) · Mid-Rattanakosin to the present; the trade dates the struck-portrait form to the reign of Rama V · Nationwide
what (th): เหรียญโลหะปั๊มรูปเหมือนพระเกจิ มีชื่อ วัด และปีที่สร้าง ออกเป็นรุ่น เป็นพระเครื่องที่บอกอายุตัวเองชัดที่สุด ไม่มีผู้อยู่ พลังอยู่ที่บารมีของท่านและการปลุกเสก
what (en): A struck coin-form medallion carrying a revered monk's portrait, name and temple, usually dated to the batch (รุ่น). The most datable of all forms — the coin itself says when.
story: Temples strike medallions in batches for an occasion — a birthday merit-making, a consecration, a building fund — and the first batch of a monk (รุ่นแรก) is the one the trade prices highest. Within a batch the metal sets the order: gold, silver, naak, then copper or gilt. One free Commons piece is a 2506 silver reverse struck for an abbot's 84th birthday; another is a Wat Kalong medallion with the takraw-ball yantra. The form gives the market its clearest dating, which is why so many copies are of medallions.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; a phra khrueang. Provenance question is authenticity and batch.
- look at: Struck, not cast: crisp edges, fine relief, a flat back. Casting texture points to a rup lo or a cast copy [catalogue]
- look at: The lettering names the monk, temple and BE year; the most datable of forms, the coin itself says when [catalogue]
- look at: A loop, either struck integral or soldered, and a cut or milled rim [tradition]
- look at: Copper, brass, silver, naak, gold, or gilt (กะไหล่) over base metal; within one batch the metal orders the price [tradition]
- vs rup-lo: A medallion is flat and struck with a loop; a rup lo is a three-dimensional casting of the same monk
- vs locket: A locket carries a photograph under glass or resin with material packed behind it; a medallion is solid struck metal front to back
- vs luang-pu-thuat: Luang Pu Thuat pieces include medallions, but the canonical early runs are pressed wan tablets and cast 'flat-iron back' figures; a medallion of him is a rian kechi of one monk
- vs jatukham: A Jatukham is a large deity medallion; a rian kechi shows a monk

## รูปหล่อ · rup lo · cast monk figure
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/rup-lo/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/rup-lo.json
id: rup-lo · level: kind
aliases: รูปหล่อโบราณ · รูปหล่อลอยองค์ · รูปเหมือนหล่อ · รูปหล่อปั๊ม · roop lor · rup lor · roop lor boran · cast monk statuette · loi ong figure
class: พระเครื่อง (Buddhist amulet) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), สัมฤทธิ์ (bronze), นวโลหะ (nine-metal alloy), เนื้อเงิน (silver) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape) · region: th
origin:  · วัดและสำนักทั่วประเทศ Temples nationwide; the trade's reference lineage for the old cast form is Luang Pho Ngoen of Wat Bang Khlan · Rattanakosin to the present · Nationwide
what (th): รูปพระสงฆ์นั่งสมาธิหล่อโลหะลอยองค์ คือญาติสามมิติของเหรียญ มีตั้งแต่ขนาดห้อยคอถึงตั้งบูชา พลังอยู่ที่บารมีของท่านและการปลุกเสก ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A small cast statue of a monk seated in meditation — the medallion's three-dimensional cousin, from pendant size up to the altar.
story: The trade separates the old lost-wax or sand-cast pieces (รูปหล่อโบราณ) from later die-struck three-dimensional ones (รูปหล่อปั๊ม), and holds Luang Pho Ngoen of Wat Bang Khlan as the reference lineage for the old form. Today most temples issue a cast figure of their own master with a code and serial, sold in the same batches as the medallion.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed; a phra khrueang.
- look at: Fully three-dimensional; a flat portrait is a medallion [catalogue]
- look at: Bald, robed, no ushnisha and usually no lotus base: a monk, not a Buddha [catalogue]
- look at: Underside shows a cut sprue, file marks, or a plugged pour hole; casting leaves these, striking does not [tradition]
- look at: Modern temple runs usually stamp a code and serial number; a type mark, not a proof [tradition]
- vs rian-kechi: A rup lo is in the round; a rian kechi is a flat struck disc with a loop
- vs phra-kring: A kring is a Buddha with a lotus base and a pellet; a rup lo is a monk, and a pellet in one is the exception the trade names separately
- vs luang-pu-thuat: A cast Luang Pu Thuat is a rup lo of one monk with its own canonical forms; the kind here is the general form
- vs rup-lersi: A lersi wears a beard and tiger skin; a rup lo is a shaven monk in robes
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## รูปพระฤๅษี · rup phra ruesi · Phra Lersi figure (the hermit-teacher)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/rup-lersi/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/rup-lersi.json
id: rup-lersi · level: kind
aliases: ฤๅษี · ฤาษี · พระฤๅษี · พ่อแก่ · ปู่ฤๅษี · lersi · ruesi · reusi · pho kae · hermit sage · rishi figure · Por Gae
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: figure · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over) · region: th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) ให้ ๓ วิธี Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, three moulding methods · Undated treatise · Central Thai tradition
what (th): รูปพระฤๅษีห่มหนังเสือ ครูของวิชาทั้งปวง บูชาในวันไหว้ครู ตำราในชุดนี้ให้วิธีปั้น: ดินยอดปลวกและใบไม้ ๗ อย่าง ปั้นเป็นพระมหาฤๅษี
what (en): The tiger-skinned hermit sage — the tradition's own teacher-figure, honoured at every wai khru. A treatise in this corpus gives a moulding recipe: termite-mound earth and seven named leaves, shaped into the Great Lersi.
story: Manuscript 6983 gives three ways. Method 1, for whoever would learn medicine and hold mantras so they rise in power: earth from the tops of seven termite mounds moulded into the Great Lersi, seven leaves sealed inside, ascetic offering-foods set out, the katha beginning นาโคคีรียะ recited 108 times and then the Itipiso 108. Method 2 mixes earths gathered by sevens from named places with burned leaves (the treatise gives a making-recipe; its ingredients are not reproduced here); the figure presides whenever medicine is ground, on a white cloth with bai-si to left and right. Method 3 seats him cross-legged with a rosary, marks numerals on crown, arms, knees and base, and consecrates the leaves 108 times before sealing them in. The text closes: whoever finds this treatise has met the Lersi himself.
keeping: Unplaced: the class vocabulary does not yet carry the lersi as a member term, and this record keeps class null rather than guess. Most keepers treat the figure as a teacher venerated on wai-khru days, not a resident to feed; the treatise sets offerings before him when work begins and asks his leave. Held here ahead of a vocabulary entry.
- look at: A human figure, not a Buddha and not a monk: the hermit has a chignon-crown, beard and tiger-skin where a monk has robes and a shaven head [catalogue]
- look at: Treatise pieces are moulded from termite-mound earth gathered at seven places (method 2 adds earths gathered by sevens from named places): a coarse earth body, not pressed powder [catalogue]
- look at: Seven named leaves are sealed inside: chumsaeng, ratchaphruek, makham-kai, matum (bael), khan-song, kanlapaphruek, chaiyaphruek — a filled cavity is the type's mark [catalogue]
- look at: The Pho Kae mask-head of the performing arts is a teacher-icon, not the amulet figure, though it is the same sage [tradition]
- vs chuchok: Chuchok is an old beggar with a staff and bag and no crown; the lersi has the chignon-crown, tiger-skin and rosary. Both are unplaced by the class vocabulary.
- vs luang-pu-thuat: Luang Pu Thuat is a monk, shaven and robed; the hermit wears his hair up and his beard long.
- vs phra-siwali: Phra Siwali stands with umbrella and staff and is an arahant monk; the lersi sits with a rosary and is no monk at all.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo is a cast monk; the hermit is a lay teacher-sage. Same casting, different head.

## สายสิญจน์ · sai sin · Sai sin (blessed cotton thread)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/sai-sin/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/sai-sin.json
id: sai-sin · level: kind
native: ຝ້າຍຜູກແຂນ (lo) · អំបោះសែន (km)
aliases: ด้ายสายสิญจน์ · ด้ายมงคล · ด้ายผูกข้อมือ · ฝ้ายผูกแขน · ด้ายปริตร · sai sin · saisin · fai phuk khaen · sai sinchana · sacred thread · blessed string bracelet · baci string
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: th, la, kh
origin:  ·  · Undatable; older than any object in this catalogue · Thailand, Laos, Cambodia
what (th): ด้ายฝ้ายดิบสีขาวที่พระถือขณะเจริญพระพุทธมนต์ วงรอบบ้าน พันองค์พระ แล้วตัดผูกข้อมือเป็นสิริมงคล ใช้ทั่วไทย ลาว เขมร ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): Raw white cotton thread held by the monks during paritta chanting, run round a house or a Buddha image, then cut and tied at the wrist as a blessing. Thai, Lao and Khmer alike; the chant is the power, nobody is home.
story: th.wikipedia calls it paritta thread: the monks hold it while chanting, it circles a house clockwise at a merit-making, wraps a Buddha image, is tied at the wrist, and as the twinned มงคลแฝด crowns bride and groom. The Lao and Isan baci ties it on the right wrist for the khwan, worn at least three days and untied, never cut. Ms 6983 uses it as the boundary of the working space — three turns, or seven layers with yantra hung at the eight directions, the thread spun by a virgin girl — inside which oil is cooked, a kuman made or a cloth inscribed. The thread is the frame around every other recipe in this catalogue.
keeping: Worn until it falls off or is untied; the baci custom is never to cut it. Nothing to feed. When done, it goes somewhere clean — a tree, a shrine — not the bin.
- look at: Undyed raw cotton with nothing written on it; once inscribed and plaited it is a phirot or a waist-cord, not sai sin [cited]
- look at: A loose wrist loop with a plain knot; not a bracelet with a clasp [cited]
- look at: Lao and Isan strings also come yellow (faith), red (bravery) or black (mourning) per en.wikipedia; white is the default everywhere [cited]
- look at: There is no antique market: every string is new, and what is paid for is the rite, not the thread [field]
- vs waen-phirot: A phirot is plaited from an inscribed strip and lacquered; sai sin is bare thread.
- vs takrut: A takrut may hang on sai sin cord; the cord is then the string, not the charm.
- vs prachiat: A prachiat is an inscribed cloth band for the head or arm; sai sin is thread at the wrist.

## สาลิกา · salika · Salika (golden-tongued myna)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/salika/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/salika.json
id: salika · level: kind
aliases: สาลิกาลิ้นทอง · สาริกา · ตะกรุดสาลิกา · สาลิกาคู่ · sarika · salika lin thong · sariga · golden-tongue myna · myna charm
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: figure · materials: เนื้อทองคำ (gold), เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), ค้าขาย (trade, selling) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983 · Undated treatise; one recipe fixes the inscribing to the full-moon Monday of the twelfth lunar month · Central Thai tradition
what (th): นกสาลิกาคู่แห่งวาจาไพเราะ พ่อค้า คนจีบ และใครก็ตามที่ต้องให้คนเชื่อพกไว้ มักเป็นนกคู่เล็กโลหะหรือไม้ หรือยันต์รูปนก ดัชนียันต์ที่นี่มีลาย
what (en): The paired myna birds of sweet speech — carried by sellers, suitors and anyone who must be believed. Usually a small couple of birds in metal or wood, or the yantra of them; the yant index here draws the design.
story: The treatise gives four salika recipes. The gold-tongue takrut beats grade-eight gold thin, inscribes a Buddha-figure yantra, consecrates it with the ten-precepts formula, and is held under the tongue before speaking or preaching so that whoever sees your face loves you. A second uses two phai of Bang Saphan gold inscribed on the full-moon Monday of the twelfth month with bai-si and a pig's head for the teacher. The Salika Mahosot draws two facing birds on paper, gold, silver, lead or copper, each sex with its own katha, then rolls it as a takrut or seats it in a beeswax case — for preachers and singers. The fourth, 'salika that closes the coffin-mouth', is an object of another class wearing this name; the treatise gives a making-recipe; its ingredients are not reproduced here.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed — for the bird pair and the gold-tongue takrut. The coffin-mouth salika in the same treatise belongs to another class by its making; the name does not settle the making.
- look at: The birds come as a pair; a single bird is another charm or half a set [catalogue]
- look at: The takrut form is tiny: the treatise uses two phai of gold, a weight that rolls to a fingernail [catalogue]
- look at: Usually kept in oil; expect a greasy surface and an oil-stained case [tradition]
- look at: Its work is metta and speech; a piece sold for invulnerability is another kind wearing the name [catalogue]
- vs takrut: A salika takrut is a takrut by form; the yantra and the under-the-tongue use make it this kind. File by the yantra when it is visible, by the seller's name when it is not.
- vs nang-kwak: Nang Kwak is a beckoning woman, a deva venerated with offerings; the salika is a bird with nobody home. Both are sold for trade.
- vs phaya-khrut: Garuda is a winged deva for authority; the salika is a small paired songbird for speech.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:en-wiki-takrut — Takrut — Wikipedia; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## สีผึ้ง · si phueng · Charm wax (lip-wax)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/si-phueng/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/si-phueng.json
id: si-phueng · level: kind
aliases: สีผึ้งสีปาก · ขี้ผึ้งเสน่ห์ · สีผึ้งเมตตา · สีผึ้งมหาเสน่ห์ · see pheung · see phueng · sri phueng · love wax · beeswax salve · metta balm
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: wax · materials: — · functions: มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), มหาละลวย (infatuation, bewitchment) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) — ๑๔ ตำรับ Anonymous treatise, manuscript 6983 — fourteen recipes · Undated treatise · Central Thai tradition
what (th): ขี้ผึ้งหุงในตลับเล็ก แตะปากหรือหน้าผากก่อนพูด ขาย หรือจีบ ตำรามี ๑๔ ตำรับเสน่ห์ ของในตลับเป็นอะไรขึ้นกับมือใครหุง
what (en): A wax or balm in a small tin, touched to lips or brow before speaking, selling, courting. The corpus's formulary holds attraction-wax recipes; what a given pot is depends on whose hands made it.
story: Fourteen recipes. Formula 1 moulds the wax into Mae Thorani treading Rahu, numbers her limbs, makes offerings for three days with an egg a day, then cooks her with moss from the town gate and the elephant post, civet and borneol, with งะญะพะมะ written on the pot. Formula 3 moulds a man and a woman on ghost-piercing sticks, throws consecrated rice until they kiss, adds turtle gall and cooks in an eggshell. For formula 8 the treatise gives a making-recipe; its ingredients are not reproduced here; formula 10 takes the wax through three firings in the ordination hall — element, flame and sun — and grades it by how many it survived. Formula 14 sends chaste children named Rak and Di to buy the wax and shapes the hearthstones as Nonthuk, Hanuman and Ravana. It is touched to the lips, cheeks, crown or a hem; Thai Wikipedia's article on ไสยศาสตร์ gives 'consecrate wax and anoint the lips for attraction' as its stock example of a charm.
keeping: Unplaced by the class vocabulary, and that refusal is the keeping note: a herbal wax owes nothing, one cooked by the other route wants a spirit-object's care. Ask whose hands made it; if nobody can say, treat the tin as if someone were home.
- look at: A salve in a tin, used by anointing, never worn; the form alone separates it from every other kind here [catalogue]
- look at: Recipes buy wax from three vendors without haggling and favour three-colour wax — white, red, yellow (formulas 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14) [catalogue]
- look at: The aromatic base repeats across recipes — civet, borneol, agarwood, kalamphak, rak son flower, scented oil — so a scented wax is the type, not a sign of anything [catalogue]
- look at: Formula 10 grades the wax by firings — element fire, flame fire, sun fire; one firing is third grade, three is first — a grade a buyer cannot read off the tin [catalogue]
- look at: Class follows the making: formula 8 cooks by a route the treatise gives and this catalogue does not reproduce; formula 10 cooks in the ubosot. The pot does not say which; the maker's lineage does [catalogue]
- look at: Applied by finger to target — ring finger for women, index for lords and monks (formula 13) [catalogue]
- vs waan: Waan is a plant; wax is a cooked salve that may contain waan. One is alive, one is finished.
sources: s:holding-key — manuscript-wiki/data/holding_key.json — the 36-kind identification key behind wichaa.net/holding; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-functions — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/functions.md — function axis; s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:th-wiki-saiyasat — ไสยศาสตร์ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: high · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## เสื้อยันต์ · suea yan · Suea yan (yantra shirt)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/suea-yan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/suea-yan.json
id: suea-yan · level: kind
aliases: เสื้อยันต์แดง · เสื้อลงยันต์ · seua yant · sua yant · yant shirt · yantra shirt · talismanic shirt · war shirt
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: cloth · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), มหาอุด (stopping projectiles / misfire) · region: th
origin:  ·  · th.wikipedia dates prachiat distribution to soldiers to King Taksin (B.E. 2312) and Rama I (B.E. 2328); the shirt is those cloths sewn up. No dated shirt named. · Thailand
what (th): เสื้อที่เขียนหรือพิมพ์ยันต์เต็มตัว แบบเก่าเย็บจากผ้าประเจียดผืนเล็กหลายผืน สวมออกศึกหรือขึ้นชก เชื่อว่าคงกระพันแคล้วคลาด ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A shirt inscribed with yantra all over — in the old form, small prachiat cloths sewn into a garment — worn into battle or the ring for invulnerability and evasion. Power in the inscription; nobody home.
story: th.wikipedia treats the shirt as one form of prachiat: small inscribed cloths sewn into a garment. It records such cloths handed to commanders under King Taksin and to soldiers under Rama I, and their later life on boxers. The tattoo article says the shirt carries the tattoo's own repertoire — eight-direction yantra, Hanuman, tiger — on cloth instead of skin. Ms 6983 has no shirt recipe; its cloth pieces are prachiat and handkerchiefs.
keeping: Nothing to feed; kept folded and high. The custom of not washing it with ordinary laundry is tradition, not a rule this catalogue can cite.
- look at: A garment with sleeves or armholes, not a flat cloth [cited]
- look at: Older shirts show seams joining several small cloths, hand-drawn in black ink; printed one-colour yantra with no seams is a modern issue [cited]
- look at: Designs repeat the tattoo repertoire — eight-direction, Hanuman, tiger [cited]
- look at: Hand ink soaks through to the inside; screen-print sits on one face [tradition]
- vs pha-yan: A pha yan is a flat cloth; a suea yan is cut and sewn to be worn. Same class and keeping.
- vs prachiat: A prachiat is a band for the head or arm; th.wikipedia defines the shirt as prachiat cloths sewn together.
- vs khmer-yantra-cloth: Khmer yantra cloth is a flat cloth in Khmer script; a Thai shirt is a garment, though the scripts overlap.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/cc203327e4e1ddd52759a71125add424f0d389fe2d34a59fc633bd203fb2595a.jpg · CC0 · Iudexvivorum · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=62443102
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/2911447e32a3620e142e555a7b43f0ade7c42f6422c70e09e4b62b4893a7216f.jpg · CC0 · Iudexvivorum · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=62443106
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/273b3ca959f0c904f46a4c399d71c94c0a4fc8ecdb1baabc4d984477b233b783.jpg · CC0 · Iudexvivorum · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=62443107
sources: s:th-wiki-prachiat — ประเจียด — วิกิพีเดีย; s:th-wiki-sak-yant — การสักยันต์ — วิกิพีเดีย; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:vault-materials — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/materials.md — เนื้อ material axis; s:commons-amulets-th — Wikimedia Commons — Category:Amulets of Thailand (and subcategories)

## เข็มฝัง · susuk · Susuk (charm needles implanted under the skin)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/susuk/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/susuk.json
id: susuk · level: kind
native: سوسوق (Jawi) · susuk (ms) · susuk (id)
aliases: ซูซุก · เข็มทองฝังหน้า · ฝังเข็มเสน่ห์ · susuk emas · susuk berlian · charm needles · golden needles · beauty needles · implant charms
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: other · materials: เนื้อทองคำ (gold), เนื้อเงิน (silver) · functions: มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades) · region: my, id, sg
origin:  · โบโมะห์ / ดุกุน ฝังพร้อมคาถา น้ำมัน และคำสั่งให้ปิดเป็นความลับ A bomoh or dukun implants it with incantation and oil rubbing, and tells the wearer to keep it secret · First radiographic report 1928 (en.wikipedia); id.wikipedia holds the practice came to Indonesia from Malaysia · Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, Singapore; the Thai deep south by tradition
what (th): เข็มทอง เงิน หรือเพชรที่โบโมะห์ฝังใต้ผิวหนัง — มักที่คางหรือแก้ม — เพื่อความงาม เสน่ห์ บารมี หรือความคงกระพัน มองไม่เห็น เห็นในเอกซเรย์ อิสลามถือว่าฮะรอม ผู้ฝังถือข้อห้ามและเชื่อว่าต้องถอดก่อนตาย
what (en): Gold, silver or diamond needles a bomoh sets under the skin — chin and cheeks most often — for beauty, allure, presence or invulnerability. Invisible except on a radiograph. Islam rules it haram; the wearer keeps food taboos and holds that the needles must come out before death.
story: The wearer is told to keep it secret and to keep pantangan — no certain bananas, no papaya, no satay skewers, no passing under a clothesline; break them and the susuk weakens or turns harmful. Tradition says a person still carrying susuk dies hard, and that once removed the face returns to its real age within six months, so removal is for the same practitioner who set it. Medicine knows susuk from incidental X-rays, the first reported in 1928. Malay Wikipedia's example is a named celebrity with gold needles and diamonds in her chin.
keeping: Class null: nothing in the vault covers an implant — it is not kept, it is worn inside. What the wearer owes is the taboos and a correct removal; that is the whole of the upkeep, and the whole of why the tradition says who set it matters.
- look at: Detectable only on a radiograph, usually incidentally; clinicians must tell it from other foreign bodies [cited]
- look at: Reported composition: gold alloyed with traces of copper, silver and aluminium; diamonds in some cases [cited]
- look at: Sites: face, chest, breast, lower back and limbs; the chin is the site most often named [cited]
- look at: Wearers keep pantangan — no lady-finger bananas, papaya, satay skewers; not passing under a clothesline or a stair [cited]
- vs takrut: Thai practice also implants a takrut under the skin, but that is an inscribed tube; a susuk is a bare needle with no writing. Both show on X-ray; the tube is the tell.
- vs jimat: A jimat is carried and can be set down; a susuk is in the flesh.
- vs luk-om: A luk om is a bead held in the mouth or carried, never implanted.
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:en-wiki-susuk — Susuk — Wikipedia; s:id-wiki-susuk — Susuk — Wikipedia bahasa Indonesia; s:ms-wiki-susuk — Susuk — Wikipedia Bahasa Melayu
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ตะกรุด · takrut · Takrut (inscribed scroll-tube)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/takrut/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/takrut.json
id: takrut · level: kind
aliases: ตะกรุดโทน · ตะกรุดคู่ · ตะกรุดสามกษัตริย์ · ตะกรุดโสฬส · takrud · tagrud · takrut thon · takrut sam kasat · yantra scroll · rolled yantra amulet
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: tube · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), เนื้อทองคำ (gold), เนื้อเงิน (silver), เนื้อนาค (copper-gold alloy (rose gold)), ตะกั่ว (lead), ทองแดง (copper) · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), ค้าขาย (trade, selling), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) มีบทที่ระบุว่าเป็นของสมเด็จพระวันรัต (แดง) และหลวงปู่บุญ วัดกลางบางแก้ว Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983; two recipes are ascribed to Somdet Phra Wannarat (Daeng) and to Luang Pu Bun of Wat Klang Bang Kaeo · Undated treatise. English Wikipedia calls the takrut the most-mentioned amulet in Khun Chang Khun Phaen and puts its Buddhist form at roughly the 13th century, uncited · Country-wide; Khom script in the centre, Tham script in the north
what (th): แผ่นโลหะ ใบลาน หรือหนัง ลงยันต์แล้วม้วนแน่น ร้อยเชือกคาดเอวหรือห้อยคอ อานุภาพอยู่ที่อักขระและพิธีที่ปิดผนึก ไม่มีผู้ใดสถิต ตำราในคลังนี้เต็มไปด้วยสิ่งที่เขียนไว้ข้างใน
what (en): A sheet of metal — or palm-leaf, or skin — inscribed with a yantra and rolled tight, worn on a cord at the waist or neck. Power lives in the inscription and the rite that closed it. The treatises this site keeps are full of what gets written inside.
story: The treatise gives a dozen recipes. The three-tube trade set inscribes three fish yantras on gold, silver and nak; the chakkraphat set puts a 4x4 magic square on silver and gold. The single 'hundred-thousand-rains' takrut is inscribed inside the ordination hall under a white canopy bearing the eight-direction yantra, the stylus first blessed with ma-a-u, and its cord is spun from virgin thread and dyed with seven leaves of each of seven plants. The nine-tube set assigns each tube a job, from warding ghosts to turning weapons. One further recipe inscribes a sheet of a material the treatise names and this catalogue does not reproduce, rolls and plaits it, lacquers and gilds it, and consecrates it with the Three Refuges 108 times.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed. Safe to adopt with unknown history — with the class's one flagged exception: a takrut whose sheet the treatise takes from a source not reproduced here is a spirit-bearing object in this form, and the making, not the tube, decides.
- look at: A rolled hollow tube with a cord channel. A flat inscribed sheet is a pha yan or a yantra plate, not a takrut [cited]
- look at: The treatise inscribes on gold, silver, nak, lead, copper or paper; Thai Wikipedia adds snake skin, buffalo horn and bamboo [catalogue]
- look at: Plaited, lacquered and gilded over per one of the treatise's recipes; the inscription is usually invisible and only the tube ends show [catalogue]
- look at: Count the tubes: single, pair, three, nine or sixteen each answer to a named recipe; the nine-tube set assigns one purpose per tube [catalogue]
- look at: Skin-rolled takrut are the class's stated exception: same form, different making. Ask what the sheet is [catalogue]
- vs pha-yan: Same class, different form: a takrut is a rolled tube, a pha yan a flat cloth. Neither is fed.
- vs salika: A salika takrut is a small tube held under the tongue; a salika figure is a bird. The yantra names the bird; the form decides which record.
- vs bia-kae: A bia kae is a cowrie packed with mercury and wrapped in lead — a shell, not a rolled sheet, though both get the plaited-cord finish.

## เครื่องรางมลายู · tangkal · Tangkal (Malay protective charm, any form)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/tangkal/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/tangkal.json
id: tangkal · level: kind
native: تڠكل (Jawi) · tangkal (ms) · tangkal / penangkal (id)
aliases: ตังกัล · ของกันภัยมลายู · penangkal · tangkal bala · pelindung · Malay ward · warding charm
class: ยังไม่ชี้ขาด (left to a knower) · resident: None · upkeep: None · provenance sensitivity: None
form: other · materials: — · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: my, id, sg
origin:  · โบโมะห์ / ปะวัง หรือทำเองในครัวเรือน A bomoh or pawang for the made kinds; households make the simplest wards themselves · Folk practice older than Islam in the region and continuing beside it · Malay world
what (th): คำมลายูสำหรับของกันภัยทุกชนิด — จากด้ายดำผูกข้อมือถึงกิ่งหนามแขวนประตู — คำนี้บอกหน้าที่ (ตังกัล = ปัดออก) ไม่บอกรูป ถ้ามีตัวเขียนก็เป็นจิมัตด้วย
what (en): The Malay word for any object that wards — from a black thread on the wrist to a thorny branch over the door. It names a job (menangkal, to turn aside), not a form, which is why Malay Wikipedia files it with azimat and everyday speech keeps them apart: jimat is carried for luck, tangkal is set against a threat.
story: Malay Wikipedia folds azimat and tangkal into one article and defines the pair as a thing believed to give its owner luck and/or protection, listing gems, statues, coins, plants, animals and even spoken formulas as forms. In practice tangkal is the protection half: against ghosts (hantu), against misfortune (bala), against the evil eye. A bomoh or pawang makes the serious ones; a household hangs its own thorns. The word is also the region's answer to 'what is that thing over the door' — it is a tangkal, and the answer says nothing about what it is made of.
keeping: Class left null on purpose: tangkal is an umbrella over several vault classes (natural matter, inscribed sheets), and the vault has no ward-by-function category. Nearly all are impersonal — nothing fed, nothing owed; a frayed thread or a dried branch is simply replaced.
- look at: No writing on it at all is the usual mark of a tangkal as against a jimat; once Arabic appears the two words overlap [cited]
- look at: Natural or household matter — a fang, a thorn, a stone, black thread, a scrap of iron — chosen for what it repels [tradition]
- look at: Where it hangs is the tell: doorways, windows, cradles and fields as often as the body [tradition]
- look at: The name states the threat, not the material: tangkal bala (against misfortune), tangkal hantu (against ghosts) [tradition]
- vs jimat: A jimat is a written object carried for luck and protection both; a tangkal is anything that wards, written or not. Every written tangkal is a jimat; most tangkal are not written.
- vs rajah: A rajah is writing and nothing else; a tangkal usually carries none.
- vs mustika: A mustika is a stone kept for its own inherent tuah; a tangkal is kept to turn something away. A stone hung at a door is a tangkal, the same stone in a ring is a mustika.
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:ms-wiki-azimat — Azimat (Tangkal) — Wikipedia Bahasa Melayu; s:en-wiki-tawiz — Ta'wiz — Wikipedia; s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: low · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ท้าวเวสสุวรรณ · thao wetsuwan · Thao Wessuwan (guardian-king of the yaksha)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/thao-wessuwan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/thao-wessuwan.json
id: thao-wessuwan · level: kind
aliases: ท้าวเวสวัณ · ท้าวกุเวร · พระไพศรพณ์ · ท้าวเวสสุวัณ · thao wessuwan · thao wetsawan · thao kuwen · wessuwan · Vessavana · Vaisravana · Kubera · guardian of the north
class: เทพ / เทวดา (deva-tier resident) · resident: deva · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อโลหะ (metal (unspecified)), ทองเหลือง (brass), เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: กันผี (warding spirits), คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), ค้าขาย (trade, selling) · region: th-central, th
origin:  ·  · An old Buddhist guardian figure; as a mass-market amulet the surge dates to about 2022, when the large statue at Wat Chulamani, Samut Songkhram, became a phenomenon · Nationwide; the recent wave centres on Samut Songkhram
what (th): ท้าวเวสสุวรรณ ราชาแห่งยักษ์ ผู้รักษาทิศเหนือ มือกุมกระบอง — รูปหล่อ จี้ และแผ่นติดประตู เป็นเทพที่บูชาผ่านวัตถุ ถวายเครื่องสักการะและความเคารพ ไม่ใช่ผีที่ต้องเลี้ยงข้าว
what (en): The northern guardian-king of the yaksha, club in hand — statue, pendant and gate-plaque. A deva venerated through the object: offerings and respect, not meals.
story: One of the Four Great Kings, lord of the yaksha and guardian of the north. The older Thai use is a yantra or small image hung at a baby's cradle so no spirit troubles the child; the modern one is a figure at the door of a house or shop, keeping ghosts and black magic off the threshold and guarding what is stored inside. The trade form took off around 2022 after the large statue at Wat Chulamani in Samut Songkhram drew crowds, and the same duty now sells at every scale from garden statue to silver pendant. His image is also the emblem of the Thai public prosecutors, which tells you how he is read: an enforcer, not a benefactor.
keeping: Someone is home, at the deva tier: owed veneration — flowers, incense, water, respect — not feeding. Can be set down; worth asking who venerated it before you, but not a spirit with a history that bites.
- look at: A yaksha figure, never a Buddha or a monk: a venerated deva, not a raised spirit [catalogue]
- look at: The club is the identifying attribute; a giant without one is likely another yaksha (a temple gate-guardian, a Ramakien figure) [cited]
- look at: Guardian of the north and lord of the yaksha, one of the Four Great Kings; the same figure is the emblem of the Thai public prosecutors, so an official seal is not an amulet [cited]
- look at: The older form is a yantra or image hung at a child's cradle to keep spirits off the infant; the cast statue and pendant are the modern trade form [cited]
- look at: Current listings are resin, plated brass and silver, one of the fastest-growing categories in the market; volume says nothing about any one piece [catalogue]
- vs phaya-khrut: Wessuwan is a standing giant with a club; the garuda is a winged man-bird. Same class (deva, veneration), different body — count the wings.
- vs jatukham: Jatukham is a large round disc with a seated deva ringed by Rahu heads or zodiac animals; Wessuwan is a full standing yaksha figure, rarely a disc.
- vs hun-phayon: A hun phayon is an armed man-figure animated to serve and fed daily; Wessuwan is a deva shown as a giant, owed respect and offerings, never a meal-a-day.
- vs rup-lo: A rup lo casts a monk in robes; Wessuwan is a crowned, fanged giant. Both are cast metal, so the face decides.

## ว่าน · waan · Waan (sacred tuber)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/waan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/waan.json
id: waan · level: kind
aliases: ว่านมงคล · ว่านยา · เนื้อว่าน · wan · wahn · nuea waan · power plant · sacred herb · magical tuber
class: เครื่องรางธรรมชาติ (natural talisman) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: plant · materials: เนื้อว่าน (sacred-herb paste) · functions: เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), มหาเสน่ห์ (powerful attraction, allure), โชคลาภ (luck and windfall) · region: th, th-north
origin:  ·  · Undated; the treatise assumes ว่าน as a stock ingredient throughout · Thailand generally; the material axis notes northern practice is particularly rich
what (th): ว่านคือพืชมีฤทธิ์ — หัวหรือเหง้าที่ปลูก ตากแห้ง แกะ หรือใส่กระถาง คุณอยู่ที่ชนิดและการเลี้ยง เป็นชนิดเดียวในหน้านี้ที่ยังมีชีวิตได้ บางคนรดน้ำให้
what (en): A plant of power — a rhizome or tuber grown, dried, carved or potted, its virtue in the species and the keeping. The one kind on this page that can still be alive; some keepers water theirs.
story: The treatise never gives waan a recipe of its own because it is in everyone else's: ว่านนางกวัก is carved into a Nang Kwak and put in a money bag; ว่านเพชรน้อย, ว่านเพชรใหญ่ and ว่านเพชรสังฆาต are ground with lodestone and laterite into an invulnerability pellet, or with burnt sacred leaves into a Hanuman; the tiger-waking katha calls on the tubers proh, phlai and lemongrass by name. The market sells it two ways — a living plant in a pot, and a named ingredient inside love-wax, oils and kuman lockets. Some keepers water theirs.
keeping: Nobody home, nothing owed in the spirit sense; a living one needs water and light like any plant, which is the closest this class comes to upkeep. Safe to adopt with unknown history.
- look at: It is a plant part: a tuber, rhizome or living stem, never a pressed tablet [catalogue]
- look at: Ages by drying and shrinking, not by patina or crust — the material axis's dating signal for เนื้อว่าน [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise names species by job: ว่านนางกวัก carved into Nang Kwak; ว่านเพชรน้อย, ว่านเพชรใหญ่ and ว่านเพชรสังฆาต ground into Hanuman figures and invulnerability pellets [catalogue]
- look at: The species name states the job (ว่านดอกทอง for attraction, ว่านนางกวัก for trade); in listings the bare term collides with กว่าน 'than', which the search excludes [catalogue]
- look at: A potted living plant and a dried tuber are the same kind at two moments; the trade sells both [tradition]
- vs si-phueng: Waan is a plant; charm wax is a cooked salve in a tin that may contain waan as an ingredient. One is alive, one is finished.
- vs khot-kala: Both are natural class; a khot is a stone-hard nodule found and kept as is, a waan grows and can be planted.
- image: https://wichaa.net/img/7d7cfa7dd092724ef0055f0165927313eae9e5d51dacfe495a1460fb7b78c0ee.jpg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · เจษฎา33304 · https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=196501927

## แหวนพิรอด · waen phirot · Phirot ring (plaited yantra ring)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/waen-phirot/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/waen-phirot.json
id: waen-phirot · level: kind
aliases: พิรอด · แหวนหัวพิรอด · พิรอดนิ้ว · พิรอดแขน · waen pirod · pirod ring · phirot · woven yantra ring · pirod armband
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: ring · materials: — · functions: คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), จังงัง (stupefaction, being frozen), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: th-central, th
origin: วัดประดู่โรงธรรม (วัดประดู่ทรงธรรม) อยุธยา Wat Pradu Rong Tham / Pradu Songtham, Ayutthaya — named by both the treatise and th.wikipedia · พระอุปัชฌาย์ม่วง (หลวงพ่อม่วง) วัดประดู่โรงธรรม Preceptor Muang of Wat Pradu Rong Tham, the maker both sources name; the ring itself is older than any one maker · th.wikipedia says King Rama V praised Luang Pho Muang's rings in his own writing; the treatise is undated · Central Thailand
what (th): แหวนที่ถักจากแถบกระดาษ ผ้า หรือด้ายซึ่งลงยันต์และเสกแล้ว ขมวดปลายเป็นหัวพิรอด สวมนิ้วหรือรัดแขน เชื่อกันว่าอยู่คงแคล้วคลาด ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ไม่ต้องเลี้ยง
what (en): A ring plaited from an inscribed, consecrated strip of paper, cloth or thread, its ends worked into the phirot knot, worn on a finger or the upper arm for invulnerability and evasion. Power in the inscription and the rite; nobody home.
story: The treatise gives several recipes. Plait phraek grass into a phirot-headed ring and consecrate it seven times against all weapons; or inscribe a Khom katha on parchment-paper, plait it into the ring, empower it on your own body 108 times and wear it against bows, crossbows and firearms. One band-yantra version is to be made on an auspicious day, best a lunar eclipse, chanted eighteen times so that fangs and tusks are struck still; if a lord is angry, put the ring on and recite the Triple Refuge until it passes. The treatise names the same maker th.wikipedia does — Preceptor Muang of Wat Pradu Rong Tham — and Wikipedia adds the test: finished rings went into a charcoal fire, and only those that did not burn were gilded and given out.
keeping: Nothing to feed and nobody to answer to: a consecrated object, kept with ordinary respect. Same keeping as a takrut.
- look at: It is plaited, not cast: a solid-metal ring with a yantra is a different object [cited]
- look at: Look for the raised phirot knot with 3, 5 or 9 peaks [cited]
- look at: Black lacquer skin, sometimes gilded; the plait shows through under a loupe [cited]
- look at: th.wikipedia records that the Wat Pradu rings were put in a charcoal fire and only the unburnt ones kept. A story about the making, not a test a buyer can run [cited]
- vs takrut: A takrut is the same inscribed strip rolled into a tube and hung; a phirot is the strip plaited into a ring you wear. Same class.
- vs sai-sin: Sai sin is bare white thread tied at the wrist after chanting, no yantra, no lacquer; a phirot is plaited, lacquered and inscribed.
- vs luk-sakot: Luk sakot are small lead beads on a cord; a phirot is a single plaited ring.
sources: s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:th-wiki-phirot — พิรอด — วิกิพีเดีย; s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity)
confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-02

## วัวธนู · wua thanu · Wua thanu (guardian bull)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/wua-thanu/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/wua-thanu.json
id: wua-thanu · level: kind
aliases: ควายธนู · วัธนู · wua tanu · khwai thanu · kwai tanoo · bow-bull · buffalo talisman · guardian buffalo
class: หุ่นพยนต์ (animated effigy / servant-golem) · resident: animated · upkeep: veneration · provenance sensitivity: medium
form: figure · materials: เนื้อดิน (clay body) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: th-central, th
origin:  · ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง (ไม่ระบุผู้แต่ง) Anonymous amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983 · Undated treatise; Thai Wikipedia ties the buffalo form to rice-farming animism without a date · Central Thai tradition
what (th): รูปวัวหรือควายที่สาน ปั้น หรือหล่อ แล้วปลุกด้วยคาถาให้เฝ้าบ้าน ตำราให้ทำโรงให้อยู่ บอกความประสงค์ และเลี้ยงด้วยหญ้าและน้ำอย่างสัตว์เป็น ผู้ร้ายเข้ามาให้ชน
what (en): A bull or buffalo figure — woven, moulded or cast — woken by katha to guard the house. The treatise gives it a shed, tells it what is wanted, and feeds it grass and water like a living beast; intruders are to be gored.
story: Method 1 cuts, in a single stroke and with the namo tassa, a bamboo that grew arching over a path, splits it and weaves a bull while reciting 'om ko-no ko-no' to the end, consecrates it seven more times, builds it a shed, instructs it to gore any wrongdoer to death, and offers white liquor. Method 2 moulds clay or beeswax into a bull and consecrates it with a katha in which the bull's horns are spears and its gaze spans a hundred thousand leagues, then gives it a place, grass and water under its own feeding-katha, and tells it what is wanted — against every kind of theft. The buffalo is made the same way with gods assembled into its body; the treatise says make one or the other, not both.
keeping: Something animated is home. It owes a place, grass, water and instructions; Thai Wikipedia records a regional belief that a neglected buffalo turns on its keeper. Class placement is this record's inference — see form.notes_en — and worth asking who kept it before you.
- look at: A whole bull or buffalo figure, never a bare horn — a horn alone is a natural talisman [catalogue]
- look at: Woven bamboo strip, clay or beeswax in the treatise; cast metal on the modern shelf [catalogue]
- look at: A kept piece has a shed or place of its own with grass and water set out; that upkeep is the class tell [catalogue]
- look at: The treatise says choose bull or buffalo, not both; a pair is a market idea [catalogue]
- vs hun-phayon: A hun phayon is a man with a weapon, a wua thanu a bull; both are woken by katha, housed and fed, so the class is shared and only the figure differs.
- vs phaya-tao-ruean: The house-turtle is a blessed animal amulet with nobody home; the bull is fed grass and water. Same shelf, different keeping.
- vs kuman-thong: A kuman is a child-spirit raised as family; the bull is a guard animal fed as an animal. Neither is a phra khrueang.
sources: s:vault-classes — wichaa-vault _meta/vocab/classes.md — class axis (resident / upkeep / provenance_sensitivity); s:ms6983 — ตำราสร้างเครื่องรางของขลัง — amulet-making treatise, manuscript 6983, bilingual transcription (170 pp, 160 formulas); s:th-wiki-khwai-thanu — ควายธนู — วิกิพีเดีย; s:amulet-reference — amulet-reference.html — 22 specimen cards, 7 formula cards, 112-term market taxonomy (2026-07); s:tradition — General knowledge of the Thai / Lanna amulet tradition (model training + secondary literature), hedged — never a specific date, title or scholar unless separately cited
confidence: medium · needs_verification: True · updated: 2026-09-02

## ยันต์ลาว · yan (Lao Tham-script yantra) · Lao yantra in Tham script
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/lao-yan/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/lao-yan.json
id: lao-yan · level: kind
native: ຍັນ (lo)
aliases: ยันต์ธรรมลาว · ยันต์อีสาน · ยันต์ตัวธรรม · ยันต์ล้านช้าง · yan lao · yan tham lao · yan isan · yantra lao · Lao Tham yantra · Isan yantra · Lan Xang yantra
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: other · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth), ตะกั่ว (lead), ทองแดง (copper) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), กันผี (warding spirits), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity) · region: la, th-isan
origin:  · พระและหมอธรรมลาว-อีสาน Lao and Isan monks and mo tham, the lay ritualists who read Tham · Lao Tham is an adaptation of Lanna Tham; the oldest dated Isan example is the inscription on the base of the principal Buddha at Wat Phra That Phanom, 1503 (BE 2046), under Lan Xang · Lan Xang — Luang Prabang, Vientiane — and Isan
what (th): ยันต์ที่เขียนด้วยตัวธรรมลาว สายอักษรเดียวกับล้านนา ใช้บนผ้า ตะกรุด ใบลาน และผิวหนัง พลังอยู่ที่อักขระและพิธี ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A yantra written in Lao Tham, the Lanna-family sacred script of Lan Xang and Isan, carried on cloth, in a takrut, on palm leaf, or on skin. Power lives in the letters and the rite; nobody is home.
story: Lao Tham — to tham, 'the dhamma letters' — is the Lanna script adapted for Lao and reserved for scripture: Pali texts, Jataka, and the bound manuscripts of village temples. The oldest dated Isan example is the 1503 inscription at Wat Phra That Phanom, written under Lan Xang. After the Burmese took Lanna in the sixteenth century, Vientiane and Luang Prabang became the manuscript centres, and the Lao Wikipedia records a 1910 assembly that assigned Tham to religious text and the modern Lao script to the state. Today its use in Laos is limited to long-term monks, so the yantra written in it is as much a survival of literacy as of magic.
keeping: Impersonal: kept high, never stepped over, nothing fed. What the keeper owes is care for the letters.
- look at: The Northeast writes its yantra in the Isan / Lao Tham script, the North in Lanna Tham, the Centre in Khom — the script names the region before the design does [cited]
- look at: Lao Tham is an adaptation of Lanna Tham in both structure and letter shape; Lao speakers call the Lanna form aksorn yuan — the two are one family and a loupe separates them by hand, not by system [cited]
- look at: Tai Tham carries two numeral systems, Lek Hora for general use and Lek Nai Tham for liturgy; a Tham yantra may use either [cited]
- look at: Pali mixed with the vernacular and almost no Sanskrit, as in the Thai and Khmer traditions [cited]
- look at: In Laos the script's use is limited to long-term monks, so freshly written and correctly read Tham yantra are scarcer each decade [cited]
- vs yan-lanna: Same Tham family: Lanna is the source, Lao the adaptation. Tell by letter shapes and by the vernacular mixed into the Pali — Kam Mueang against Lao — and by where it was made.
- vs pha-yan: A Central Thai pha yan is in Khom; a Lao yantra in Tham. Angular versus round under the loupe.
- vs khmer-yantra-cloth: The Khmer cloth is in Khom / Mul letters; the Lao design in Tham.
- vs takrut: A takrut is a form; a Lao yantra is the design that may be rolled inside one. If the sheet is in Tham, it is both.

## ยันต์ล้านนา · yan lanna · Lanna yantra (Tai Tham script)
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/yan-lanna/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/yan-lanna.json
id: yan-lanna · level: kind
aliases: ผ้ายันต์ล้านนา · ยันต์ตัวเมือง · ยันต์เทียน · ยันต์อักษรธรรม · yant lanna · yan tua mueang · yan thian · Northern Thai yantra · Tua Mueang yantra · Lanna yant cloth
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: cloth · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), เมตตามหานิยม (loving-kindness and wide popularity), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: th-north
origin:  · ครูบาและพ่อหนานล้านนา Lanna monks (khruba) and ex-monk lay masters (pho nan) · Continues the palm-leaf manuscript tradition written in Tai Tham; script use in the north declined after 1930s Thaification and is reviving · Chiang Mai, Lamphun, Lampang, Phrae, Nan, Chiang Rai
what (th): ยันต์ของภาคเหนือ เขียนด้วยอักษรธรรมล้านนา (ตัวเมือง) บนผ้า เทียน หรือแผ่นโลหะ อำนาจอยู่ที่อักขระและพิธี ไม่มีผู้อยู่ ลายยันต์จากตำรามีดัชนีที่ wichaa.net/yant
what (en): The northern yantra: grids, rings and figures written in Tai Tham (ตัวเมือง) script on cloth, in candles, or on metal. Power sits in the inscription and the rite, nobody home. The drawn designs from the treatises have their own index at wichaa.net/yant.
story: Tai Tham is the script Lanna used for Pali and its palm-leaf scriptures, so the north wrote its yantra in it rather than in Khom. Thai Wikipedia's เลขยันต์ has candle yantras as the region's commonest form and its cloth yantras larger than elsewhere. Thaification in the 1930s pushed the script out of schools, but monks kept reading it and it is being relearned; the yantra never stopped being written. The sibling index at wichaa.net/yant catalogues 36 designs across 63 treatise plates by virtue and figure.
keeping: Nothing owed and nobody home. Ordinary respect for an inscribed object: not underfoot, not in a low place.
- look at: The script is rounded Tai Tham, not the angular Khom of central yantra: the one mark that settles north against centre at a glance [cited]
- look at: Candle yantras are the commonest northern carrier; a written sheet rolled inside the wax [cited]
- look at: Northern cloth yantras run larger than central ones [cited]
- look at: The script carries Pali and Kam Mueang; astrological and dharma numerals sit in the cells [cited]
- look at: Tai Tham, Tham Isan and Lao Tham are close cousins; telling them apart takes the letter forms, not the layout [cited]
- vs pha-yan: Same class, same cloth: a central pha yan is written in Khom script, a Lanna one in Tai Tham. Read the letters.
- vs lao-yan: A Lao yan is in Lao Tham script, a near cousin of Tai Tham; only the letter forms separate them
- vs khmer-yantra-cloth: A Khmer yantra cloth is in Khmer script with Khmer figure drawing
- vs takrut: A takrut is a yantra rolled in a metal tube; a Lanna yantra can be rolled into one too, and then the script is the only tell

## ผ้ายันต์เขมร · yoan (Khmer yantra cloth) · Khmer yantra cloth
URL: https://wichaa.net/amulets/kind/khmer-yantra-cloth/
JSON: https://wichaa.net/amulets/api/kind/khmer-yantra-cloth.json
id: khmer-yantra-cloth · level: kind
native: យ័ន្ត (km)
aliases: ผ้ายันต์ขอม · ยันต์เขมร · ผ้าขาวม้ายันต์ · yan khmer · yantra khmer · pha yan khmer · krama yoan · Cambodian yantra cloth · Khmer yant · yantra krama
class: วัตถุมงคล (ยันต์) (blessed/inscribed object) · resident: none · upkeep: none · provenance sensitivity: low
form: cloth · materials: ผ้ายันต์ (inscribed cloth) · functions: คุ้มครอง (general protection, watching over), คงกระพัน (invulnerability to blades), แคล้วคลาด (evasion, narrow escape), กันผี (warding spirits) · region: kh
origin:  · ครูขแมร์ อาจารย์ และพระ Kru khmer, achar and monks of the yogavacara line · Undated; yantra practice in Cambodia is traced to the Khmer Empire around the ninth century, and the cloth form is documented into the present · Cambodia
what (th): ผ้าเขียนยันต์ตัวขอมของเขมร แขวนขื่อบ้าน พับพก หรือคาดตัวนักสู้ พลังอยู่ที่อักขระและพิธี ไม่มีผู้อยู่
what (en): A cloth drawn with Khom-letter yantra in the Cambodian tradition — hung from the house beam, folded into a pocket, or tied on a fighter. Power lives in the inscription and the rite; nobody is home.
story: The Khmer Wikipedia article defines a yoan (យ័ន្ត) as a design drawn on white cloth or paper, and the Cambodian Hevajra yantra shows the Angkor-period esoteric layer still inside it. The English article on yantra cloth records the Khmer habits — a rain-quail motif, and raising the cloth to the house beam as the blessing that makes a house a home — and fighters in bokator go in wrapped in cloth and enchanted cords. Achar and kru khmer draw and bless them; factory-printed cloths without the rite circulate alongside. The gatha written on the cloth is the same Pali formula that goes into a katha tube or onto the skin.
keeping: Impersonal: hung high, never stepped over, nothing fed. The keeper owes respect to the letters, not to an occupant.
- look at: Red, black or white ground carrying Buddhist esoteric inscriptions and geometric designs [cited]
- look at: Khmer versions often carry the rain-quail motif and are raised on a house beam as the blessing of the house; Thai versions lean to Nang Kwak and monk portraits [cited]
- look at: Letters are the Khom / Mul hand that Cambodia and Thailand both use for yantra on cloth, paper and brass; the hand alone will not settle which side of the border made it [cited]
- look at: Bokator fighters tie blue and red silk cords (sangvar day) at head and biceps once believed enchanted for strength; the cloth worn into the ring is the same protective idea on a garment [cited]
- look at: Factory-printed cloths without the rite are common; the same design can be a consecrated object or a souvenir, and the cloth will not tell you which [cited]
- vs pha-yan: Same class and form as the Thai pha yan; the Khmer cloth is told by motif (rain quail, Hevajra yantra) and by the maker's lineage, not by the script, which is shared.
- vs khmer-katha: The katha is a rolled metal tube; this is a flat cloth. Same class, different form.
- vs suea-yan: A yantra shirt is a stitched garment worn over the torso; the Khmer cloth is an unstitched square hung or wrapped.
- vs lao-yan: Lao yantra is in round Tham letters; the Khmer cloth in Khom. Look at the script before the design.
